sections.title: Mathematical assumptions
sections.markdown:
## Mathematical assumptions

Read and Green distinguish weak- and strong-pairing phases of a two-dimensional spinless complex p-wave model. Their continuum chemical potential is measured relative to the band bottom: its zero marks a gap-closing transition in that model. The broken symmetry alone does not distinguish the two phases. This continuum criterion must not be copied unchanged into a lattice or multiband calculation. [R1](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a)

For an independent lattice illustration, set hopping and pairing scales to one and use $H(\mathbf{k})=\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{k})\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}$, with $\mathbf{h}=(\sin k_x,\chi\sin k_y,-2\cos k_x-2\cos k_y-\mu)$ and $\chi=\pm1$. In this Nambu convention the off-diagonal gap is $\sin k_x-i\chi\sin k_y$. Define the occupied-band Berry connection as $\mathbf{A}=i\langle u_-|\nabla_{\mathbf{k}}u_-\rangle$. With the orientation $(k_x,k_y)$, the lower-band Chern number for $\chi=1$ is $0,-1,+1,0$ in the intervals separated by $\mu=-4,0,4$. Reversing $\chi$ reverses its sign. [R1](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a) [R2](#ref-source-69d33a869fbbb0c6)

Sixteen calculations compare two mesh sizes, four chemical potentials and both handedness choices. Berry-link phases from explicit occupied eigenvectors agree with independently summed spherical solid angles. Four analytic gap-closing checks identify the excluded critical points; no gapped-band invariant is assigned there. The same complex gap can thus accompany a zero or nonzero Chern number. The calculation fixes the gap by hand and omits self-consistency, realistic bands and disorder. [R1](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a)

A boundary calculation illustrates a different distinction. In Huang, Taylor and Kallin's ideal sharp-edge continuum treatment, occupied bound states and continuum states both contribute to the integrated current. For axial harmonic index $m=1$, their respective values are $1/2$ and $-1/4$ in units $\hbar k_F^2/(4\pi m^*)$ per spin component. For integer $m>1$, each integrated contribution vanishes in this limit despite the chiral edge branches. Independent angular quadrature reproduces the analytic sums for six values of $m$. [R3](#ref-source-25d6a80b561d5ad2)

That cancellation is not a universal absence of current in higher-order chiral pairing. The same paper shows that making the density vary slowly over distances much longer than the coherence length restores a current; lattice effects also matter. A sharp specular boundary, a smooth trap and a disordered multiband surface are different problems. The calculation above does not predict a magnetic-field amplitude for a real sample. [R3](#ref-source-25d6a80b561d5ad2)

sections.title: Experimental criteria
sections.markdown:
## Experimental criteria

Kerr rotation probes an optical response. In the clean Galilean-invariant limit, a spatially uniform electric field couples to center-of-mass motion and the charge Hall response vanishes even for complex pairing. At the single-particle level, the clean one-band current-vertex structure also gives a cancellation; multiband and impurity processes require separate treatment. Optical frequency, refractive response and geometry matter. Neither a null Kerr measurement nor one nonzero angle can be converted directly into a Chern number. [R1](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a) [R2](#ref-source-69d33a869fbbb0c6)

For UPt3, retain Schemm and colleagues' distinction between the Kerr onset near 0.46 K and the upper susceptibility onset near 0.55 K, including optical heating and field-training controls. For Sr2RuO4, Pustogow and colleagues' oxygen NMR response constrains a simple fixed-d-vector interpretation. The later 2026 muon Knight-shift study also has field-dependent extraction and low-temperature magnetization limits. These are complementary constraints, not a license to restore a historically favored chiral p-wave label as settled fact. [R4](#ref-source-d3edee404071ac81) [R5](#ref-source-c7f8b99a795aba41) [R9](#ref-source-c4434644191d0174)

Mielke and colleagues studied KV3Sb5, not the whole AV3Sb5 family interchangeably. Their selected manuscript shows an increased muon relaxation below the charge-order scale near 80 K that remains approximately constant across the superconducting transition near 1.1 K. They explicitly discuss electric-field-gradient contributions and use high-field measurements to support an electronic interpretation. The methods report residual-field compensation better than 30 mG; a 50 G longitudinal field decouples the relaxation. These are charge-order constraints, not a new superconducting chirality onset at 80 K. [R6](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3)

Chen and colleagues studied CsV3Sb5 with tunneling and Josephson spectroscopy. Their selected manuscript distinguishes bulk signatures near 2.8 K from a surface transition near 2.3 K, and uses a calibrated 300 mK electron temperature. Spatial gap and conductance modulations motivate their roton-PDW interpretation. The authors explicitly state that roton excitations were not directly observed. A proposed complex vortex–antivortex pattern is therefore an interpretation to test, not a measured uniform chiral d-wave order parameter. [R7](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961)

sections.title: Limits and disputes
sections.markdown:
## Limits and disputes

Local magnitude alone does not resolve handedness: $|\Delta|^2=|\Delta^*|^2$. Four complex spatial examples verify this identity without making a tunneling-response model. A Josephson signal can support superconducting coherence, while determining orbital phase structure requires suitable reference geometry and controls. Fourier peaks, gap-depth maps and zero-bias peaks must retain their individual evidential roles. [R7](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961)

Do not require every time-reversal-breaking state to belong to a two-dimensional crystal representation. Complex combinations of distinct representations or interband phases can behave differently. Likewise, half-quantum vortices can occur in equal-spin-pairing states without establishing orbital chirality. A strain response or vortex signature must be interpreted in the actual symmetry and spin-orbit setting. [R2](#ref-source-69d33a869fbbb0c6) [R8](#ref-source-3c7aa9b4c8da3abf)

The local topology check is a fully gapped two-dimensional model. Nodal three-dimensional superconductors may instead require momentum-resolved invariants; a single integer cannot simply be carried over. Edge spectra, thermal transport, optical response and screened equilibrium charge currents require distinct calculations. Complete scientific acceptance, final-version comparisons, raw-data review and material-specific modelling remain open. [R1](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a) [R2](#ref-source-69d33a869fbbb0c6) [R3](#ref-source-25d6a80b561d5ad2)

sections.title: Discovery implications
sections.markdown:
## Discovery implications

First identify the transition and its probe. Then specify the order-parameter basis, domain controls, bulk gap and Hamiltonian used for any topology claim. Compare positive and null evidence under compatible conditions, retaining charge-order and superconducting temperature scales separately. A useful discovery target is a state that satisfies these linked tests, not a material selected merely for a complex gap notation or a kagome lattice. In the clean Galilean-invariant limit, a spatially uniform electric field couples to center-of-mass motion and the charge Hall response vanishes even for complex pairing. At the single-particle level, the clean one-band current-vertex structure also gives a cancellation; multiband and impurity processes require separate treatment. Optical frequency, refractive response and geometry matter. Neither a null Kerr measurement nor one nonzero angle can be converted directly into a Chern number.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-a33c639b7db4f05a, source-69d33a869fbbb0c6.

Conditions: Explicit band, Berry and boundary conventions; fixed-gap models are not material fits. Experimental temperatures retain sample, probe and phase distinctions.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c7-claim-experimental-criteria-2

For UPt3, retain Schemm and colleagues' distinction between the Kerr onset near 0.46 K and the upper susceptibility onset near 0.55 K, including optical heating and field-training controls. For Sr2RuO4, Pustogow and colleagues' oxygen NMR response constrains a simple fixed-d-vector interpretation. The later 2026 muon Knight-shift study also has field-dependent extraction and low-temperature magnetization limits. These are complementary constraints, not a license to restore a historically favored chiral p-wave label as settled fact.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-d3edee404071ac81, source-c7f8b99a795aba41, source-c4434644191d0174.

Conditions: Explicit band, Berry and boundary conventions; fixed-gap models are not material fits. Experimental temperatures retain sample, probe and phase distinctions.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c7-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Mielke and colleagues studied KV3Sb5, not the whole AV3Sb5 family interchangeably. Their selected manuscript shows an increased muon relaxation below the charge-order scale near 80 K that remains approximately constant across the superconducting transition near 1.1 K. They explicitly discuss electric-field-gradient contributions and use high-field measurements to support an electronic interpretation. The methods report residual-field compensation better than 30 mG; a 50 G longitudinal field decouples the relaxation. These are charge-order constraints, not a new superconducting chirality onset at 80 K.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-484da7abcc165cd3.

Conditions: Explicit band, Berry and boundary conventions; fixed-gap models are not material fits. Experimental temperatures retain sample, probe and phase distinctions.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c7-claim-experimental-criteria-4

Chen and colleagues studied CsV3Sb5 with tunneling and Josephson spectroscopy. Their selected manuscript distinguishes bulk signatures near 2.8 K from a surface transition near 2.3 K, and uses a calibrated 300 mK electron temperature. Spatial gap and conductance modulations motivate their roton-PDW interpretation. The authors explicitly state that roton excitations were not directly observed. A proposed complex vortex–antivortex pattern is therefore an interpretation to test, not a measured uniform chiral d-wave order parameter.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-057c43c86174f961.

Conditions: Explicit band, Berry and boundary conventions; fixed-gap models are not material fits. Experimental temperatures retain sample, probe and phase distinctions.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c7-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Local magnitude alone does not resolve handedness: $|\Delta|^2=|\Delta^*|^2$. Four complex spatial examples verify this identity without making a tunneling-response model. A Josephson signal can support superconducting coherence, while determining orbital phase structure requires suitable reference geometry and controls. Fourier peaks, gap-depth maps and zero-bias peaks must retain their individual evidential roles.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-057c43c86174f961.

Conditions: Explicit band, Berry and boundary conventions; fixed-gap models are not material fits. Experimental temperatures retain sample, probe and phase distinctions.

### scwiki-c7-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

Do not require every time-reversal-breaking state to belong to a two-dimensional crystal representation. Complex combinations of distinct representations or interband phases can behave differently. Likewise, half-quantum vortices can occur in equal-spin-pairing states without establishing orbital chirality. A strain response or vortex signature must be interpreted in the actual symmetry and spin-orbit setting.

### scwiki-c7-claim-limits-and-disputes-3

The local topology check is a fully gapped two-dimensional model. Nodal three-dimensional superconductors may instead require momentum-resolved invariants; a single integer cannot simply be carried over. Edge spectra, thermal transport, optical response and screened equilibrium charge currents require distinct calculations. Complete scientific acceptance, final-version comparisons, raw-data review and material-specific modelling remain open.

First identify the transition and its probe. Then specify the order-parameter basis, domain controls, bulk gap and Hamiltonian used for any topology claim. Compare positive and null evidence under compatible conditions, retaining charge-order and superconducting temperature scales separately. A useful discovery target is a state that satisfies these linked tests, not a material selected merely for a complex gap notation or a kagome lattice.

articles.body:
## Scope

A pair-density wave (PDW) concerns finite-wavevector components of a superconducting pair field. A charge-density wave (CDW), a modulated tunneling spectrum and a modulated pair field are different observables. Specify the underlying lattice or superlattice, the electromagnetic gauge convention and whether a uniform condensate coexists. A single plane-wave phase has constant magnitude; periodic magnitude alone also need not establish a new spontaneous broken translation symmetry. [R1](#ref-source-824e7016c4d4c3a8) [R10](#ref-source-61d655195d7db259)

The conventional Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) problem uses spin imbalance to motivate finite-momentum pairing. Fulde and Ferrell's clean exchange-field model includes a compensating normal contribution to the current: a phase gradient must not be equated with an uncompensated equilibrium current. The Larkin–Ovchinnikov paper appeared in Russian in 1964 and English translation in 1965; its institutional publication record is checked here, but the original full text remains an access gap. Modern orbital-FFLO proposals require separate assumptions. [R1](#ref-source-824e7016c4d4c3a8) [R2](#ref-source-21442c6eb33d9b94) [R9](#ref-source-ad66f48ab9369ce9)

## Mathematical assumptions

For a scalar illustration in a fixed gauge, write $\Delta(x)=d_0+d_+e^{iQx}+d_-e^{-iQx}$. The Fourier coefficients of $|\Delta|^2$ are $C_0=|d_0|^2+|d_+|^2+|d_-|^2$, $C_Q=d_+d_0^*+d_0d_-^*$ and $C_{2Q}=d_+d_-^*$, with negative-wavevector coefficients given by conjugation. Four independent discrete Fourier examples reproduce these identities. They are algebraic intensity identities, not a derivation of electronic charge density or a tunneling response. [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4) [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

For $d_0=d_-=0$, the Fulde–Ferrell-type plane wave has constant $|\Delta|$. Equal real $d_+=d_-=d/2$ instead give the Larkin–Ovchinnikov-type standing wave $d\cos Qx$: the pair field has period $2\pi/Q$, while its squared magnitude has period $\pi/Q$. Adding a real uniform component produces a Q harmonic through interference. A missing Q intensity harmonic therefore does not rule out a pure standing-wave pair field, and a detected 2Q charge harmonic does not uniquely identify one. These imposed examples do not compare free energies. [R1](#ref-source-824e7016c4d4c3a8) [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4) [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

Under an electron gauge phase $\alpha$, both pair components acquire $e^{2i\alpha}$. The product $d_+d_-^*$ is neutral, whereas $d_+d_-$ transforms with $e^{4i\alpha}$ and has zero net wavevector. Three numerical phase checks confirm the distinction. A composite with charge 4e is not by itself evidence for a thermodynamically coherent charge-4e phase. Berg, Fradkin and Kivelson's 2009 melting theory proposes such a phase and fractional flux as a test; that proposal is distinct from the 2007 layer-decoupling paper. [R8](#ref-source-cb08c313e0597487)

Berg and colleagues' 2007 stripe model suppresses leading interplane Josephson coupling through a particular antiphase pattern and stacking. An independent overlap calculation gives $\langle\cos Qx\cos Qy\rangle=0$ over complete periods for perpendicular stripes, but parallel stripes give $1/2$. Adding a common uniform amplitude $u$ gives $u^2$; a cropped window need not cancel. The quartic overlap remains $\langle\cos^2Qx\cos^2Qy\rangle=1/4$. This illustrates why cancellation of the lowest coupling does not mean all coupling vanishes. The paper retains higher-order/further-neighbor terms and discusses defects that spoil exact cancellation. [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4)

An illustrative vortex-halo envelope $A(r)=e^{-r/\xi}$ produces a Q amplitude proportional to $A\Delta_0^*$ and a 2Q amplitude proportional to $A^2$. If $\Delta_0$ is approximately constant, the latter decays twice as fast. Four independent logarithmic-slope checks verify this and show failure of that ratio when the uniform component recovers from zero. The relation is conditional, especially near the core; it is not a universal PDW diagnostic. [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

## Experimental criteria

Tranquada and colleagues' 1995 neutron study concerns static spin/charge stripes in Nd-substituted La–Sr–Cu–O at $x=0.12$. That diffraction evidence does not directly measure a superconducting pair field. Layer decoupling and charge harmonics are useful cross-checks only when competing charge, magnetic and structural explanations are addressed. [R3](#ref-source-b33aab72ae697f3a) [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4)

Hamidian and colleagues' 2016 experiment used a superconducting Bi2212 nanoflake tip for scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy below 50 mK. It reported modulations near $Q_P=(0.25\pm0.02)\,2\pi/a_0$, superposed on a stronger uniform component. It is not the later field-induced vortex-halo spectroscopy experiment. Their phase-diffusion model uses $I(V)=I_J^2 ZV/[2(V^2+V_c^2)]$, with $V_c=2eZk_BT^*/\hbar$. The measured peak $I_c=\hbar I_J^2/(8ek_BT^*)$ differs from the underlying Josephson critical current $I_J$; three independent numerical peak searches verify this relation. The effective noise temperature $T^*$ must not simply be replaced by refrigerator temperature. [R5](#ref-source-66a2b2a9519f6f44)

Edkins and colleagues' 2019 study used single-electron STM, explicitly without scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy. At 2 K it compared 0 and 8.25 T in the same Bi2212 field of view using the same tip. Approximately eight-cell and four-cell electronic modulations support a PDW interpretation within the authors' model. The fitted Fourier widths are not exactly in a two-to-one ratio. Sublattice form factors belong to the measured electronic response and must not be copied directly onto the pair field. The core region is excluded from the simple envelope argument. Raw-data fitting and the complete supplement are not reproduced here. [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

Chen and colleagues' 2021 CsV3Sb5 work reports spatial gap/conductance modulations and Josephson spectroscopy on prepared surfaces. Bulk and surface temperature scales differ, and the author manuscript explicitly says roton excitations were not directly observed. Its proposed complex PDW interpretation is not a direct phase measurement or a universal statement about kagome superconductors. The selected manuscript and methods check is inherited from the chiral-pairing entry. [R7](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961)

In May 2026, Cao and colleagues reported a hysteretic tunneling-gap transition in multilayer NbSe2 under an in-plane field, consistent with a possible orbital FFLO state. Their reported angle, disorder and thickness dependences matter; the selected theoretical discussion neglects vortices in its energy comparison. This is evidence for a transition with a proposed interpretation, not a direct image of finite pair momentum. Only the publisher abstract, introduction and selected model passage have been checked here. [R9](#ref-source-ad66f48ab9369ce9)

## Limits and disputes

Keep four distinctions explicit: pair tunneling versus single-electron tunneling; induced modulation versus a primary instability; field-induced versus spontaneous behavior; and a surface observation versus a bulk thermodynamic phase. A particular gap map cannot alone determine the pair phase. A nonzero composite amplitude, a half-vortex proposal or an unusual transport curve likewise needs a separate coherence and alternative-explanation analysis. sections.markdown:
## Mathematical assumptions

For a scalar illustration in a fixed gauge, write $\Delta(x)=d_0+d_+e^{iQx}+d_-e^{-iQx}$. The Fourier coefficients of $|\Delta|^2$ are $C_0=|d_0|^2+|d_+|^2+|d_-|^2$, $C_Q=d_+d_0^*+d_0d_-^*$ and $C_{2Q}=d_+d_-^*$, with negative-wavevector coefficients given by conjugation. Four independent discrete Fourier examples reproduce these identities. They are algebraic intensity identities, not a derivation of electronic charge density or a tunneling response. [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4) [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

For $d_0=d_-=0$, the Fulde–Ferrell-type plane wave has constant $|\Delta|$. Equal real $d_+=d_-=d/2$ instead give the Larkin–Ovchinnikov-type standing wave $d\cos Qx$: the pair field has period $2\pi/Q$, while its squared magnitude has period $\pi/Q$. Adding a real uniform component produces a Q harmonic through interference. A missing Q intensity harmonic therefore does not rule out a pure standing-wave pair field, and a detected 2Q charge harmonic does not uniquely identify one. These imposed examples do not compare free energies. [R1](#ref-source-824e7016c4d4c3a8) [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4) [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

Under an electron gauge phase $\alpha$, both pair components acquire $e^{2i\alpha}$. The product $d_+d_-^*$ is neutral, whereas $d_+d_-$ transforms with $e^{4i\alpha}$ and has zero net wavevector. Three numerical phase checks confirm the distinction. A composite with charge 4e is not by itself evidence for a thermodynamically coherent charge-4e phase. Berg, Fradkin and Kivelson's 2009 melting theory proposes such a phase and fractional flux as a test; that proposal is distinct from the 2007 layer-decoupling paper. [R8](#ref-source-cb08c313e0597487)

Berg and colleagues' 2007 stripe model suppresses leading interplane Josephson coupling through a particular antiphase pattern and stacking. An independent overlap calculation gives $\langle\cos Qx\cos Qy\rangle=0$ over complete periods for perpendicular stripes, but parallel stripes give $1/2$. Adding a common uniform amplitude $u$ gives $u^2$; a cropped window need not cancel. The quartic overlap remains $\langle\cos^2Qx\cos^2Qy\rangle=1/4$. This illustrates why cancellation of the lowest coupling does not mean all coupling vanishes. The paper retains higher-order/further-neighbor terms and discusses defects that spoil exact cancellation. [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4)

An illustrative vortex-halo envelope $A(r)=e^{-r/\xi}$ produces a Q amplitude proportional to $A\Delta_0^*$ and a 2Q amplitude proportional to $A^2$. If $\Delta_0$ is approximately constant, the latter decays twice as fast. Four independent logarithmic-slope checks verify this and show failure of that ratio when the uniform component recovers from zero. The relation is conditional, especially near the core; it is not a universal PDW diagnostic. [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

sections.markdown:
## Experimental criteria

Tranquada and colleagues' 1995 neutron study concerns static spin/charge stripes in Nd-substituted La–Sr–Cu–O at $x=0.12$. That diffraction evidence does not directly measure a superconducting pair field. Layer decoupling and charge harmonics are useful cross-checks only when competing charge, magnetic and structural explanations are addressed. [R3](#ref-source-b33aab72ae697f3a) [R4](#ref-source-7148789acde770d4)

Hamidian and colleagues' 2016 experiment used a superconducting Bi2212 nanoflake tip for scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy below 50 mK. It reported modulations near $Q_P=(0.25\pm0.02)\,2\pi/a_0$, superposed on a stronger uniform component. It is not the later field-induced vortex-halo spectroscopy experiment. Their phase-diffusion model uses $I(V)=I_J^2 ZV/[2(V^2+V_c^2)]$, with $V_c=2eZk_BT^*/\hbar$. The measured peak $I_c=\hbar I_J^2/(8ek_BT^*)$ differs from the underlying Josephson critical current $I_J$; three independent numerical peak searches verify this relation. The effective noise temperature $T^*$ must not simply be replaced by refrigerator temperature. [R5](#ref-source-66a2b2a9519f6f44)

Edkins and colleagues' 2019 study used single-electron STM, explicitly without scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy. At 2 K it compared 0 and 8.25 T in the same Bi2212 field of view using the same tip. Approximately eight-cell and four-cell electronic modulations support a PDW interpretation within the authors' model. The fitted Fourier widths are not exactly in a two-to-one ratio. Sublattice form factors belong to the measured electronic response and must not be copied directly onto the pair field. The core region is excluded from the simple envelope argument. Raw-data fitting and the complete supplement are not reproduced here. [R6](#ref-source-d306adac5d567426)

Chen and colleagues' 2021 CsV3Sb5 work reports spatial gap/conductance modulations and Josephson spectroscopy on prepared surfaces. Bulk and surface temperature scales differ, and the author manuscript explicitly says roton excitations were not directly observed. Its proposed complex PDW interpretation is not a direct phase measurement or a universal statement about kagome superconductors. The selected manuscript and methods check is inherited from the chiral-pairing entry. [R7](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961)

In May 2026, Cao and colleagues reported a hysteretic tunneling-gap transition in multilayer NbSe2 under an in-plane field, consistent with a possible orbital FFLO state. Their reported angle, disorder and thickness dependences matter; the selected theoretical discussion neglects vortices in its energy comparison. This is evidence for a transition with a proposed interpretation, not a direct image of finite pair momentum. Only the publisher abstract, introduction and selected model passage have been checked here. [R9](#ref-source-ad66f48ab9369ce9)

For $d_0=d_-=0$, the Fulde–Ferrell-type plane wave has constant $|\Delta|$. Equal real $d_+=d_-=d/2$ instead give the Larkin–Ovchinnikov-type standing wave $d\cos Qx$: the pair field has period $2\pi/Q$, while its squared magnitude has period $\pi/Q$. Adding a real uniform component produces a Q harmonic through interference. A missing Q intensity harmonic therefore does not rule out a pure standing-wave pair field, and a detected 2Q charge harmonic does not uniquely identify one. These imposed examples do not compare free energies.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-824e7016c4d4c3a8, source-7148789acde770d4, source-d306adac5d567426.

Conditions: Fixed scalar amplitudes and imposed wavevectors; complete periods for zero-overlap result. No self-consistent stability or material response fit. Envelope ratio requires a constant uniform background.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

Under an electron gauge phase $\alpha$, both pair components acquire $e^{2i\alpha}$. The product $d_+d_-^*$ is neutral, whereas $d_+d_-$ transforms with $e^{4i\alpha}$ and has zero net wavevector. Three numerical phase checks confirm the distinction. A composite with charge 4e is not by itself evidence for a thermodynamically coherent charge-4e phase. Berg, Fradkin and Kivelson's 2009 melting theory proposes such a phase and fractional flux as a test; that proposal is distinct from the 2007 layer-decoupling paper.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-cb08c313e0597487.

Conditions: Fixed scalar amplitudes and imposed wavevectors; complete periods for zero-overlap result. No self-consistent stability or material response fit. Envelope ratio requires a constant uniform background.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-4

Berg and colleagues' 2007 stripe model suppresses leading interplane Josephson coupling through a particular antiphase pattern and stacking. An independent overlap calculation gives $\langle\cos Qx\cos Qy\rangle=0$ over complete periods for perpendicular stripes, but parallel stripes give $1/2$. Adding a common uniform amplitude $u$ gives $u^2$; a cropped window need not cancel. The quartic overlap remains $\langle\cos^2Qx\cos^2Qy\rangle=1/4$. This illustrates why cancellation of the lowest coupling does not mean all coupling vanishes. The paper retains higher-order/further-neighbor terms and discusses defects that spoil exact cancellation.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-7148789acde770d4.

Conditions: Fixed scalar amplitudes and imposed wavevectors; complete periods for zero-overlap result. No self-consistent stability or material response fit. Envelope ratio requires a constant uniform background.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-5

An illustrative vortex-halo envelope $A(r)=e^{-r/\xi}$ produces a Q amplitude proportional to $A\Delta_0^*$ and a 2Q amplitude proportional to $A^2$. If $\Delta_0$ is approximately constant, the latter decays twice as fast. Four independent logarithmic-slope checks verify this and show failure of that ratio when the uniform component recovers from zero. The relation is conditional, especially near the core; it is not a universal PDW diagnostic.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-d306adac5d567426.

Conditions: Fixed scalar amplitudes and imposed wavevectors; complete periods for zero-overlap result. No self-consistent stability or material response fit. Envelope ratio requires a constant uniform background.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-experimental-criteria-1

Tranquada and colleagues' 1995 neutron study concerns static spin/charge stripes in Nd-substituted La–Sr–Cu–O at $x=0.12$. That diffraction evidence does not directly measure a superconducting pair field. Layer decoupling and charge harmonics are useful cross-checks only when competing charge, magnetic and structural explanations are addressed.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-b33aab72ae697f3a, source-7148789acde770d4.

Conditions: Keep each study and probe separate: 2016 pair tunneling below 50 mK; 2019 single-electron 0/8.25T comparison at 2 K. Spectroscopy and phase interpretation are not interchangeable.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Hamidian and colleagues' 2016 experiment used a superconducting Bi2212 nanoflake tip for scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy below 50 mK. It reported modulations near $Q_P=(0.25\pm0.02)\,2\pi/a_0$, superposed on a stronger uniform component. It is not the later field-induced vortex-halo spectroscopy experiment. Their phase-diffusion model uses $I(V)=I_J^2 ZV/[2(V^2+V_c^2)]$, with $V_c=2eZk_BT^*/\hbar$. The measured peak $I_c=\hbar I_J^2/(8ek_BT^*)$ differs from the underlying Josephson critical current $I_J$; three independent numerical peak searches verify this relation. The effective noise temperature $T^*$ must not simply be replaced by refrigerator temperature.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-66a2b2a9519f6f44.

Conditions: Keep each study and probe separate: 2016 pair tunneling below 50 mK; 2019 single-electron 0/8.25T comparison at 2 K. Spectroscopy and phase interpretation are not interchangeable.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Edkins and colleagues' 2019 study used single-electron STM, explicitly without scanned Josephson tunneling microscopy. At 2 K it compared 0 and 8.25 T in the same Bi2212 field of view using the same tip. Approximately eight-cell and four-cell electronic modulations support a PDW interpretation within the authors' model. The fitted Fourier widths are not exactly in a two-to-one ratio. Sublattice form factors belong to the measured electronic response and must not be copied directly onto the pair field. The core region is excluded from the simple envelope argument. Raw-data fitting and the complete supplement are not reproduced here.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-d306adac5d567426.

Conditions: Keep each study and probe separate: 2016 pair tunneling below 50 mK; 2019 single-electron 0/8.25T comparison at 2 K. Spectroscopy and phase interpretation are not interchangeable.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-experimental-criteria-4

Chen and colleagues' 2021 CsV3Sb5 work reports spatial gap/conductance modulations and Josephson spectroscopy on prepared surfaces. Bulk and surface temperature scales differ, and the author manuscript explicitly says roton excitations were not directly observed. Its proposed complex PDW interpretation is not a direct phase measurement or a universal statement about kagome superconductors. The selected manuscript and methods check is inherited from the chiral-pairing entry.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-057c43c86174f961.

Conditions: Keep each study and probe separate: 2016 pair tunneling below 50 mK; 2019 single-electron 0/8.25T comparison at 2 K. Spectroscopy and phase interpretation are not interchangeable.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-experimental-criteria-5

In May 2026, Cao and colleagues reported a hysteretic tunneling-gap transition in multilayer NbSe2 under an in-plane field, consistent with a possible orbital FFLO state. Their reported angle, disorder and thickness dependences matter; the selected theoretical discussion neglects vortices in its energy comparison. This is evidence for a transition with a proposed interpretation, not a direct image of finite pair momentum. Only the publisher abstract, introduction and selected model passage have been checked here.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-ad66f48ab9369ce9.

Conditions: Keep each study and probe separate: 2016 pair tunneling below 50 mK; 2019 single-electron 0/8.25T comparison at 2 K. Spectroscopy and phase interpretation are not interchangeable.

### scwiki-c8-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Keep four distinctions explicit: pair tunneling versus single-electron tunneling; induced modulation versus a primary instability; field-induced versus spontaneous behavior; and a surface observation versus a bulk thermodynamic phase. A particular gap map cannot alone determine the pair phase. A nonzero composite amplitude, a half-vortex proposal or an unusual transport curve likewise needs a separate coherence and alternative-explanation analysis.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-66a2b2a9519f6f44, source-d306adac5d567426, source-cb08c313e0597487.

Conditions: Surface and bulk, induced and primary, charge and pair observables are distinct. No material-wide proof inferred from a modulation.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and independent examples only; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c8-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

The 2026 report by Wang and colleagues deliberately calls its moiré result Cooper-pair density modulation (CPDM): the authors describe periodic order-parameter variation without additional translation-symmetry breaking. That distinction prevents treating every periodic pairing texture as a spontaneous PDW. This entry has checked the institutional abstract and publication identity, not the complete measurement or microscopic model.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-61d655195d7db259.

Conditions: Surface and bulk, induced and primary, charge and pair observables are distinct. No material-wide proof inferred from a modulation.

Store the probe, temperature, magnetic-field magnitude and orientation, surface preparation, Fourier convention, uniform component and normalization with every candidate. Compare observations with an explicit response model before assigning an order parameter. Our local algebra, peak and overlap checks test stated examples; they do not reproduce the experiments, establish a material ground state, or close full scientific acceptance.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-7148789acde770d4, source-66a2b2a9519f6f44, source-d306adac5d567426, source-ad66f48ab9369ce9.

articles.body:
## Scope

Spin singlet and spin triplet describe antisymmetric and symmetric two-electron spin states. They do not, by themselves, identify a crystal representation, a pairing mechanism, chirality or topology. The familiar even-parity singlet / odd-parity triplet rule assumes even-frequency pairing and a symmetric orbital or band exchange sector. State these assumptions before applying it to a material. [R1](#ref-source-8d1b859d5ffcad9f) [R4](#ref-source-0342c1624c6eb6d0)

Spin–orbit coupling (SOC) makes physical spin different from a band label. In a time-reversal-invariant centrosymmetric normal state, inversion combined with time reversal produces a degenerate pair at each momentum. Such a doublet need not transform under crystal rotations as an ordinary spin-1/2 pseudospin: Samokhin identifies exceptional twofold bands where the usual axial-vector transformation of the triplet component fails. His classification retains even/odd intraband components in its static convention; the exception concerns crystal transformation rules, not the Pauli principle. [R5](#ref-source-f2133d67ac862ff4)

## Mathematical assumptions

For a homogeneous pair correlation with combined spin and orbital indices $a,b$, fermion exchange requires $F_{ab}(\mathbf k,i\omega_n)=-F_{ba}(-\mathbf k,-i\omega_n)$. If spin, momentum, orbital and frequency exchange can each be diagonalized, their signs obey $s_Ss_Ps_Os_\omega=-1$. Here frequency exchange is not the physical time-reversal operation. For $s_O=s_\omega=+1$, spin singlet implies even momentum parity and triplet implies odd momentum parity. Reversing either the orbital or frequency sign reverses that implication. An independent matrix check tests all 16 sign combinations, accepting eight and rejecting eight. These are allowed symmetry sectors, not evidence that all are stable phases. [R4](#ref-source-0342c1624c6eb6d0)

In a chosen spin-1/2 basis, write the static gap matrix $\Delta=(\psi+\mathbf d\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma)i\sigma_y$. The scalar is the spin-antisymmetric component; the vector multiplies symmetric spin matrices. An analogous decomposition in a band doublet must retain that basis's actual symmetry matrices. In higher-angular-momentum low-energy bands, coupled angular-momentum sectors replace a simple singlet/triplet classification; microscopic fermion antisymmetry still applies. Leggett's helium framework and crystal symmetry classifications are useful references, with their respective physical settings kept separate. The 1976 Leggett correction withdraws a historical factor-of-two discrepancy claim. [R1](#ref-source-8d1b859d5ffcad9f) [R2](#ref-source-b4553aaaeacb3c3d) [R3](#ref-source-24556d6dba4d8cc1) [R4](#ref-source-0342c1624c6eb6d0) [R5](#ref-source-f2133d67ac862ff4)

For the illustrative noncentrosymmetric Hamiltonian $h=\xi I+\alpha\mathbf g\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma$, take real odd $\mathbf g(-\mathbf k)=-\mathbf g(\mathbf k)$ and an imposed even singlet gap $\psi i\sigma_y$. The anomalous Green function can contain a triplet component even though the imposed triplet gap is zero. ## Experimental criteria

A Knight shift includes spin and orbital contributions and depends on field direction, SOC, hyperfine coupling and the superconducting measurement conditions. Pustogow and colleagues' 2019 Sr2RuO4 study used reduced radio-frequency excitation to address heating and reported a spin-susceptibility reduction. The selected author-version passages checked here do not establish every possible representation. The 2026 muon result adds a low-field constraint, with a finite temperature floor and extrapolation assumptions; it also does not constitute a complete order-parameter identification. Compare the actual susceptibility tensor and conditions with competing states. [R9](#ref-source-c7f8b99a795aba41) [R10](#ref-source-c4434644191d0174)

An upper critical field above a simple weak-coupling Pauli estimate is not a stand-alone triplet test. Orbital depairing, SOC, strong coupling, multiband effects and field direction must be addressed. In particular, Frigeri's field calculation neglects orbital depairing and considers a continuous instability: its formally large paramagnetic limit is not an unlimited physical upper critical field. In UTe2, the discovery paper's measured field range and higher extrapolated scale must remain distinct. [R6](#ref-source-6c944305286c9cad) [R14](#ref-source-ca6322be2694e430)

UGe2, URhGe and UCoGe motivate triplet and equal-spin pairing through superconductivity associated with ferromagnetism, but discovery evidence does not determine a complete odd-parity representation. Check microscopic coexistence and sample volume rather than infer them solely from two transition anomalies. UTe2 must not be placed in the same category of established long-range ferromagnetic superconductors; its historical interpretation is not a substitute for a current material-specific review. The uranium discovery abstracts and selected UTe2 text have different review depths here. [R11](#ref-source-db2917242488a101) [R12](#ref-source-15aec45a868e9fb9) [R13](#ref-source-a4695ba5bfa789f3) [R14](#ref-source-ca6322be2694e430)

Do not infer a singlet–triplet mixing fraction from crystal inversion breaking. Symmetry permits compatible components; microscopic interactions decide their magnitude. Conversely, an orbital-antisymmetric spin-triplet sector can have even momentum parity at even frequency. Neither an unchanged Knight shift nor a measured decrease alone fixes all SOC-coupled possibilities. A ferromagnetic background, a large critical field, nodes or broken time reversal similarly fails to identify a unique representation. Keep spin structure, momentum parity, orbital exchange, frequency dependence, crystal representation and topology as separate questions. The finite tests on this page validate specified algebra; they do not establish energetic stability or reproduce susceptibility data. ## Discovery implications

For each candidate, record inversion and magnetic symmetries, the electronic basis, orbital or band indices, frequency convention, field direction, temperature, heating controls, measured observables and alternative explanations. Report a proposed gap only at the level supported by mutually consistent probes and a stated response model. Retain both Frigeri papers when using the corrected SOC argument. Full scientific acceptance, complete version comparisons and experimental reproduction remain open. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-c9-claim-scope-1

Spin singlet and spin triplet describe antisymmetric and symmetric two-electron spin states. They do not, by themselves, identify a crystal representation, a pairing mechanism, chirality or topology. The familiar even-parity singlet / odd-parity triplet rule assumes even-frequency pairing and a symmetric orbital or band exchange sector. State these assumptions before applying it to a material.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-8d1b859d5ffcad9f, source-0342c1624c6eb6d0.

Conditions: Distinguish physical spin, band doublet and crystal representation; static intraband parity is conditional on the named basis.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and independent finite examples; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c9-claim-scope-2

Spin–orbit coupling (SOC) makes physical spin different from a band label. In a time-reversal-invariant centrosymmetric normal state, inversion combined with time reversal produces a degenerate pair at each momentum. Such a doublet need not transform under crystal rotations as an ordinary spin-1/2 pseudospin: Samokhin identifies exceptional twofold bands where the usual axial-vector transformation of the triplet component fails. His classification retains even/odd intraband components in its static convention; the exception concerns crystal transformation rules, not the Pauli principle.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f2133d67ac862ff4.

Conditions: Distinguish physical spin, band doublet and crystal representation; static intraband parity is conditional on the named basis.

### scwiki-c9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

For a homogeneous pair correlation with combined spin and orbital indices $a,b$, fermion exchange requires $F_{ab}(\mathbf k,i\omega_n)=-F_{ba}(-\mathbf k,-i\omega_n)$. If spin, momentum, orbital and frequency exchange can each be diagonalized, their signs obey $s_Ss_Ps_Os_\omega=-1$. Here frequency exchange is not the physical time-reversal operation. For $s_O=s_\omega=+1$, spin singlet implies even momentum parity and triplet implies odd momentum parity. Reversing either the orbital or frequency sign reverses that implication. An independent matrix check tests all 16 sign combinations, accepting eight and rejecting eight. These are allowed symmetry sectors, not evidence that all are stable phases.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-0342c1624c6eb6d0.

Conditions: Exchange-product rule for resolved sectors. Imposed Nambu/helicity gap examples, no self-consistency, material stability or transition prediction. Frigeri approximation and erratum both retained.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and independent finite examples; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-c9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

In a chosen spin-1/2 basis, write the static gap matrix $\Delta=(\psi+\mathbf d\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma)i\sigma_y$. The scalar is the spin-antisymmetric component; the vector multiplies symmetric spin matrices. An analogous decomposition in a band doublet must retain that basis's actual symmetry matrices. In higher-angular-momentum low-energy bands, coupled angular-momentum sectors replace a simple singlet/triplet classification; microscopic fermion antisymmetry still applies. Leggett's helium framework and crystal symmetry classifications are useful references, with their respective physical settings kept separate. The 1976 Leggett correction withdraws a historical factor-of-two discrepancy claim.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-8d1b859d5ffcad9f, source-b4553aaaeacb3c3d, source-24556d6dba4d8cc1, source-0342c1624c6eb6d0, source-f2133d67ac862ff4.

### scwiki-c9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

For the illustrative noncentrosymmetric Hamiltonian $h=\xi I+\alpha\mathbf g\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma$, take real odd $\mathbf g(-\mathbf k)=-\mathbf g(\mathbf k)$ and an imposed even singlet gap $\psi i\sigma_y$. The anomalous Green function can contain a triplet component even though the imposed triplet gap is zero. Twelve independent matrix inversions reproduce the helicity-projector expression, in the specified Nambu convention, $F=-\sum_{\lambda=\pm}\psi P_\lambda i\sigma_y/[\omega_n^2+(\xi+\lambda\alpha|\mathbf g|)^2+|\psi|^2]$, where $P_\lambda=(I+\lambda\hat{\mathbf g}\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma)/2$. Different denominators generate a triplet correlation; they coincide at the particle-hole-symmetric test point. This distinguishes a pair correlation from a self-consistent triplet order parameter. The calculation is an imposed mean-field example, not a prediction of a material's mixing ratio.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-6c944305286c9cad.

Conditions: Exchange-product rule for resolved sectors. Imposed Nambu/helicity gap examples, no self-consistency, material stability or transition prediction. Frigeri approximation and erratum both retained.

### scwiki-c9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-4

With an imposed aligned component $\mathbf d=d\hat{\mathbf g}$, the two gap magnitudes are $|\psi+d|$ and $|\psi-d|$ in this simple model. Five direct gap-matrix checks recover the squared magnitudes, including complex relative phase. A zero in one branch requires the appropriate cancellation, not merely the absence of inversion symmetry. The interaction, band structure and gap equation must determine the actual amplitudes. At points where $\mathbf g=0$, its unit vector and this helicity construction require separate treatment.

### scwiki-c9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-5

Frigeri and colleagues' weak-coupling calculation neglects small singlet–triplet coupling terms associated with particle-hole asymmetry and analyzes the channels separately. Its leading triplet suppression contains $|\mathbf d|^2-|\hat{\mathbf g}\cdot\mathbf d|^2$: alignment avoids this particular suppression. The erratum adds an omitted linear term to the MnSi SOC vector, $\mathbf g=\alpha_1\mathbf k+\alpha_2[k_x(k_y^2-k_z^2),k_y(k_z^2-k_x^2),k_z(k_x^2-k_y^2)]$. Thus a conclusion about suppression of a p-wave component depends on the relative coefficients; alignment alone does not choose the stable state. Three independent angular examples check that dependence without calculating a transition temperature. The erratum also rescales the original Fig. 2 SOC parameter by dividing it by $\sqrt{3/2}$.

### scwiki-c9-claim-experimental-criteria-1

A Knight shift includes spin and orbital contributions and depends on field direction, SOC, hyperfine coupling and the superconducting measurement conditions. Pustogow and colleagues' 2019 Sr2RuO4 study used reduced radio-frequency excitation to address heating and reported a spin-susceptibility reduction. The selected author-version passages checked here do not establish every possible representation. The 2026 muon result adds a low-field constraint, with a finite temperature floor and extrapolation assumptions; it also does not constitute a complete order-parameter identification. Compare the actual susceptibility tensor and conditions with competing states.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-c7f8b99a795aba41, source-c4434644191d0174.

### scwiki-c9-claim-experimental-criteria-2

An upper critical field above a simple weak-coupling Pauli estimate is not a stand-alone triplet test. Orbital depairing, SOC, strong coupling, multiband effects and field direction must be addressed. In particular, Frigeri's field calculation neglects orbital depairing and considers a continuous instability: its formally large paramagnetic limit is not an unlimited physical upper critical field. In UTe2, the discovery paper's measured field range and higher extrapolated scale must remain distinct.

UGe2, URhGe and UCoGe motivate triplet and equal-spin pairing through superconductivity associated with ferromagnetism, but discovery evidence does not determine a complete odd-parity representation. Phase-sensitive junctions, impurity response and spin-sensitive probes can provide complementary constraints, but interfaces can select or generate correlations absent from the bulk gap. Tanaka and Golubov's proximity theory explicitly permits odd-frequency, even-parity triplet correlations in a diffusive normal metal. That is not by itself an intrinsic odd-frequency bulk superconducting phase. The publisher abstract has been checked; the full junction derivation remains open.

### scwiki-c9-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Do not infer a singlet–triplet mixing fraction from crystal inversion breaking. Symmetry permits compatible components; microscopic interactions decide their magnitude. Conversely, an orbital-antisymmetric spin-triplet sector can have even momentum parity at even frequency. Physical-spin pairing and the intraband pseudospin gap can therefore carry different descriptions after projection. Clepkens and colleagues' interorbital “shadowed-triplet” construction illustrates this distinction as a model proposed for Sr2RuO4, not an experimentally established assignment. Only its author abstract and publication identity are checked here.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-0342c1624c6eb6d0, source-6c944305286c9cad, source-2928c6abb9344456.

### scwiki-c9-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

Neither an unchanged Knight shift nor a measured decrease alone fixes all SOC-coupled possibilities. A ferromagnetic background, a large critical field, nodes or broken time reversal similarly fails to identify a unique representation. Keep spin structure, momentum parity, orbital exchange, frequency dependence, crystal representation and topology as separate questions. The finite tests on this page validate specified algebra; they do not establish energetic stability or reproduce susceptibility data.

claims.statement: An elemental superconductor contains one chemical element, but that label does not specify its crystal structure, bands, coupling strength or pressure history. Elemental systems provide useful benchmarks for electron–phonon theory; they do not all reduce to one weak-coupling model. Niobium's approximately 9.2 K transition is a useful conventional scale, not a ceiling on elemental superconductivity or a certified value for every sample.

articles.body:
## Scope

An elemental superconductor contains one chemical element, but that label does not specify its crystal structure, bands, coupling strength or pressure history. Elemental systems provide useful benchmarks for electron–phonon theory; they do not all reduce to one weak-coupling model. Niobium's approximately 9.2 K transition is a useful conventional scale, not a ceiling on elemental superconductivity or a certified value for every sample. [R5](#ref-source-aa8182fe7a3d8d0c) [R15](#ref-source-835031575efae07a)

The mercury discovery is associated with Onnes's 1911 report. His later Nobel lecture describes the abrupt resistance decrease near 4.2 K, explicitly qualified by measurement accuracy, and a current threshold above which voltage reappeared. The lecture scan includes subsequent notes and a 1914 addendum; those later observations should not be dated to 1911. It is a firsthand account, not a substitute for a modern magnetic-volume or heat-capacity measurement. [R1](#ref-source-d36e5a81b57e823f)

## Mathematical assumptions

The isotope coefficient is $\alpha=-d\ln T_c/d\ln M$. If harmonic frequencies scale as $M^{-1/2}$ while the dimensionless pairing parameters remain fixed, the corresponding transition scale has $\alpha=1/2$. This is a conditional model statement, not a value certified here for the original mercury datasets. Maxwell and Reynolds are retained as the historical experimental sources; their full datasets still require direct review. An isotope substitution may also change structure or anharmonic motion, so a measured coefficient must retain its sample and phase conditions. [R2](#ref-source-eff5a2a1c455e7f6) [R3](#ref-source-e8a489943f13c9f8) [R6](#ref-source-0620df96ebbf2a66)

The weak-coupling isotropic BCS benchmark is $2\Delta(0)/(k_BT_c)\simeq3.53$. Lead is a strong-coupling benchmark, so that number is not a compulsory fit to its tunneling spectrum. Retardation makes the gap energy dependent; a full gap alone does not establish its sign structure or the microscopic pairing interaction. [R16](#ref-source-d56b04dc0b32c796) [R17](#ref-source-ba10e800a1246bf6)

For an illustrative McMillan-type estimate, write $T_c=(\omega_{\log}/1.2)\exp[-A/D]$, with $A=1.04(1+\lambda)$ and $D=\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda)>0$, taking $\omega_{\log}$ in kelvin. If $\mu^*=\mu/[1+\mu\ln(E_{\mathrm{el}}/\omega_{\log})]$, with the two cutoff scales in the same units, fixed $\lambda,\mu,E_{\mathrm{el}}$ give $\alpha=\tfrac12[1-A(1+0.62\lambda)(\mu^*)^2/D^2]$. Three finite-difference mass substitutions independently confirm this derivative and its difference from the fixed-$\mu^*$ limit. These examples are not mercury fits. The estimate omits the full Allen–Dynes shape factors and is not a universal upper bound. [R5](#ref-source-aa8182fe7a3d8d0c) [R6](#ref-source-0620df96ebbf2a66) [R16](#ref-source-d56b04dc0b32c796)

In the Sc paper's Table I, six printed estimates are consistent with the input rounding intervals. Sc-IV printed inputs yield 21.37/18.72 K, versus listed 21.5/18.8 K; exact reproduction needs unrounded inputs. Sc-V at 260 GPa gives 30.07/26.38 K for $\mu^*=0.10/0.13$. These are calculations, not the measured 37.6 K onset at a different pressure. The reported extrapolated $B_{c2}(0)=21.3$ T implies $\xi=\sqrt{\Phi_0/(2\pi B_{c2})}=39.31$ angstrom; this checks units, not the extrapolation model. [R10](#ref-source-dc73a11d591aebd0)

## Experimental criteria

Tunneling is valuable when the measured superconducting conductance is normalized by an appropriate normal reference. Rowell's 1970 account states the crucial conditions: the current must be tunneling current and the barrier must remain effectively unchanged through the transition. Unnormalized structure can instead reflect the barrier or its excitations. The 1965 McMillan–Rowell paper establishes the historical lead inversion reference, but its original quantitative inversion has not been independently rerun here. A phonon density of states alone is not the coupling-weighted spectrum $\alpha^2F$. [R4](#ref-source-b66885f8fdc58181) [R7](#ref-source-27b24b231ced1ec3) [R16](#ref-source-d56b04dc0b32c796)

Lithium illustrates why conditions cannot be dropped from a material label. Shimizu and colleagues reported compressed Li reaching about 20 K at 48 GPa in 2002; Tuoriniemi and colleagues reported an ambient-pressure transition around 0.4 mK in 2007, with a Meissner-state figure. The latter is 0.0004 K, not 0.4 K. These source checks cover abstracts and selected captions; they do not establish an entire phase diagram or independently validate the underlying data. [R8](#ref-source-cc7115129638a171) [R9](#ref-source-61e8b60fcacfb53b)

Wang and colleagues reported Sc onset at 37.6 K and 243 GPa, distinct from the plotted 37.3 K at 244 GPa. Four-probe warming measurements used diamond Raman pressure calibration; onset means departure from the normal-state line. Field/current suppression supports the transport assignment, but no Meissner measurement was supplied. Phase boundaries were inferred from transition trends and compared with earlier diffraction. Applied fields reached 9 T; 21.3 T is an extrapolation. [R10](#ref-source-dc73a11d591aebd0)

Sakata and colleagues reported Ca-VII near 29 K at 216 GPa. Their selected methods describe room-temperature diffraction and transport; a room-temperature structure measurement does not automatically determine the low-temperature phase. An Andersson comment is part of the source trail, but its contents have not yet been obtained in this review. The reported result remains attributed to its authors, with that reconciliation open. [R11](#ref-source-bc42a3144ddb335e) [R12](#ref-source-c563fd6be7dd9167)

Iron is another warning against classification by ambient behavior. Shimizu and colleagues reported a resistance drop and Meissner signal below 2 K under 15–30 GPa in the non-magnetic state. This abstract-level evidence does not identify the pairing interaction or justify transferring a simple weak-coupling description from an unrelated element. Magnetic history, structure and purity need their own assessment. [R13](#ref-source-7301d50108f9de56)

## Limits and disputes

A finite resistive transition, instrument-limited zero resistance, field suppression, magnetic shielding and a bulk thermodynamic anomaly answer different questions. Compare them on the same sample or explain why samples differ. Report the thermometer, onset/midpoint/zero criterion, pressure calibration, pressure medium, compression path and structural measurement temperature. Missing information stays unknown rather than being inferred from the chemical formula. [R1](#ref-source-d36e5a81b57e823f) [R8](#ref-source-cc7115129638a171) [R10](#ref-source-dc73a11d591aebd0) [R11](#ref-source-bc42a3144ddb335e)

The September 2026 Sc theory paper connects compression, increasing overlap of 3d orbitals and band broadening to stronger electron–phonon coupling. Its phrase “electronic mechanism” does not mean a demonstrated nonphonon pairing glue. This page has checked the publisher abstract only: no new experimental transition, full calculation or universal elemental record is inferred from that description. Historical “highest” claims must be dated to the publication and its comparison set. [R14](#ref-source-29962a8944db57fa)

## Discovery implications

Treat an element as a collection of phase-specific test cases. Useful screening combines a dynamically and thermodynamically plausible structure, electron–phonon matrix elements, electronic energy scales and a stated Coulomb treatment, then asks which experimental observable could falsify the prediction. Agreement with one transition temperature does not validate the whole spectral function, numerical convergence or phase assignment. Keep calculated values separate from experimental transition records and preserve negative or incomplete evidence. [R5](#ref-source-aa8182fe7a3d8d0c) [R6](#ref-source-0620df96ebbf2a66) [R16](#ref-source-d56b04dc0b32c796)

## Related topics

Continue with [isotope effects](/scwiki/isotope-effect), [BCS theory](/scwiki/bcs-weak-coupling), [Eliashberg theory](/scwiki/eliashberg-strong-coupling), [superconducting gaps](/scwiki/superconducting-gap) and [critical fields](/scwiki/critical-fields).

## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d1-claim-scope-1

An elemental superconductor contains one chemical element, but that label does not specify its crystal structure, bands, coupling strength or pressure history. Elemental systems provide useful benchmarks for electron–phonon theory; they do not all reduce to one weak-coupling model. Niobium's approximately 9.2 K transition is a useful conventional scale, not a ceiling on elemental superconductivity or a certified value for every sample.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-aa8182fe7a3d8d0c, source-835031575efae07a.

Conditions: Element, phase and sample conditions; historical lecture dates separated.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and bounded independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-d1-claim-scope-2

The mercury discovery is associated with Onnes's 1911 report. His later Nobel lecture describes the abrupt resistance decrease near 4.2 K, explicitly qualified by measurement accuracy, and a current threshold above which voltage reappeared. The lecture scan includes subsequent notes and a 1914 addendum; those later observations should not be dated to 1911. It is a firsthand account, not a substitute for a modern magnetic-volume or heat-capacity measurement.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-d36e5a81b57e823f.

Conditions: Element, phase and sample conditions; historical lecture dates separated.

### scwiki-d1-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

The isotope coefficient is $\alpha=-d\ln T_c/d\ln M$. If harmonic frequencies scale as $M^{-1/2}$ while the dimensionless pairing parameters remain fixed, the corresponding transition scale has $\alpha=1/2$. This is a conditional model statement, not a value certified here for the original mercury datasets. Maxwell and Reynolds are retained as the historical experimental sources; their full datasets still require direct review. An isotope substitution may also change structure or anharmonic motion, so a measured coefficient must retain its sample and phase conditions.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-eff5a2a1c455e7f6, source-e8a489943f13c9f8, source-0620df96ebbf2a66.

Conditions: Finite imposed isotope model and printed-parameter formula check; no DFT, stability or experimental replication.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and bounded independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-d1-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

The weak-coupling isotropic BCS benchmark is $2\Delta(0)/(k_BT_c)\simeq3.53$. Lead is a strong-coupling benchmark, so that number is not a compulsory fit to its tunneling spectrum. Retardation makes the gap energy dependent; a full gap alone does not establish its sign structure or the microscopic pairing interaction.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-d56b04dc0b32c796, source-ba10e800a1246bf6.

Conditions: Finite imposed isotope model and printed-parameter formula check; no DFT, stability or experimental replication.

Verification scope: Named primary passages and bounded independent examples only; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-d1-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

For an illustrative McMillan-type estimate, write $T_c=(\omega_{\log}/1.2)\exp[-A/D]$, with $A=1.04(1+\lambda)$ and $D=\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda)>0$, taking $\omega_{\log}$ in kelvin. If $\mu^*=\mu/[1+\mu\ln(E_{\mathrm{el}}/\omega_{\log})]$, with the two cutoff scales in the same units, fixed $\lambda,\mu,E_{\mathrm{el}}$ give $\alpha=\tfrac12[1-A(1+0.62\lambda)(\mu^*)^2/D^2]$. Three finite-difference mass substitutions independently confirm this derivative and its difference from the fixed-$\mu^*$ limit. These examples are not mercury fits. The estimate omits the full Allen–Dynes shape factors and is not a universal upper bound.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-aa8182fe7a3d8d0c, source-0620df96ebbf2a66, source-d56b04dc0b32c796.

Conditions: Finite imposed isotope model and printed-parameter formula check; no DFT, stability or experimental replication.

### scwiki-d1-claim-experimental-criteria-1

Tunneling is valuable when the measured superconducting conductance is normalized by an appropriate normal reference. Rowell's 1970 account states the crucial conditions: the current must be tunneling current and the barrier must remain effectively unchanged through the transition. Unnormalized structure can instead reflect the barrier or its excitations. The 1965 McMillan–Rowell paper establishes the historical lead inversion reference, but its original quantitative inversion has not been independently rerun here. A phonon density of states alone is not the coupling-weighted spectrum $\alpha^2F$.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-b66885f8fdc58181, source-27b24b231ced1ec3, source-d56b04dc0b32c796.

Conditions: Keep named source, phase, pressure and measurement criteria; abstract-only and inaccessible-comment scopes explicit.

Lithium illustrates why conditions cannot be dropped from a material label. Shimizu and colleagues reported compressed Li reaching about 20 K at 48 GPa in 2002; Tuoriniemi and colleagues reported an ambient-pressure transition around 0.4 mK in 2007, with a Meissner-state figure. Wang and colleagues reported Sc onset at 37.6 K and 243 GPa, distinct from the plotted 37.3 K at 244 GPa. ### scwiki-d1-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

A finite resistive transition, instrument-limited zero resistance, field suppression, magnetic shielding and a bulk thermodynamic anomaly answer different questions. Compare them on the same sample or explain why samples differ. Report the thermometer, onset/midpoint/zero criterion, pressure calibration, pressure medium, compression path and structural measurement temperature. Missing information stays unknown rather than being inferred from the chemical formula.

The September 2026 Sc theory paper connects compression, increasing overlap of 3d orbitals and band broadening to stronger electron–phonon coupling. Its phrase “electronic mechanism” does not mean a demonstrated nonphonon pairing glue. This page has checked the publisher abstract only: no new experimental transition, full calculation or universal elemental record is inferred from that description. Historical “highest” claims must be dated to the publication and its comparison set.

### scwiki-d1-claim-discovery-implications-1

Treat an element as a collection of phase-specific test cases. Useful screening combines a dynamically and thermodynamically plausible structure, electron–phonon matrix elements, electronic energy scales and a stated Coulomb treatment, then asks which experimental observable could falsify the prediction. Agreement with one transition temperature does not validate the whole spectral function, numerical convergence or phase assignment. Keep calculated values separate from experimental transition records and preserve negative or incomplete evidence.

claims.statement: Organic charge-transfer salts provide distinct low-dimensional settings for superconductivity. The Bechgaard salts (TMTSF)₂X have strongly anisotropic electronic motion; the κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂X family has conducting molecular layers and is widely studied near a pressure-controlled Mott transition. The anion, molecular packing, sample history and field direction are part of the material identity. A pairing assignment for one salt or field regime is not a classification of the entire family.

claims.statement: Izawa's rotating-field thermal-conductivity analysis separates $\kappa(\theta)=C_0+C_2\cos(2\theta)+C_4\cos(4\theta)$, where the angle is between the heat current and the in-plane field. The large twofold term has a substantial phonon-scattering contribution, whereas the low-temperature fourfold term is interpreted through nodal quasiparticles. An independent synthetic harmonic-recovery check confirms the decomposition algebra, not the original fit or the inferred gap symmetry. A 45° rotation reverses the sign of the fourfold basis function, so node labels require a stated crystallographic convention.

claims.statement: The normal-state anisotropic shift used by Shinagawa is $K=K_{\mathrm{iso}}+K_{\mathrm{ax}}(3\cos^2\theta-1)$, with $K_{\mathrm{iso}}=3.9\times10^{-4}$ and $K_{\mathrm{ax}}=10.5\times10^{-4}$. Substitution gives 2,490 ppm at 0° and −660 ppm at 90°. These are signed model contributions, not directly the observed superconducting change. Reducing the spin contribution can move resonance shifts in opposite directions for two orientations. articles.body:
## Scope

Organic charge-transfer salts provide distinct low-dimensional settings for superconductivity. The Bechgaard salts (TMTSF)₂X have strongly anisotropic electronic motion; the κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂X family has conducting molecular layers and is widely studied near a pressure-controlled Mott transition. The anion, molecular packing, sample history and field direction are part of the material identity. A pairing assignment for one salt or field regime is not a classification of the entire family. [R3](#ref-source-2cc5358d54a65217) [R9](#ref-source-39706a37d6f5ce86) [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

The 1980 Jérome report identifies superconductivity in (TMTSF)₂PF₆. Its bibliographic identity is checked here, while the original experimental text remains an access gap. For κ-Br, the 1990 Kini paper explicitly distinguishes an inductive onset of 11.6 K from a resistive onset of 12.5 K in its title. Those criteria should survive quotation and database export. Its original publication is July 1990; the publisher's 2002 online date does not move the discovery into a later decade. [R1](#ref-source-2c57ae9e6e679429) [R2](#ref-source-c3edeba243e544d9)

## Mathematical assumptions

Izawa's rotating-field thermal-conductivity analysis separates $\kappa(\theta)=C_0+C_2\cos(2\theta)+C_4\cos(4\theta)$, where the angle is between the heat current and the in-plane field. The large twofold term has a substantial phonon-scattering contribution, whereas the low-temperature fourfold term is interpreted through nodal quasiparticles. An independent synthetic harmonic-recovery check confirms the decomposition algebra, not the original fit or the inferred gap symmetry. A 45° rotation reverses the sign of the fourfold basis function, so node labels require a stated crystallographic convention. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76)

The normal-state anisotropic shift used by Shinagawa is $K=K_{\mathrm{iso}}+K_{\mathrm{ax}}(3\cos^2\theta-1)$, with $K_{\mathrm{iso}}=3.9\times10^{-4}$ and $K_{\mathrm{ax}}=10.5\times10^{-4}$. Substitution gives 2,490 ppm at 0° and −660 ppm at 90°. These are signed model contributions, not directly the observed superconducting change. Reducing the spin contribution can move resonance shifts in opposite directions for two orientations. Hyperfine calibration, chemical shifts, screening fields and pulse heating must therefore accompany a spin-pairing inference. [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

Kagawa's transport analysis found approximate exponents $(\delta,\beta,\gamma)=(2,1,1)$, satisfying $\delta=1+\gamma/\beta$. Checking that identity does not independently validate a universality class. The analysis maps conductance onto an order parameter and treats pressure/temperature mixing within stated approximations; it excludes the closest region to the endpoint because of calibration and sample limitations. A later theoretical treatment shows how conductivity can couple to singular quantities other than the thermodynamic order parameter. Transport exponents and thermodynamic exponents must not be equated automatically. [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3) [R12](#ref-source-8e919dde44063203)

## Experimental criteria

Lefebvre's κ-Cl phase diagram combines proton NMR with AC susceptibility under helium-gas pressure. NMR uses a 0.5 T field perpendicular to the layers; susceptibility uses an approximately 0.05 Oe oscillating field parallel to them, without a static field. Slow pressure and temperature sweeps, restricted to helium's fluid region, resolve hysteresis and changing phase fractions. The reported meeting region near 282 bar and 13.1 K is not evidence that antiferromagnetism and superconductivity occupy every microscopic volume together: the paper explicitly discusses inhomogeneous coexistence. [R3](#ref-source-2cc5358d54a65217)

In the separate κ-Cl conductance experiment, a critical endpoint occurs near 39.7 ± 0.1 K and 24.8 ± 0.1 MPa. Here the paper's symbol Tc denotes the Mott endpoint, not a superconducting transition. Four-probe measurements, helium pressure sweeps near 3 MPa per hour and a current-independence check over two orders of magnitude underpin this assignment. The endpoint pressure is 0.0248 GPa; confusing MPa with GPa would introduce a factor of one thousand. [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3)

Izawa studies κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂Cu(NCS)₂ with a reported resistive transition near 10.4 K. Heat flows along the b axis, with in-plane field alignment better than 0.01°. At 2 T the fourfold component becomes visible around 0.52 and 0.43 K, at approximately 0.2% of the normal-state total conductivity. These low temperatures are probe conditions, not additional transition temperatures. Extracting such a small electronic modulation requires separating phonons, vortex scattering and the field/temperature regime; the sign cannot be interpreted without that model. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76)

For (TMTSF)₂ClO₄, Shinagawa's samples were cooled at 7 mK per minute through anion ordering near 24 K and showed resistive/rf onset near 1.4 K. NMR pulses with tip angles below 3° were checked for heating using simultaneous resistance measurements. Low-field shifts support reduced spin susceptibility, while relaxation near 100 mK changes sharply around 15 kOe. That crossover field is neither a superconducting temperature nor, by itself, a unique identification of an FFLO or triplet state. [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

## Limits and disputes

The earlier Lee result concerns a different salt, (TMTSF)₂PF₆, at 7 kbar with field along the conducting a axis; its abstract reports little Knight-shift change and argues for triplet pairing. The later ClO₄ study finds a low-field singlet-compatible response and leaves its high-field state unresolved. These are condition-specific observations. High upper critical fields, unchanged shifts in one regime or proximity to spin-density-wave order cannot alone establish family-wide p-wave superconductivity. [R6](#ref-source-e055004651dafe18) [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

For κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂Cu₂(CN)₃, absence of magnetic ordering down to 32 mK motivated a spin-liquid interpretation, while pressure studies found a neighboring superconducting region. Subsequent spin-gap work supports a valence-bond interpretation but does not uniquely exclude a gapped chiral spin liquid. Mounting strain and microcracks complicate comparison with a nominally hydrostatic experiment. Neither an exchange scale nor a spin-gap anomaly should become a superconducting Tc record. [R7](#ref-source-9d15cd9236072f5c) [R8](#ref-source-0443485ac20d3a8c) [R11](#ref-source-5e0dcd80e8b64a1b)

The original κ-Br reference in the pinned draft had an unrelated DOI. The correct identifier is 10.1021/ic00339a004; 10.1021/ic00331a012 identifies a metal-complex structural-analysis paper. This public article corrects the citation while preserving the fixed source file. Discovery-era methods, complete supplements, final-version comparisons and original-data refits remain outside parts of this scoped review. [R2](#ref-source-c3edeba243e544d9)

## Discovery implications

Compare pressure, chemical substitution and strain through measured phase diagrams rather than treating them as interchangeable tuning knobs. Report the exact salt, cooling protocol, pressure medium, field orientation and transition criterion before comparing performance. A useful next measurement should distinguish competing explanations—for example by combining bulk thermodynamics, low-heating spin probes and controlled-disorder studies on the same specimen. A nearby Mott state constrains a mechanism without identifying it uniquely. [R3](#ref-source-2cc5358d54a65217) [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3) [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

Molecular superconductors also provide a warning against copying symmetry names between coordinate systems. The κ-NCS thermal-conductivity paper discusses nodal directions relative to b and c as well as a rotated convention. Preserve those directions and the observable itself when comparing with theories. Fullerides belong to a separate molecular family with different orbital degeneracy and vibronic physics; the shared word “organic” does not make their pairing evidence interchangeable. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76) [R9](#ref-source-39706a37d6f5ce86)

## Related topics

Continue with [RVB and doped Mott insulators](/scwiki/rvb-and-doped-mott-insulators), [Mottness](/scwiki/mottness-and-superconductivity), [d-wave pairing](/scwiki/d-wave), [p-wave candidates](/scwiki/p-wave) and [fulleride superconductors](/scwiki/fulleride-superconductors).

# Organic superconductors: charge-transfer salts, Mott physics and pairing probes

Compare molecular salts through pressure, cooling history, nodal transport and spin response, while separating superconducting transitions from Mott endpoints and probe conditions.
