The 1980 Jérome report identifies superconductivity in (TMTSF)₂PF₆. Its bibliographic identity is checked here, while the original experimental text remains an access gap. For κ-Br, the 1990 Kini paper explicitly distinguishes an inductive onset of 11.6 K from a resistive onset of 12.5 K in its title. Those criteria should survive quotation and database export. Its original publication is July 1990; the publisher's 2002 online date does not move the discovery into a later decade. [R1](#ref-source-2c57ae9e6e679429) [R2](#ref-source-c3edeba243e544d9)

## Mathematical assumptions

Izawa's rotating-field thermal-conductivity analysis separates $\kappa(\theta)=C_0+C_2\cos(2\theta)+C_4\cos(4\theta)$, where the angle is between the heat current and the in-plane field. The large twofold term has a substantial phonon-scattering contribution, whereas the low-temperature fourfold term is interpreted through nodal quasiparticles. An independent synthetic harmonic-recovery check confirms the decomposition algebra, not the original fit or the inferred gap symmetry. A 45° rotation reverses the sign of the fourfold basis function, so node labels require a stated crystallographic convention. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76)

The normal-state anisotropic shift used by Shinagawa is $K=K_{\mathrm{iso}}+K_{\mathrm{ax}}(3\cos^2\theta-1)$, with $K_{\mathrm{iso}}=3.9\times10^{-4}$ and $K_{\mathrm{ax}}=10.5\times10^{-4}$. Substitution gives 2,490 ppm at 0° and −660 ppm at 90°. These are signed model contributions, not directly the observed superconducting change. Reducing the spin contribution can move resonance shifts in opposite directions for two orientations. Hyperfine calibration, chemical shifts, screening fields and pulse heating must therefore accompany a spin-pairing inference. [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

Kagawa's transport analysis found approximate exponents $(\delta,\beta,\gamma)=(2,1,1)$, satisfying $\delta=1+\gamma/\beta$. Checking that identity does not independently validate a universality class. The analysis maps conductance onto an order parameter and treats pressure/temperature mixing within stated approximations; it excludes the closest region to the endpoint because of calibration and sample limitations. A later theoretical treatment shows how conductivity can couple to singular quantities other than the thermodynamic order parameter. Transport exponents and thermodynamic exponents must not be equated automatically. [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3) [R12](#ref-source-8e919dde44063203)

## Experimental criteria

Lefebvre's κ-Cl phase diagram combines proton NMR with AC susceptibility under helium-gas pressure. NMR uses a 0.5 T field perpendicular to the layers; susceptibility uses an approximately 0.05 Oe oscillating field parallel to them, without a static field. Slow pressure and temperature sweeps, restricted to helium's fluid region, resolve hysteresis and changing phase fractions. The reported meeting region near 282 bar and 13.1 K is not evidence that antiferromagnetism and superconductivity occupy every microscopic volume together: the paper explicitly discusses inhomogeneous coexistence. [R3](#ref-source-2cc5358d54a65217)

In the separate κ-Cl conductance experiment, a critical endpoint occurs near 39.7 ± 0.1 K and 24.8 ± 0.1 MPa. Here the paper's symbol Tc denotes the Mott endpoint, not a superconducting transition. Four-probe measurements, helium pressure sweeps near 3 MPa per hour and a current-independence check over two orders of magnitude underpin this assignment. The endpoint pressure is 0.0248 GPa; confusing MPa with GPa would introduce a factor of one thousand. [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3)

Izawa studies κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂Cu(NCS)₂ with a reported resistive transition near 10.4 K. Heat flows along the b axis, with in-plane field alignment better than 0.01°. At 2 T the fourfold component becomes visible around 0.52 and 0.43 K, at approximately 0.2% of the normal-state total conductivity. These low temperatures are probe conditions, not additional transition temperatures. Extracting such a small electronic modulation requires separating phonons, vortex scattering and the field/temperature regime; the sign cannot be interpreted without that model. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76)

For (TMTSF)₂ClO₄, Shinagawa's samples were cooled at 7 mK per minute through anion ordering near 24 K and showed resistive/rf onset near 1.4 K. NMR pulses with tip angles below 3° were checked for heating using simultaneous resistance measurements. Low-field shifts support reduced spin susceptibility, while relaxation near 100 mK changes sharply around 15 kOe. That crossover field is neither a superconducting temperature nor, by itself, a unique identification of an FFLO or triplet state. [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

## Limits and disputes

The earlier Lee result concerns a different salt, (TMTSF)₂PF₆, at 7 kbar with field along the conducting a axis; its abstract reports little Knight-shift change and argues for triplet pairing. The later ClO₄ study finds a low-field singlet-compatible response and leaves its high-field state unresolved. These are condition-specific observations. High upper critical fields, unchanged shifts in one regime or proximity to spin-density-wave order cannot alone establish family-wide p-wave superconductivity. [R6](#ref-source-e055004651dafe18) [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

For κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂Cu₂(CN)₃, absence of magnetic ordering down to 32 mK motivated a spin-liquid interpretation, while pressure studies found a neighboring superconducting region. Subsequent spin-gap work supports a valence-bond interpretation but does not uniquely exclude a gapped chiral spin liquid. Mounting strain and microcracks complicate comparison with a nominally hydrostatic experiment. Neither an exchange scale nor a spin-gap anomaly should become a superconducting Tc record. [R7](#ref-source-9d15cd9236072f5c) [R8](#ref-source-0443485ac20d3a8c) [R11](#ref-source-5e0dcd80e8b64a1b)

The original κ-Br reference in the pinned draft had an unrelated DOI. The correct identifier is 10.1021/ic00339a004; 10.1021/ic00331a012 identifies a metal-complex structural-analysis paper. This public article corrects the citation while preserving the fixed source file. Discovery-era methods, complete supplements, final-version comparisons and original-data refits remain outside parts of this scoped review. [R2](#ref-source-c3edeba243e544d9)

## Discovery implications

Compare pressure, chemical substitution and strain through measured phase diagrams rather than treating them as interchangeable tuning knobs. Report the exact salt, cooling protocol, pressure medium, field orientation and transition criterion before comparing performance. A useful next measurement should distinguish competing explanations—for example by combining bulk thermodynamics, low-heating spin probes and controlled-disorder studies on the same specimen. A nearby Mott state constrains a mechanism without identifying it uniquely. [R3](#ref-source-2cc5358d54a65217) [R4](#ref-source-09e9a4299e3fd1d3) [R10](#ref-source-c08f058f3170fafa)

Molecular superconductors also provide a warning against copying symmetry names between coordinate systems. The κ-NCS thermal-conductivity paper discusses nodal directions relative to b and c as well as a rotated convention. Preserve those directions and the observable itself when comparing with theories. Fullerides belong to a separate molecular family with different orbital degeneracy and vibronic physics; the shared word “organic” does not make their pairing evidence interchangeable. [R5](#ref-source-9fb11dd7e1fcdc76) [R9](#ref-source-39706a37d6f5ce86)

Organic charge-transfer salts provide distinct low-dimensional settings for superconductivity. The Bechgaard salts (TMTSF)₂X have strongly anisotropic electronic motion; the κ-(BEDT-TTF)₂X family has conducting molecular layers and is widely studied near a pressure-controlled Mott transition. The anion, molecular packing, sample history and field direction are part of the material identity. A pairing assignment for one salt or field regime is not a classification of the entire family.

articles.body:
## Scope

Two-dimensional geometry and interface location describe different properties. Weak out-of-plane dispersion does not alone establish a two-dimensional phase transition. An interface can support a superconducting region between constituents that are not superconducting separately. Charge redistribution, oxygen defects, strain, orbital structure and disorder can change together, so an enhanced transition does not identify one universal interface mechanism. [R1](#ref-source-ea5d0c80335c450d) [R2](#ref-source-684b96e9dbb65a64)

Pair formation and macroscopic phase coherence need not coincide. Every temperature below retains its probe and criterion: a spectral gap, resistance onset, noise-floor zero, magnetic screening or BKT analysis. An ultrathin film may also have finite lateral size, nonuniform current paths and coupling to its substrate. These conditions matter when comparing it with an ideal phase model. [R4](#ref-source-a95bcf0cb2681557) [R6](#ref-source-8f81510a80c35e3a) [R8](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

## Mathematical assumptions

In the convention $F=(J_s/2)\int d^2r\,|\nabla\theta|^2$, the ideal BKT jump is $k_BT_{\mathrm{BKT}}=\pi J_s(T_{\mathrm{BKT}}^-)/2$. Here $J_s$ is the long-wavelength, renormalized total phase stiffness, with units of energy. It is not the bare pairing amplitude or a separately measured geometric contribution. Magnetic screening, finite size and interlayer coupling limit the length scales over which the logarithmic-vortex description applies. BCS-like amplitude formation and BKT phase ordering are not mutually exclusive microscopic pairing mechanisms. [R6](#ref-source-8f81510a80c35e3a) [R7](#ref-source-408113812912d816)

For a homogeneous local sheet response, $J_s=\hbar^2/(4e^2L_k)$ relates the same stiffness to sheet kinetic inductance. Combining it with the jump gives $L_k=\Phi_0^2/(8\pi k_BT_{\mathrm{BKT}})$, where $\Phi_0=h/(2e)$. Independent electron-density and pair-density conventions give the same conversion. At a hypothetical 0.188 K jump it predicts approximately 65.5 nH per square; this is a model conversion, not an inductance measured in Reyren's device. Finite-frequency response must not be silently identified with the asymptotic equilibrium stiffness. [R6](#ref-source-8f81510a80c35e3a) [R8](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

## Experimental criteria

A convincing BKT comparison combines current–voltage behavior, an appropriate resistance-fluctuation regime and stiffness where available. An apparent cubic law over a chosen current interval is insufficient: the synthetic response $V=I+I^3$ has nearly cubic high-current behavior while retaining finite low-current resistance. Likewise, an activated resistor can mimic a linearized BKT plot in a narrow window. These checked counterexamples test logical uniqueness, not the validity of any cited experiment. Heating, current window, finite size and inhomogeneity need independent controls. [R8](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

Reyren's 2007 LaAlO3/SrTiO3 measurements distinguish eight-unit-cell and fifteen-unit-cell LaAlO3 overlayers, with resistance reaching the noise floor below approximately 200 and 100 mK respectively at 100 nA. Those overlayer thicknesses are not measured superconducting-sheet widths. The field-dependent transition uses 50% of the 1 K resistance; extrapolated zero-temperature fields of 65 and 30 mT are therefore criterion-dependent estimates. [R1](#ref-source-ea5d0c80335c450d)

For the eight-unit-cell sample, the current–voltage exponent reaches three near 188 mK and the resistance-tail analysis yields about 190 mK. Figure 4 also shows an ohmic low-current regime attributed to finite size. Agreement between these analyses is informative without eliminating their assumptions. The paper's roughly 10 nm thickness bound relies on an oxygen-defect/carrier-profile scenario and bulk carrier requirements, rather than direct spatial imaging or a unique explanation of carrier origin. [R1](#ref-source-ea5d0c80335c450d)

## Oxide interface controls

The Reyren specimens use TiO2-terminated SrTiO3, pulsed-laser growth and oxygen treatment during cooling. A two-unit-cell reference remains insulating within the reported measurement window. These controls constrain oxygen-vacancy interpretations but do not prove that defects are absent. Later electrostatic gating requires nonlinear capacitance integration and attention to conditioning history; a dome does not establish carrier density as the only variable or identify a unique quantum critical pairing interaction. [R1](#ref-source-ea5d0c80335c450d) [R9](#ref-source-e9e3a49b753191bc)

In Gozar's author manuscript, I denotes insulating La2CuO4, M denotes metallic La1.55Sr0.45CuO4 and S denotes oxygenated superconducting La2CuO4+δ. Reversing I–M to M–I changes the characteristic transition from roughly 15 to 30 K; oxygenating M–I produces M–S near 50 K. The thickness-series figure uses a resistance midpoint. Its separate screening figure reports 33.2 K for S and 51.6 K for M–S, measured with 10 kHz mutual inductance. Screening and transport criteria must remain distinct. [R2](#ref-source-684b96e9dbb65a64)

The layer-thickness and screening-current analyses constrain an interfacial region approximately one to two unit cells thick, subject to their structural and electrodynamic models. Microscopy bounds cation interdiffusion at roughly one unit cell; it does not establish perfectly abrupt chemistry. Logvenov's original abstract describes layer-selective Zn markers that suppress superconductivity and locate the response within a single CuO2 plane. That selected abstract supports the localization statement, while its full methods and calibration remain unchecked here. [R2](#ref-source-684b96e9dbb65a64) [R3](#ref-source-7fcd7faadf66481b)

## FeSe spectra and annealing

He and colleagues' 2012 author version, associated with the 2013 journal article, follows annealing-dependent electronic phases in single-layer FeSe/SrTiO3. Figure 3 extracts gaps from symmetrized energy-distribution curves and compares them with BCS-form temperature fits. Sequence 10 has an approximately 10 meV gap closing around 40 K; sequence 15 reaches roughly 19 meV and 65 ± 5 K. The latter is an ARPES gap scale, not a measured zero-resistance temperature. [R4](#ref-source-a95bcf0cb2681557)

The inferred electron count assumes two degenerate electron sheets, and the observed band evolution is not a simple rigid shift. Annealing may alter selenium or oxygen content and atomic configuration; later annealing also degrades sample quality. The selected author text describes direct single-layer transport and magnetic measurements as still underway. A BCS-shaped fit is compatible with a superconducting interpretation but does not independently demonstrate global phase coherence. [R4](#ref-source-a95bcf0cb2681557)

Lee's later replica-band study supports coupling between FeSe electrons and a substrate-related phonon, while its estimated pairing enhancement depends on the assumed background interaction. Its 58 ± 7 K fitted gap closing belongs to that specimen and analysis, not to He's annealing sequence. Replica bands alone do not partition every contribution to the pairing kernel. See [multiband pairing](/scwiki/multiband-pairing) for the source-specific model limitations. [R5](#ref-source-f9fe6e9bc3792dcc)

## Limits and disputes

A superconducting single layer establishes sufficiency under its preparation and measurement conditions, not that interlayer coupling is universally irrelevant. Interface records should not be merged with bulk, transient or high-pressure records. Complete scientific acceptance remains open: selected original passages and figures, inherited named checks and model arithmetic are documented, while full supplements, final-author comparisons, raw-data reanalysis and independent replication are incomplete. [R1](#ref-source-ea5d0c80335c450d) [R2](#ref-source-684b96e9dbb65a64) [R3](#ref-source-7fcd7faadf66481b) [R4](#ref-source-a95bcf0cb2681557)

## Discovery implications

Separate thickness, termination, oxygen history, strain and electrostatics in a controlled comparison. Report the current and frequency window, temperature criterion, sample variation and structural uncertainty. A useful mechanism should predict which intervention changes a gap and which changes phase stiffness, with observations that can distinguish competing explanations. Keep those outcomes separate in prose, search filters and exported evidence. [R4](#ref-source-a95bcf0cb2681557) [R5](#ref-source-f9fe6e9bc3792dcc) [R8](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7) [R9](#ref-source-e9e3a49b753191bc)

## Related topics

Continue with [BKT transitions](/scwiki/bkt-transition), [transport evidence](/scwiki/zero-resistance), [electrostatic gating](/scwiki/electrostatic-gating), [multiband pairing](/scwiki/multiband-pairing), and [geometric stiffness](/scwiki/geometric-superfluid-weight).

### scwiki-d11-claim-experimental-criteria-3

For the eight-unit-cell sample, the current–voltage exponent reaches three near 188 mK and the resistance-tail analysis yields about 190 mK. Figure 4 also shows an ohmic low-current regime attributed to finite size. Agreement between these analyses is informative without eliminating their assumptions. The paper's roughly 10 nm thickness bound relies on an oxygen-defect/carrier-profile scenario and bulk carrier requirements, rather than direct spatial imaging or a unique explanation of carrier origin.

### scwiki-d11-claim-oxide-interface-controls-1

The Reyren specimens use TiO2-terminated SrTiO3, pulsed-laser growth and oxygen treatment during cooling. A two-unit-cell reference remains insulating within the reported measurement window. These controls constrain oxygen-vacancy interpretations but do not prove that defects are absent. Later electrostatic gating requires nonlinear capacitance integration and attention to conditioning history; a dome does not establish carrier density as the only variable or identify a unique quantum critical pairing interaction.

### scwiki-d11-claim-oxide-interface-controls-2

In Gozar's author manuscript, I denotes insulating La2CuO4, M denotes metallic La1.55Sr0.45CuO4 and S denotes oxygenated superconducting La2CuO4+δ. Reversing I–M to M–I changes the characteristic transition from roughly 15 to 30 K; oxygenating M–I produces M–S near 50 K. The thickness-series figure uses a resistance midpoint. Its separate screening figure reports 33.2 K for S and 51.6 K for M–S, measured with 10 kHz mutual inductance. Screening and transport criteria must remain distinct.

The layer-thickness and screening-current analyses constrain an interfacial region approximately one to two unit cells thick, subject to their structural and electrodynamic models. Microscopy bounds cation interdiffusion at roughly one unit cell; it does not establish perfectly abrupt chemistry. Logvenov's original abstract describes layer-selective Zn markers that suppress superconductivity and locate the response within a single CuO2 plane. That selected abstract supports the localization statement, while its full methods and calibration remain unchecked here.

He and colleagues' 2012 author version, associated with the 2013 journal article, follows annealing-dependent electronic phases in single-layer FeSe/SrTiO3. The inferred electron count assumes two degenerate electron sheets, and the observed band evolution is not a simple rigid shift. Annealing may alter selenium or oxygen content and atomic configuration; later annealing also degrades sample quality. The selected author text describes direct single-layer transport and magnetic measurements as still underway. articles.body:
## Scope

Topological superconductivity concerns the superconducting quasiparticle state, not merely a topological normal-state band next to a superconducting transition. Candidate platforms include intrinsically paired crystals, proximitized surfaces and engineered semiconductor devices. This comparison separates measured superconductivity, a proposed topological phase and evidence for localized Majorana modes. Their criteria and relevant dimensionality differ; a surface result does not automatically classify an entire three-dimensional bulk. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R3](#ref-source-7dc64372df6ba886) [R8](#ref-source-e2865b9f2461bc7f)

For a fully gapped Bogoliubov–de Gennes description, topology depends on dimensionality, symmetries and the occupied quasiparticle states. This restricted framework does not exhaust interacting or nodal superconductivity. A local zero-bias peak is neither a universal requirement for every topological superconductor nor sufficient proof of a Majorana mode. Demonstrating non-Abelian operations is a further question; it is not the definition of every bulk topological superconducting phase. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R4](#ref-source-45c980d0afc5ac14) [R5](#ref-source-87a91e2d8cd79e95) [R11](#ref-source-dca781066e96eecc)

## Mathematical assumptions

One clean single-subband wire model uses $H(k)=\xi_k\tau_z+\alpha k\tau_z\sigma_y+V_Z\sigma_x+\Delta\tau_x$, where $\xi_k=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)-\mu$, $\sigma$ acts on spin and $\tau$ on particle–hole space. Here $\Delta$ is real induced pairing, spin–orbit and Zeeman axes are perpendicular, and $V_Z=|g\mu_B B|/2$ is an energy rather than a magnetic field. With $a=\alpha k$, diagonalization yields $E_\pm^2=\xi_k^2+a^2+V_Z^2+\Delta^2\pm2\sqrt{V_Z^2(\xi_k^2+\Delta^2)+\xi_k^2a^2}$. [R4](#ref-source-45c980d0afc5ac14) [R5](#ref-source-87a91e2d8cd79e95)

The zero-momentum gap closes at $V_Z^2=\mu^2+\Delta^2$. In the stated gapped wire model, the side with $V_Z^2>\mu^2+\Delta^2$ supports the topological phase. The inequality alone is not a material diagnostic: setting spin–orbit coupling to zero can leave finite-momentum gapless excitations even when it holds. Independent checks compare 54 matrix spectra, three closure points and that counterexample. They do not simulate multiband disorder, orbital depairing, interfaces or a complete material invariant. [R4](#ref-source-45c980d0afc5ac14) [R5](#ref-source-87a91e2d8cd79e95)

Fu–Berg supplies a sufficient criterion for fully gapped, time-reversal-invariant odd-parity pairing in an inversion-symmetric weak-pairing setting, using the parity of enclosed time-reversal-invariant momenta. It is not a necessary criterion for every topological superconductor, nor proof that a particular doped crystal realizes odd parity. Fu–Kane's proximitized helical surface is a different construction: its uniform superconducting surface and a vortex carrying a localized mode must be distinguished. [R2](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R3](#ref-source-7dc64372df6ba886)

## Experimental criteria

Hor's Cu-intercalated Bi2Se3 study reports a transition near 3.8 K. In the checked author manuscript, Cu0.12Bi2Se3 has a magnetic response roughly one-fifth of ideal diamagnetism at the lowest accessible temperature, which the authors treat as a lower bound because the transition is incomplete. The resistance does not reach zero. This establishes why sample preparation and connected superconducting paths matter; neither a universal superconducting volume nor topological pairing can be inferred from those numbers alone. [R6](#ref-source-0857b567ea17c2f2)

Butch's YPtBi crystals show a resistive transition near 0.77 K with an AC diamagnetic response. The critical-field curve uses a 50% resistive criterion, with 10–90% bounds, and field perpendicular to [001]. The often-quoted 1.5 T is a zero-temperature extrapolation. Converting it with $B_{c2}=\Phi_0/(2\pi\xi^2)$ gives about 14.8 nm as a consistency estimate. Superconductivity in a candidate topological semimetal does not itself identify its pairing topology or establish a calibrated superconducting volume. [R7](#ref-source-4d53a5f7cdff4a54)

Two iron-chalcogenide papers require separate attribution. sections.markdown:
## Mathematical assumptions

One clean single-subband wire model uses $H(k)=\xi_k\tau_z+\alpha k\tau_z\sigma_y+V_Z\sigma_x+\Delta\tau_x$, where $\xi_k=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)-\mu$, $\sigma$ acts on spin and $\tau$ on particle–hole space. Here $\Delta$ is real induced pairing, spin–orbit and Zeeman axes are perpendicular, and $V_Z=|g\mu_B B|/2$ is an energy rather than a magnetic field. With $a=\alpha k$, diagonalization yields $E_\pm^2=\xi_k^2+a^2+V_Z^2+\Delta^2\pm2\sqrt{V_Z^2(\xi_k^2+\Delta^2)+\xi_k^2a^2}$. [R4](#ref-source-45c980d0afc5ac14) [R5](#ref-source-87a91e2d8cd79e95)

The zero-momentum gap closes at $V_Z^2=\mu^2+\Delta^2$. In the stated gapped wire model, the side with $V_Z^2>\mu^2+\Delta^2$ supports the topological phase. The inequality alone is not a material diagnostic: setting spin–orbit coupling to zero can leave finite-momentum gapless excitations even when it holds. Independent checks compare 54 matrix spectra, three closure points and that counterexample. They do not simulate multiband disorder, orbital depairing, interfaces or a complete material invariant. [R4](#ref-source-45c980d0afc5ac14) [R5](#ref-source-87a91e2d8cd79e95)

Fu–Berg supplies a sufficient criterion for fully gapped, time-reversal-invariant odd-parity pairing in an inversion-symmetric weak-pairing setting, using the parity of enclosed time-reversal-invariant momenta. It is not a necessary criterion for every topological superconductor, nor proof that a particular doped crystal realizes odd parity. Fu–Kane's proximitized helical surface is a different construction: its uniform superconducting surface and a vortex carrying a localized mode must be distinguished. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d12-claim-scope-1

Topological superconductivity concerns the superconducting quasiparticle state, not merely a topological normal-state band next to a superconducting transition. Candidate platforms include intrinsically paired crystals, proximitized surfaces and engineered semiconductor devices. This comparison separates measured superconductivity, a proposed topological phase and evidence for localized Majorana modes. Their criteria and relevant dimensionality differ; a surface result does not automatically classify an entire three-dimensional bulk.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-37986d2488e4cace, source-4e92d11d59fb3441, source-7dc64372df6ba886, source-e2865b9f2461bc7f.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-scope-2

For a fully gapped Bogoliubov–de Gennes description, topology depends on dimensionality, symmetries and the occupied quasiparticle states. This restricted framework does not exhaust interacting or nodal superconductivity. A local zero-bias peak is neither a universal requirement for every topological superconductor nor sufficient proof of a Majorana mode. Demonstrating non-Abelian operations is a further question; it is not the definition of every bulk topological superconducting phase.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-37986d2488e4cace, source-45c980d0afc5ac14, source-87a91e2d8cd79e95, source-dca781066e96eecc.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

One clean single-subband wire model uses $H(k)=\xi_k\tau_z+\alpha k\tau_z\sigma_y+V_Z\sigma_x+\Delta\tau_x$, where $\xi_k=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)-\mu$, $\sigma$ acts on spin and $\tau$ on particle–hole space. Here $\Delta$ is real induced pairing, spin–orbit and Zeeman axes are perpendicular, and $V_Z=|g\mu_B B|/2$ is an energy rather than a magnetic field. With $a=\alpha k$, diagonalization yields $E_\pm^2=\xi_k^2+a^2+V_Z^2+\Delta^2\pm2\sqrt{V_Z^2(\xi_k^2+\Delta^2)+\xi_k^2a^2}$.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-45c980d0afc5ac14, source-87a91e2d8cd79e95.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

The zero-momentum gap closes at $V_Z^2=\mu^2+\Delta^2$. In the stated gapped wire model, the side with $V_Z^2>\mu^2+\Delta^2$ supports the topological phase. The inequality alone is not a material diagnostic: setting spin–orbit coupling to zero can leave finite-momentum gapless excitations even when it holds. Independent checks compare 54 matrix spectra, three closure points and that counterexample. They do not simulate multiband disorder, orbital depairing, interfaces or a complete material invariant.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-45c980d0afc5ac14, source-87a91e2d8cd79e95.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

Fu–Berg supplies a sufficient criterion for fully gapped, time-reversal-invariant odd-parity pairing in an inversion-symmetric weak-pairing setting, using the parity of enclosed time-reversal-invariant momenta. It is not a necessary criterion for every topological superconductor, nor proof that a particular doped crystal realizes odd parity. Fu–Kane's proximitized helical surface is a different construction: its uniform superconducting surface and a vortex carrying a localized mode must be distinguished.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-4e92d11d59fb3441, source-7dc64372df6ba886.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-1

Hor's Cu-intercalated Bi2Se3 study reports a transition near 3.8 K. In the checked author manuscript, Cu0.12Bi2Se3 has a magnetic response roughly one-fifth of ideal diamagnetism at the lowest accessible temperature, which the authors treat as a lower bound because the transition is incomplete. The resistance does not reach zero. This establishes why sample preparation and connected superconducting paths matter; neither a universal superconducting volume nor topological pairing can be inferred from those numbers alone.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-0857b567ea17c2f2.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Butch's YPtBi crystals show a resistive transition near 0.77 K with an AC diamagnetic response. The critical-field curve uses a 50% resistive criterion, with 10–90% bounds, and field perpendicular to [001]. The often-quoted 1.5 T is a zero-temperature extrapolation. Converting it with $B_{c2}=\Phi_0/(2\pi\xi^2)$ gives about 14.8 nm as a consistency estimate. Superconductivity in a candidate topological semimetal does not itself identify its pairing topology or establish a calibrated superconducting volume.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-4d53a5f7cdff4a54.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary text/figures and restricted model checks; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Two iron-chalcogenide papers require separate attribution. Zhang's ARPES study resolves a spin-helical surface band and a superconducting surface gap around 1.8 meV, interpreted as surface topological superconductivity. Its low-temperature measurement at 2.4 K is not the reported 14.5 K transition temperature. The study's surface interpretation must not be replaced by a statement that all bulk pairing is topological. In its angular-gap figure, hollow mirrored markers are not additional independent measurements.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-e2865b9f2461bc7f.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-4

Wang's distinct vortex-STM paper studies FeTe0.55Se0.45. Figure 2 spectra at 0.55 K and 0.5 T parallel to c are normalized by integrated spectral area; they cannot be read as an absolute quantized conductance plateau. The approximately 0.3 meV peak width contains instrumental and thermal broadening. Barrier and temperature scans elsewhere use different fields. The zero-energy signal is interpreted as Majorana evidence, while the displayed braiding sequence is a proposal, not a performed operation.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-5

Xu's Bi2Te3/NbSe2 heterostructure study compares vortex spectra across film thicknesses. The checked 2013 author version underlying the 2015 publication distinguishes where split peaks become experimentally resolvable from the extrapolated origin of their splitting. The former is around 20 nm even for thinner films; the latter changes near four quintuple layers and supports the authors' Majorana interpretation. Treating every unsplit interval as a directly measured Majorana radius would discard both the extrapolation and approximately 0.2 meV resolution.

### scwiki-d12-claim-experimental-criteria-6

Semiconductor readout advances also need their own evidence category. Aghaee's 2025 InAs–Al experiment measures single-shot parity interferometrically and explicitly retains an Andreev-state alternative. Van Loo's 2026 work demonstrates parity readout in a minimal Kitaev-chain device, with a two-site rather than asymptotically long-chain model. These are useful experimental capabilities; neither result, as scoped here, establishes braiding or fault-tolerant topological computation. Readout performance, spatial nonlocality and a protected bulk phase remain distinct questions.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-e3824a8727c3ec54, source-a3c2dc153700478a.

### scwiki-d12-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Confinement, disorder and ordinary Andreev states can produce misleading local zero-bias signatures. Even apparent agreement with an ideal conductance value needs temperature, barrier, calibration and nonlocal checks. The 2018 paper *Quantized Majorana conductance* was retracted in 2021; its original result is retained here only as retracted history. The notice describes charge-jump corrections, an axis-label problem and conductance recalibration. A withdrawn claim cannot count as independent confirmation of later devices.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-dca781066e96eecc, source-6a7f18eec743e89d, source-f127bb2d99183698.

Conditions: Separate bulk, surface, wire and device claims; preserve composition, field, temperature, resolution, transport criterion and publication/retraction status.

### scwiki-d12-claim-discovery-implications-1

Specify the target first: bulk odd-parity superconductivity, a proximitized topological surface, a wire end state or a controllable parity device. Then record composition, geometry, temperature, field, superconducting criterion and competing-state tests for that target. Compare complementary probes on characterized samples and preserve failures and retractions. Strong spin–orbit coupling or an attractive band calculation can motivate an experiment, but cannot replace identification of the actual paired phase and its protected observables.

A 10 July 2026 preprint by Zatelli and colleagues reports coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains. claims.statement: Ising protection refers to the influence of spin–orbit coupling on the response of Cooper pairs to an applied field. It does not mean that every paired state is purely singlet, or that a large in-plane critical field proves triplet pairing. Broken inversion can admit mixed components, while additional Fermi pockets, interlayer coupling, scattering and geometry change the interpretation. Topological superconductivity is a further classification, not a synonym for strong spin–orbit coupling.

Its eigenvalues are $\pm\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$. On the positive branch the spin directions are $\mathbf n_\eta=(b,0,\eta\lambda)/\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$: opposite out-of-plane components persist while the field cants both spins in-plane. This two-level model omits momentum-dependent bands, Rashba terms and other pockets.

articles.body:
## Scope

Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide superconductivity includes gate-doped semiconductors such as MoS2 and WS2, as well as intrinsically metallic NbSe2 and TaS2. They should not all be described as semiconductors or assigned one pairing mechanism. Atomic thickness, the thickness of an accumulated conducting layer and the dimensionality relevant to superconducting coherence are also different properties. Preserve polytype, substrate, layer count and preparation before comparing experiments. [R1](#ref-source-e8b9a66d143832fb) [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8) [R7](#ref-source-03aca3bf939d3e53) [R8](#ref-source-8fbffce60f5c5245)

Ising protection refers to the influence of spin–orbit coupling on the response of Cooper pairs to an applied field. It does not mean that every paired state is purely singlet, or that a large in-plane critical field proves triplet pairing. Broken inversion can admit mixed components, while additional Fermi pockets, interlayer coupling, scattering and geometry change the interpretation. Topological superconductivity is a further classification, not a synonym for strong spin–orbit coupling. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R4](#ref-source-c80fb39cdf748a83) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

## Mathematical assumptions

A restricted normal-state illustration uses $H_\eta=\eta\lambda\sigma_z+b\sigma_x$, where $\eta=\pm1$ labels opposite valleys, $\sigma$ acts on spin, $\lambda$ is an Ising spin–orbit energy and $b$ an in-plane Zeeman energy. Its eigenvalues are $\pm\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$. On the positive branch the spin directions are $\mathbf n_\eta=(b,0,\eta\lambda)/\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$: opposite out-of-plane components persist while the field cants both spins in-plane. This two-level model omits momentum-dependent bands, Rashba terms and other pockets. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

For corresponding spinors, $|u_+^T i\sigma_yu_-|^2=\lambda^2/(\lambda^2+b^2)$ is the squared singlet pairing matrix element. It is twice the singlet probability of the normalized tensor-product state, so those quantities must not be confused. Twelve independent diagonalizations check this distinction and spin orientations. This normal-state calculation neither solves a superconducting gap equation nor establishes singlet dominance, a critical field or a material pairing mechanism. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

The weak-coupling reference $B_P=\Delta_0/(\sqrt2\mu_B)\simeq1.86\,T_c$ uses tesla for field and kelvin for temperature, with $g=2$, negligible spin–orbit effects and $\Delta_0\simeq1.764k_BT_c$. This is a paramagnetic benchmark, not a universal upper bound including orbital effects. Similarly, the BKT transport signature $V\propto I^3$ has a restricted dynamical regime; finite size, heating and inhomogeneity can invalidate a naive exponent-only diagnosis. Neither comparison identifies the pairing interaction. [R11](#ref-source-d32df19524b2a1c8) [R12](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

## Experimental criteria

Ye's MoS2 study established a gate-controlled superconducting dome in a band insulator. Lu's later Ising study illustrates why the chosen threshold matters: its checked author manuscript uses 90% of normal resistance for the phase diagram and 50% elsewhere. Those temperatures cannot be silently substituted for one another, for a measured zero-resistance temperature or for a fitted BKT temperature. The dome itself is not evidence selecting a unique pairing mechanism. [R1](#ref-source-e8b9a66d143832fb) [R2](#ref-source-cba51ab2111ccf0a)

Saito's high-field MoS2 device gives a particularly clear warning. Its reported transition near 6.5 K and in-plane critical field near 52 T at 1.5 K use a 75%-of-normal-resistance criterion; that device did not reach zero resistance. The separate low-field sample's 9.7 K transition uses 50%. The 55 T pulsed-field ceiling is not identical to the extracted 52 T boundary. The experiment and band calculations support spin–valley protection, while neither these criteria nor the measurement temperature establish triplet order. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e)

Costanzo's atomically thin MoS2 experiments demonstrate a monolayer resistance drop to the measured zero level, but only one contact pair in the illustrated device shows it. Other monolayers show no transition down to the 1.5 K base temperature. Different contact regions reveal substantial density variation, associated with frozen-liquid detachment. A tendency toward weaker monolayer superconductivity in this set of devices is therefore not a universal prohibition on strong two-dimensional pairing. The critical-field comparison uses half the normal resistance. [R7](#ref-source-03aca3bf939d3e53)

In NbSe2, Xi's Ising paper extracts an Aslamazov–Larkin fit scale close to half the normal resistance; its current-excitation BKT estimate lies closer to the one-percent criterion. The roughly 3 K monolayer fit scale must not be relabelled as a direct BKT temperature. The paper considers reduced interlayer pairing and argues that the competing CDW effect on this trend is likely weak. That interpretation differs from asserting that enhanced CDW necessarily causes the superconducting suppression. [R4](#ref-source-c80fb39cdf748a83)

The frequently quoted monolayer CDW scale of $145\pm3$ K comes from a separate Xi Raman/transport paper. The selected analysis follows a CDW amplitude mode and extrapolates its intensity to zero, with mean-field fits used as guides. This is neither a superconducting transition nor an independent direct measurement of the pairing interaction. Contrasting thickness trends of CDW and superconductivity motivate competing-order tests; a correlation alone does not determine their causal coupling. [R5](#ref-source-43488891372a9f8e)

De la Barrera compares metallic 2H-TaS2 and NbSe2 down to atomic thickness. The resistive curves use 50% criteria; the reported monolayer TaS2 boundary remains above the 34.5 T instrument limit below 2 K. A 65.6 T coefficient fitted near the transition is not a measured zero-temperature critical field. Even-layer enhancement also survives despite restored inversion symmetry, emphasizing the balance of interlayer and spin–orbit coupling. Encapsulation, aging and distinct thickness trends remain part of the sample record. [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

Lu's CVD monolayer WS2 dome uses an effective gate coordinate assembled from ionic-gate states and back-gate sweeps. It is not a directly applied kilovolt voltage across the ionic liquid, and Hall carrier density is nonmonotonic across the dome. The high-field study uses a separate sample B, whose optimal 50%-resistance transition is 3.15 K. Its low-edge 1.54 K state changes by only 0.08 K at 35 T. Neither number supplies a universal WS2 transition or proves that all tungsten dichalcogenides behave alike. [R8](#ref-source-8fbffce60f5c5245)

## Limits and disputes

Sajadi's monolayer WTe2 device connects gate-controlled superconductivity with a quantum-spin-Hall material platform, while retaining resistance thresholds and a finite measurement floor. Qi's pressure-dependent MoTe2 study instead follows bulk structural regimes, including low-pressure Td and high-pressure 1T-prime behavior. These are distinct geometries and phases. A topological normal-state description plus superconductivity is a reason to investigate the paired state, not sufficient demonstration of a topological superconducting gap or Majorana modes. [R9](#ref-source-e8160470a5b03301) [R10](#ref-source-9ec8f69fb4323ea6)

A September 2026 theory by Marini, Cudazzo and Calandra attributes gated-TMD domes to ionic disorder, reduced screening and enhanced Coulomb repulsion, comparing its calculations with experiment. This is a model explanation, not a new experimental transition or universal proof about every superconducting dome. Complete scientific acceptance remains open here: its full equations, other cited final-version comparisons, supplements, chemical controls and raw-data analyses are unfinished. The present checks are restricted to the named primary passages, figures and spinor model. [R1](#ref-source-e8b9a66d143832fb) [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R5](#ref-source-43488891372a9f8e) [R7](#ref-source-03aca3bf939d3e53) [R8](#ref-source-8fbffce60f5c5245) [R13](#ref-source-55a6c270d113228e)

## Discovery implications

Treat the device as part of the material: record layer count, polytype, contacts, electrolyte, gating temperature, voltage history and field orientation. Compare onset, midpoint, measured zero, phase-ordering and spectroscopic scales separately. Establish whether charge tuning also changes disorder or chemistry, and test proposed spin protection against the actual bands and geometry. The strongest next experiment distinguishes competing explanations on characterized devices instead of ranking isolated critical-field or transition-temperature numbers. [R2](#ref-source-cba51ab2111ccf0a) [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8) [R7](#ref-source-03aca3bf939d3e53) [R8](#ref-source-8fbffce60f5c5245) [R12](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

## Related topics

[Electrostatic gating](/scwiki/electrostatic-gating), [Pauli limit](/scwiki/pauli-limit), [Spin–orbit coupling](/scwiki/spin-orbit-coupling), [BKT transitions](/scwiki/bkt-transition), and [Topological candidates](/scwiki/topological-superconductor-candidates).

## Mathematical assumptions

A restricted normal-state illustration uses $H_\eta=\eta\lambda\sigma_z+b\sigma_x$, where $\eta=\pm1$ labels opposite valleys, $\sigma$ acts on spin, $\lambda$ is an Ising spin–orbit energy and $b$ an in-plane Zeeman energy. Its eigenvalues are $\pm\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$. On the positive branch the spin directions are $\mathbf n_\eta=(b,0,\eta\lambda)/\sqrt{\lambda^2+b^2}$: opposite out-of-plane components persist while the field cants both spins in-plane. This two-level model omits momentum-dependent bands, Rashba terms and other pockets. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

For corresponding spinors, $|u_+^T i\sigma_yu_-|^2=\lambda^2/(\lambda^2+b^2)$ is the squared singlet pairing matrix element. It is twice the singlet probability of the normalized tensor-product state, so those quantities must not be confused. Twelve independent diagonalizations check this distinction and spin orientations. This normal-state calculation neither solves a superconducting gap equation nor establishes singlet dominance, a critical field or a material pairing mechanism. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e) [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

The weak-coupling reference $B_P=\Delta_0/(\sqrt2\mu_B)\simeq1.86\,T_c$ uses tesla for field and kelvin for temperature, with $g=2$, negligible spin–orbit effects and $\Delta_0\simeq1.764k_BT_c$. This is a paramagnetic benchmark, not a universal upper bound including orbital effects. Similarly, the BKT transport signature $V\propto I^3$ has a restricted dynamical regime; finite size, heating and inhomogeneity can invalidate a naive exponent-only diagnosis. Neither comparison identifies the pairing interaction. [R11](#ref-source-d32df19524b2a1c8) [R12](#ref-source-1ebdfccc067bc6a7)

## Experimental criteria

Ye's MoS2 study established a gate-controlled superconducting dome in a band insulator. Lu's later Ising study illustrates why the chosen threshold matters: its checked author manuscript uses 90% of normal resistance for the phase diagram and 50% elsewhere. Those temperatures cannot be silently substituted for one another, for a measured zero-resistance temperature or for a fitted BKT temperature. The dome itself is not evidence selecting a unique pairing mechanism. [R1](#ref-source-e8b9a66d143832fb) [R2](#ref-source-cba51ab2111ccf0a)

Saito's high-field MoS2 device gives a particularly clear warning. Its reported transition near 6.5 K and in-plane critical field near 52 T at 1.5 K use a 75%-of-normal-resistance criterion; that device did not reach zero resistance. The separate low-field sample's 9.7 K transition uses 50%. The 55 T pulsed-field ceiling is not identical to the extracted 52 T boundary. The experiment and band calculations support spin–valley protection, while neither these criteria nor the measurement temperature establish triplet order. [R3](#ref-source-ec4b77f9e011c26e)

Costanzo's atomically thin MoS2 experiments demonstrate a monolayer resistance drop to the measured zero level, but only one contact pair in the illustrated device shows it. Other monolayers show no transition down to the 1.5 K base temperature. Different contact regions reveal substantial density variation, associated with frozen-liquid detachment. A tendency toward weaker monolayer superconductivity in this set of devices is therefore not a universal prohibition on strong two-dimensional pairing. The critical-field comparison uses half the normal resistance. [R7](#ref-source-03aca3bf939d3e53)

In NbSe2, Xi's Ising paper extracts an Aslamazov–Larkin fit scale close to half the normal resistance; its current-excitation BKT estimate lies closer to the one-percent criterion. The roughly 3 K monolayer fit scale must not be relabelled as a direct BKT temperature. The paper considers reduced interlayer pairing and argues that the competing CDW effect on this trend is likely weak. That interpretation differs from asserting that enhanced CDW necessarily causes the superconducting suppression. [R4](#ref-source-c80fb39cdf748a83)

The frequently quoted monolayer CDW scale of $145\pm3$ K comes from a separate Xi Raman/transport paper. The selected analysis follows a CDW amplitude mode and extrapolates its intensity to zero, with mean-field fits used as guides. This is neither a superconducting transition nor an independent direct measurement of the pairing interaction. Contrasting thickness trends of CDW and superconductivity motivate competing-order tests; a correlation alone does not determine their causal coupling. [R5](#ref-source-43488891372a9f8e)

De la Barrera compares metallic 2H-TaS2 and NbSe2 down to atomic thickness. The resistive curves use 50% criteria; the reported monolayer TaS2 boundary remains above the 34.5 T instrument limit below 2 K. A 65.6 T coefficient fitted near the transition is not a measured zero-temperature critical field. Even-layer enhancement also survives despite restored inversion symmetry, emphasizing the balance of interlayer and spin–orbit coupling. Encapsulation, aging and distinct thickness trends remain part of the sample record. [R6](#ref-source-804e0c9690bde4d8)

Lu's CVD monolayer WS2 dome uses an effective gate coordinate assembled from ionic-gate states and back-gate sweeps. It is not a directly applied kilovolt voltage across the ionic liquid, and Hall carrier density is nonmonotonic across the dome. The high-field study uses a separate sample B, whose optimal 50%-resistance transition is 3.15 K. Its low-edge 1.54 K state changes by only 0.08 K at 35 T. Neither number supplies a universal WS2 transition or proves that all tungsten dichalcogenides behave alike. [R8](#ref-source-8fbffce60f5c5245)

## Limits and disputes

Sajadi's monolayer WTe2 device connects gate-controlled superconductivity with a quantum-spin-Hall material platform, while retaining resistance thresholds and a finite measurement floor. Qi's pressure-dependent MoTe2 study instead follows bulk structural regimes, including low-pressure Td and high-pressure 1T-prime behavior. These are distinct geometries and phases. A topological normal-state description plus superconductivity is a reason to investigate the paired state, not sufficient demonstration of a topological superconducting gap or Majorana modes. [R9](#ref-source-e8160470a5b03301) [R10](#ref-source-9ec8f69fb4323ea6)

A September 2026 theory by Marini, Cudazzo and Calandra attributes gated-TMD domes to ionic disorder, reduced screening and enhanced Coulomb repulsion, comparing its calculations with experiment. This is a model explanation, not a new experimental transition or universal proof about every superconducting dome. Complete scientific acceptance remains open here: its full equations, other cited final-version comparisons, supplements, chemical controls and raw-data analyses are unfinished. The present checks are restricted to the named primary passages, figures and spinor model. ## Discovery implications

Treat the device as part of the material: record layer count, polytype, contacts, electrolyte, gating temperature, voltage history and field orientation. Compare onset, midpoint, measured zero, phase-ordering and spectroscopic scales separately. Establish whether charge tuning also changes disorder or chemistry, and test proposed spin protection against the actual bands and geometry. The strongest next experiment distinguishes competing explanations on characterized devices instead of ranking isolated critical-field or transition-temperature numbers. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d13-claim-scope-1

Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenide superconductivity includes gate-doped semiconductors such as MoS2 and WS2, as well as intrinsically metallic NbSe2 and TaS2. They should not all be described as semiconductors or assigned one pairing mechanism. Atomic thickness, the thickness of an accumulated conducting layer and the dimensionality relevant to superconducting coherence are also different properties. Preserve polytype, substrate, layer count and preparation before comparing experiments.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-e8b9a66d143832fb, source-ec4b77f9e011c26e, source-804e0c9690bde4d8, source-03aca3bf939d3e53, source-8fbffce60f5c5245.

### scwiki-d13-claim-scope-2

Topological superconductivity is a further classification, not a synonym for strong spin–orbit coupling.

articles.body:
## Scope

Kagome geometry offers a useful starting point for studying flat bands, Dirac crossings, charge order and superconductivity. It does not guarantee that a flat band lies at the Fermi energy, that magnetic frustration produces a spin liquid, or that a material has a high transition temperature. This article separates superconducting AV3Sb5 compounds, pressure-induced superconductivity in CsCr3Sb5 and charge-ordered comparison materials. Normal-state topology and superconducting topology remain separate questions. [R1](#ref-source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1) [R2](#ref-source-96cec6968d3c379a) [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R14](#ref-source-d0ee5c328ca326ee) [R16](#ref-source-e9b1bdb7cb3c0ee4) [R17](#ref-source-ed0ebd2f956f2b5f)

## Mathematical assumptions

Take one spinless orbital on each of three sites $0,\mathbf a_1/2,\mathbf a_2/2$, with triangular Bravais vectors and $q_i=\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a_i$. For positive nearest-neighbor hopping $t$, a Bloch Hamiltonian is $H=-2t\begin{pmatrix}0&c_1&c_2\\c_1&0&c_3\\c_2&c_3&0\end{pmatrix}$, where $c_1=\cos(q_1/2)$, $c_2=\cos(q_2/2)$ and $c_3=\cos[(q_2-q_1)/2]$. Its bands are $E_f=2t$ and $E_\pm=t[-1\pm\sqrt{4S-3}]$, with $S=c_1^2+c_2^2+c_3^2$. The vectors in Guo and Franz's convention are nearest-neighbor vectors, half the Bravais vectors used here. [R1](#ref-source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1)

The model has a flat-band contact at Gamma, a Dirac crossing at K and dispersive-band saddles at M. Independent diagonalization checks 1,311 momentum/hopping combinations; numerical Hessians have opposite-sign curvatures at the two M-point saddles. Adding equal same-sublattice hopping shifts all bands by $\delta(\mathbf q)=-2u[\cos q_1+\cos q_2+\cos(q_2-q_1)]$. The formerly flat branch then spans $9|u|$ between Gamma and K while the kagome geometry remains. These checks illustrate model sensitivity; they do not calculate a pairing interaction, a material transition temperature or a superconducting invariant. [R1](#ref-source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1)

Real compounds add orbital character, spin–orbit coupling, interlayer hopping and reconstruction. Kang's ARPES/DFT work distinguishes van Hove features with predominantly pure or mixed sublattice content near the Fermi energy of CsV3Sb5. Such information constrains low-energy models; a large density of states alone does not select a pairing symmetry. The presently checked author abstract is not a reproduction of the full spectral assignment or pairing calculation. [R8](#ref-source-dbcbd572b05dcaa4)

## Experimental criteria

Ortiz's original family study identified K, Rb and Cs vanadium antimonides as layered kagome metals. The later CsV3Sb5 superconductivity paper combines magnetization, resistivity and heat capacity around a 2.5 K onset. Its transport onset is suppressed at an 8 mA probe current and returns toward the nominal value at lower current, illustrating why excitation belongs in the sample record. The heat-capacity temperature floor limits conclusions about the low-temperature gap. Subsequent K and Rb member reports should retain their own samples and criteria rather than being collapsed into a universal family transition range. [R2](#ref-source-96cec6968d3c379a) [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R4](#ref-source-1dbc07dbbbe19132) [R5](#ref-source-4027fb28ea284a9f)

The same CsV3Sb5 work discusses a much higher-temperature anomaly and a normal-state topological band background. ARPES taken well above the superconducting transition and calculated surface states above the Fermi energy do not directly measure a superconducting gap invariant. Liang's three-dimensional CDW study and Li's conjoined-CDW study further emphasize stacking, temperature and surface dependence. Different modulation descriptions cannot be merged into one structure common to every sample or termination. [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R6](#ref-source-7746049011a0e640) [R7](#ref-source-80eda571fc6d710c)

Yang reports anomalous Hall response in KV3Sb5; Yu connects anomalous Hall response in CsV3Sb5 to its higher-temperature charge-order regime. Neither result is a phase-sensitive measurement of superconducting chirality. Ordinary multiband transport, scattering and Berry-curvature contributions require separate analysis. Likewise, the checked Mielke muon study concerns time-reversal symmetry breaking associated with charge order. A signal emerging near that ordering scale cannot simply be reassigned to a superconducting $d+id$ state. [R9](#ref-source-646e363b41fcabb3) [R10](#ref-source-59d803435c0df1ef) [R11](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3)

Chen's spatially resolved tunneling work proposes a roton pair-density-wave interpretation in CsV3Sb5. Pair-related modulations are significant evidence to investigate, but charge-order changes in local density of states, tunneling matrix elements and Josephson coupling remain relevant controls. Pressure studies also show nonmonotonic superconducting and charge-order scales. Two domes do not by themselves establish two pairing mechanisms: structure, bands, scattering and calibration can evolve together. [R12](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961) [R13](#ref-source-4fb5d6fb51bdb253)

For CsCr3Sb5, Liu's author manuscript and selected final-paper results report a maximum resistive onset of 6.4 K at 4.2 GPa, with zero resistance and AC susceptibility supporting bulk superconductivity over a pressure interval. Its critical-field curves instead use half the normal resistance. The fitted zero-temperature field is therefore not an independently observed field boundary. The final text explicitly leaves the field direction uncertain, preventing an anisotropy claim. The cubic-anvil measurement uses glycerol and room-temperature load calibration; the lower-pressure piston-cell setup uses a different medium and calibration. These are high-pressure records, not ambient-pressure entries or universal chromium-family numbers. [R14](#ref-source-d0ee5c328ca326ee)

Cheng's April 2026 paper adds a distinct charge-order result in CsCr3Sb5. The selected author text describes cleaved-surface STM with a 4.5 K base temperature and two higher-temperature modulation scales. Its stripe pattern breaks mirror symmetries while retaining a mirror-glide operation; opposite local textures do not define global handedness. Those surface images are not a high-pressure superconducting order-parameter measurement and cannot establish chiral superconductivity. [R15](#ref-source-c415e45e91e02c10)

FeGe and ScV6Sn6 serve as comparisons. Yin's FeGe study reports charge order, magnetic stacking and an edge state within a charge-order energy gap; Arachchige's ScV6Sn6 work reports a lattice-modulated charge-order transition. Neither cited result establishes superconductivity. Absence of such evidence in these papers should not be rewritten as a timeless claim that either material can never superconduct under any preparation or pressure. [R16](#ref-source-e9b1bdb7cb3c0ee4) [R17](#ref-source-ed0ebd2f956f2b5f)

## Limits and disputes

Allowed pairing representations are candidates until tested against the actual superconducting state. Charge-order time-reversal breaking, a normal-state anomalous Hall signal, structural handedness, tunneling modulation and a zero-bias feature each address different questions. Phase-sensitive experiments, temperature-resolved symmetry probes, bulk gap constraints and boundary-state tests can provide complementary discrimination; they are not a universal checklist that defines every possible topological superconductor. Complete scientific acceptance remains open: several references retain abstract-only review, and final-version comparisons, supplements and raw-data analyses are unfinished. [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R7](#ref-source-80eda571fc6d710c) [R10](#ref-source-59d803435c0df1ef) [R11](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3) [R12](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961) [R15](#ref-source-c415e45e91e02c10)

## Discovery implications

Record composition, pressure path, excitation, surface termination and the onset, midpoint, measured-zero and thermodynamic criteria separately. Compare measured band positions with a specified model before invoking flat-band enhancement. Test whether changing charge order also changes disorder, structure or carrier balance. The useful next experiment resolves competing interpretations on a characterized sample, rather than promoting a geometric label or an isolated transition number into a mechanism. [R1](#ref-source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1) [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R8](#ref-source-dbcbd572b05dcaa4) [R13](#ref-source-4fb5d6fb51bdb253) [R14](#ref-source-d0ee5c328ca326ee)

## Related topics

[Flat bands](/scwiki/flat-band-pairing), [Charge density waves](/scwiki/charge-density-waves), [Chiral pairing](/scwiki/chiral-pairing), [Pair density waves](/scwiki/pair-density-wave), and [Pressure tuning](/scwiki/pressure-tuning).

sections.markdown:
## Experimental criteria

Ortiz's original family study identified K, Rb and Cs vanadium antimonides as layered kagome metals. The later CsV3Sb5 superconductivity paper combines magnetization, resistivity and heat capacity around a 2.5 K onset. Its transport onset is suppressed at an 8 mA probe current and returns toward the nominal value at lower current, illustrating why excitation belongs in the sample record. The heat-capacity temperature floor limits conclusions about the low-temperature gap. Subsequent K and Rb member reports should retain their own samples and criteria rather than being collapsed into a universal family transition range. [R2](#ref-source-96cec6968d3c379a) [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R4](#ref-source-1dbc07dbbbe19132) [R5](#ref-source-4027fb28ea284a9f)

The same CsV3Sb5 work discusses a much higher-temperature anomaly and a normal-state topological band background. ARPES taken well above the superconducting transition and calculated surface states above the Fermi energy do not directly measure a superconducting gap invariant. Liang's three-dimensional CDW study and Li's conjoined-CDW study further emphasize stacking, temperature and surface dependence. Different modulation descriptions cannot be merged into one structure common to every sample or termination. [R3](#ref-source-d49026ec4f5a10a4) [R6](#ref-source-7746049011a0e640) [R7](#ref-source-80eda571fc6d710c)

Yang reports anomalous Hall response in KV3Sb5; Yu connects anomalous Hall response in CsV3Sb5 to its higher-temperature charge-order regime. Neither result is a phase-sensitive measurement of superconducting chirality. Ordinary multiband transport, scattering and Berry-curvature contributions require separate analysis. Likewise, the checked Mielke muon study concerns time-reversal symmetry breaking associated with charge order. A signal emerging near that ordering scale cannot simply be reassigned to a superconducting $d+id$ state. [R9](#ref-source-646e363b41fcabb3) [R10](#ref-source-59d803435c0df1ef) [R11](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3)

Chen's spatially resolved tunneling work proposes a roton pair-density-wave interpretation in CsV3Sb5. Pair-related modulations are significant evidence to investigate, but charge-order changes in local density of states, tunneling matrix elements and Josephson coupling remain relevant controls. Pressure studies also show nonmonotonic superconducting and charge-order scales. Two domes do not by themselves establish two pairing mechanisms: structure, bands, scattering and calibration can evolve together. [R12](#ref-source-057c43c86174f961) [R13](#ref-source-4fb5d6fb51bdb253)

For CsCr3Sb5, Liu's author manuscript and selected final-paper results report a maximum resistive onset of 6.4 K at 4.2 GPa, with zero resistance and AC susceptibility supporting bulk superconductivity over a pressure interval. Its critical-field curves instead use half the normal resistance. The fitted zero-temperature field is therefore not an independently observed field boundary. The final text explicitly leaves the field direction uncertain, preventing an anisotropy claim. The cubic-anvil measurement uses glycerol and room-temperature load calibration; the lower-pressure piston-cell setup uses a different medium and calibration. These are high-pressure records, not ambient-pressure entries or universal chromium-family numbers. [R14](#ref-source-d0ee5c328ca326ee)

Cheng's April 2026 paper adds a distinct charge-order result in CsCr3Sb5. The selected author text describes cleaved-surface STM with a 4.5 K base temperature and two higher-temperature modulation scales. Its stripe pattern breaks mirror symmetries while retaining a mirror-glide operation; opposite local textures do not define global handedness. Those surface images are not a high-pressure superconducting order-parameter measurement and cannot establish chiral superconductivity. [R15](#ref-source-c415e45e91e02c10)

FeGe and ScV6Sn6 serve as comparisons. Yin's FeGe study reports charge order, magnetic stacking and an edge state within a charge-order energy gap; Arachchige's ScV6Sn6 work reports a lattice-modulated charge-order transition. Neither cited result establishes superconductivity. Absence of such evidence in these papers should not be rewritten as a timeless claim that either material can never superconduct under any preparation or pressure. [R16](#ref-source-e9b1bdb7cb3c0ee4) [R17](#ref-source-ed0ebd2f956f2b5f)

sections.markdown:
## Limits and disputes

Allowed pairing representations are candidates until tested against the actual superconducting state. Charge-order time-reversal breaking, a normal-state anomalous Hall signal, structural handedness, tunneling modulation and a zero-bias feature each address different questions. Phase-sensitive experiments, temperature-resolved symmetry probes, bulk gap constraints and boundary-state tests can provide complementary discrimination; they are not a universal checklist that defines every possible topological superconductor. Complete scientific acceptance remains open: several references retain abstract-only review, and final-version comparisons, supplements and raw-data analyses are unfinished. Compare measured band positions with a specified model before invoking flat-band enhancement. Test whether changing charge order also changes disorder, structure or carrier balance. ### scwiki-d14-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

Take one spinless orbital on each of three sites $0,\mathbf a_1/2,\mathbf a_2/2$, with triangular Bravais vectors and $q_i=\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a_i$. For positive nearest-neighbor hopping $t$, a Bloch Hamiltonian is $H=-2t\begin{pmatrix}0&c_1&c_2\\c_1&0&c_3\\c_2&c_3&0\end{pmatrix}$, where $c_1=\cos(q_1/2)$, $c_2=\cos(q_2/2)$ and $c_3=\cos[(q_2-q_1)/2]$. Its bands are $E_f=2t$ and $E_\pm=t[-1\pm\sqrt{4S-3}]$, with $S=c_1^2+c_2^2+c_3^2$. The vectors in Guo and Franz's convention are nearest-neighbor vectors, half the Bravais vectors used here.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1.

Conditions: Keep composition, pressure, current, surface termination, temperature type and transition criterion separate. Normal-state geometry/order is not superconducting topology.

### scwiki-d14-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

The model has a flat-band contact at Gamma, a Dirac crossing at K and dispersive-band saddles at M. Independent diagonalization checks 1,311 momentum/hopping combinations; numerical Hessians have opposite-sign curvatures at the two M-point saddles. Adding equal same-sublattice hopping shifts all bands by $\delta(\mathbf q)=-2u[\cos q_1+\cos q_2+\cos(q_2-q_1)]$. The formerly flat branch then spans $9|u|$ between Gamma and K while the kagome geometry remains. These checks illustrate model sensitivity; they do not calculate a pairing interaction, a material transition temperature or a superconducting invariant.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1cd7f905ef6df6e1.

### scwiki-d14-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

Real compounds add orbital character, spin–orbit coupling, interlayer hopping and reconstruction. Kang's ARPES/DFT work distinguishes van Hove features with predominantly pure or mixed sublattice content near the Fermi energy of CsV3Sb5. Such information constrains low-energy models; a large density of states alone does not select a pairing symmetry. The presently checked author abstract is not a reproduction of the full spectral assignment or pairing calculation.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-dbcbd572b05dcaa4.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-1

Ortiz's original family study identified K, Rb and Cs vanadium antimonides as layered kagome metals. The later CsV3Sb5 superconductivity paper combines magnetization, resistivity and heat capacity around a 2.5 K onset. Its transport onset is suppressed at an 8 mA probe current and returns toward the nominal value at lower current, illustrating why excitation belongs in the sample record. The heat-capacity temperature floor limits conclusions about the low-temperature gap. Subsequent K and Rb member reports should retain their own samples and criteria rather than being collapsed into a universal family transition range.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-96cec6968d3c379a, source-d49026ec4f5a10a4, source-1dbc07dbbbe19132, source-4027fb28ea284a9f.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-2

The same CsV3Sb5 work discusses a much higher-temperature anomaly and a normal-state topological band background. ARPES taken well above the superconducting transition and calculated surface states above the Fermi energy do not directly measure a superconducting gap invariant. Liang's three-dimensional CDW study and Li's conjoined-CDW study further emphasize stacking, temperature and surface dependence. Different modulation descriptions cannot be merged into one structure common to every sample or termination.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-d49026ec4f5a10a4, source-7746049011a0e640, source-80eda571fc6d710c.

Conditions: Keep composition, pressure, current, surface termination, temperature type and transition criterion separate. Normal-state geometry/order is not superconducting topology.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Yang reports anomalous Hall response in KV3Sb5; Yu connects anomalous Hall response in CsV3Sb5 to its higher-temperature charge-order regime. Neither result is a phase-sensitive measurement of superconducting chirality. Ordinary multiband transport, scattering and Berry-curvature contributions require separate analysis. Likewise, the checked Mielke muon study concerns time-reversal symmetry breaking associated with charge order. A signal emerging near that ordering scale cannot simply be reassigned to a superconducting $d+id$ state.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-646e363b41fcabb3, source-59d803435c0df1ef, source-484da7abcc165cd3.

Conditions: Keep composition, pressure, current, surface termination, temperature type and transition criterion separate. Normal-state geometry/order is not superconducting topology.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-4

Chen's spatially resolved tunneling work proposes a roton pair-density-wave interpretation in CsV3Sb5. Pair-related modulations are significant evidence to investigate, but charge-order changes in local density of states, tunneling matrix elements and Josephson coupling remain relevant controls. Pressure studies also show nonmonotonic superconducting and charge-order scales. Two domes do not by themselves establish two pairing mechanisms: structure, bands, scattering and calibration can evolve together.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-5

For CsCr3Sb5, Liu's author manuscript and selected final-paper results report a maximum resistive onset of 6.4 K at 4.2 GPa, with zero resistance and AC susceptibility supporting bulk superconductivity over a pressure interval. Its critical-field curves instead use half the normal resistance. The fitted zero-temperature field is therefore not an independently observed field boundary. The final text explicitly leaves the field direction uncertain, preventing an anisotropy claim. The cubic-anvil measurement uses glycerol and room-temperature load calibration; the lower-pressure piston-cell setup uses a different medium and calibration. These are high-pressure records, not ambient-pressure entries or universal chromium-family numbers.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-6

Cheng's April 2026 paper adds a distinct charge-order result in CsCr3Sb5. The selected author text describes cleaved-surface STM with a 4.5 K base temperature and two higher-temperature modulation scales. Its stripe pattern breaks mirror symmetries while retaining a mirror-glide operation; opposite local textures do not define global handedness. Those surface images are not a high-pressure superconducting order-parameter measurement and cannot establish chiral superconductivity.

### scwiki-d14-claim-experimental-criteria-7

FeGe and ScV6Sn6 serve as comparisons. Yin's FeGe study reports charge order, magnetic stacking and an edge state within a charge-order energy gap; Arachchige's ScV6Sn6 work reports a lattice-modulated charge-order transition. Neither cited result establishes superconductivity. Absence of such evidence in these papers should not be rewritten as a timeless claim that either material can never superconduct under any preparation or pressure.

### scwiki-d14-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Allowed pairing representations are candidates until tested against the actual superconducting state. Charge-order time-reversal breaking, a normal-state anomalous Hall signal, structural handedness, tunneling modulation and a zero-bias feature each address different questions. Phase-sensitive experiments, temperature-resolved symmetry probes, bulk gap constraints and boundary-state tests can provide complementary discrimination; they are not a universal checklist that defines every possible topological superconductor. Complete scientific acceptance remains open: several references retain abstract-only review, and final-version comparisons, supplements and raw-data analyses are unfinished.

### scwiki-d14-claim-discovery-implications-1

Record composition, pressure path, excitation, surface termination and the onset, midpoint, measured-zero and thermodynamic criteria separately. Compare measured band positions with a specified model before invoking flat-band enhancement. Test whether changing charge order also changes disorder, structure or carrier balance. The useful next experiment resolves competing interpretations on a characterized sample, rather than promoting a geometric label or an isolated transition number into a mechanism.
