## Limits and disputes

Eu-substituted infinite-layer films show field-dependent resistance recovery in a specific sample and temperature window. Magnetic compensation and triplet pairing remain interpretations rather than conclusions forced by re-entrance alone. Complete scientific acceptance remains open. Selected primary passages, figures and model checks have been reviewed, while full supplements, final-author version comparisons, independent reproduction and raw-data analysis remain incomplete. Onset, midpoint, noise-floor zero, spectroscopic gaps and normal-state measurement temperatures retain distinct meanings. Pressure and strain comparisons require matching phase and preparation rather than ordering headline temperatures. Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

Formal charge neutrality gives nickel valence $v_{\mathrm{Ni}}=1+x+2\delta$ for an idealized $R_{1-x}\mathrm{Sr}_x\mathrm{NiO}_{2+\delta}$ with trivalent $R$, divalent Sr and divalent oxygen. For $R_3\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-\delta}$, it gives $v_{\mathrm{Ni}}=2.5-\delta$. Sixty-six exact bookkeeping checks preserve neutrality. These averages do not measure orbital occupancy, vacancy location, ligand holes or mobile carriers. In particular, an annealing-gas dose does not specify oxygen stoichiometry.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-35fd62b7cb3c490c, source-3f4ceab12660ad62.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

Even the elementary two-carrier low-field Drude expression $R_H=(p\mu_h^2-n\mu_e^2)/[e(p\mu_h+n\mu_e)^2]$, with $e>0$, prevents a unique carrier count from Hall sign alone. Three explicit counterexamples give negative Hall coefficients with different electron–hole population orderings. This model illustrates nonuniqueness; it is not a fit to nickelate data. Both Li and Hsu discuss multiband limitations, so a negative Hall coefficient must not be silently converted to a single-band electron density.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-35fd62b7cb3c490c, source-1b4b1103f747fe70.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-experimental-criteria-1

For the representative Nd0.8Sr0.2NiO2 film in Li's 2019 discovery, the published text identifies a 14.9 K onset by maximum curvature, a 13.6 K midpoint and 9.1 K resistance indistinguishable from the noise floor. The final methods describe six-point electrical measurements, 9–11 nm precursor films and topotactic reduction. Two-coil mutual inductance supports a diamagnetic response, but the authors explicitly decline to extract a penetration depth because of finite-size, disorder and other uncertainties. These three temperatures describe different criteria on the selected sample.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-35fd62b7cb3c490c.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Sun's 2023 bilayer-crystal report gives an 80 K resistance onset at 18.5 GPa in run 1 without pressure medium. Run 2 uses KBr and reaches a 78 K onset at 18.9 GPa. Figure 3 distinguishes the 10 μA run-1 excitation from 300 μA in run 2. Its magnetic response near 77 K is measured separately at 25.2 GPa. Residual resistance and specimen differences prevent combining these observations into one zero-resistance or bulk-fraction record.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-df0c15d62982f853.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-oxygen-strain-and-transport-1

Bhatt's final strain study distinguishes nominal substrate mismatch from measured strain: the strongly compressed film is labelled approximately −1.6% measured strain, rather than the inherited draft's −1.8%. Growth method, oxygen treatment and substrate vary across comparisons. In-plane compression accompanied by out-of-plane expansion is not equivalent to hydrostatic compression. The [strain](/scwiki/strain) article retains the source-specific structural comparison and its confounding variables.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-4b5b65a5047eb1a9.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-oxygen-strain-and-transport-2

Xiang's revised author manuscript demonstrates an oxygen-removal and ozone-annealing sequence that can recover degraded bilayer films. Repeating ozone treatment alone can instead damage the superconducting response. Its proposed phase diagram uses cumulative annealing-gas volume; oxygen concentration is not precisely measured, and unknown phases complicate interpretation. Figure 2 identifies a zero-resistance point near 5.5 K for sample S1049-4, far below its onset region. The recovery experiment constrains preparation sensitivity without establishing a calibrated carrier-density axis or a universal recycling recipe.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-3f4ceab12660ad62.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-oxygen-strain-and-transport-3

Hsu's final La2PrNi2O7 study defines 41 K using 90% of a fitted normal-state resistivity. Pulsed-field measurements access a low-temperature normal state with approximately quadratic resistivity; an extrapolated zero-field normal-state curve is not directly observed below the transition. The film is about 5 nm thick, grown on SrLaAlO4 with a SrTiO3 cap and kept cold between measurements. The reported effective mass uses an empirical Kadowaki–Woods relation, not direct calorimetry. These results describe a strained bilayer specimen, not every nickelate.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-1b4b1103f747fe70.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-recent-structures-and-membranes-1

Nie's publisher abstract, published in April 2026, reports ambient-pressure onset temperatures spanning 46–50 K in engineered 1212 and 2323 layer sequences, alongside a nonsuperconducting 1313 comparison. The exact operational criterion and lower nondetection bound have not been extracted here, so this range is not assigned to a precise searchable Tc record. Associated orbital and Fermi-surface observations constrain structure–electronic-state relationships; they do not independently prove a unique pairing interaction.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-2337a5bf19bca4c4.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-recent-structures-and-membranes-2

Lee's April 2026 membrane preprint reports 74.2 K at 91.5 GPa using 99.5% of an extrapolated normal-state resistance. Extended Data Figure 1 gives 69.1 K with an intersection construction and 75.4 K with a second-derivative construction for the illustrated transition. These differences are criterion dependence, not separate superconducting phases. Zero resistance is defined by the noise floor and occurs lower. The preprint remains explicitly labelled and is not an ambient-pressure result.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-0886448b2b71c919.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-recent-structures-and-membranes-3

The same preprint measures six membranes and fits an onset increase near 0.65 K/GPa over its sampled range. It uses room-temperature ruby calibration below 50 GPa and diamond Raman calibration above that, with the latter measured adjacent to the specimen. Silicone-oil solidification and nonhydrostatic stress complicate broadening. Its 13 T field measurements and fitted coherence lengths should not be mistaken for direct measurements of a much larger zero-temperature critical field. Extrapolating the pressure trend beyond the measured range is not a demonstrated materials prediction.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-0886448b2b71c919.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Eu-substituted infinite-layer films show field-dependent resistance recovery in a specific sample and temperature window. Magnetic compensation and triplet pairing remain interpretations rather than conclusions forced by re-entrance alone. The [re-entrant superconductivity](/scwiki/field-induced-superconductivity) and [magnetic substitution](/scwiki/magnetic-substitution-and-superconductivity) articles preserve field orientation, measurement temperature and alternative mechanisms. None of these observations establishes a universal nickelate gap symmetry.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-3504ee9027165d0a.

Conditions: Structural family, sample, oxygen/strain history, operational temperature criterion and publication version remain explicit.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

Complete scientific acceptance remains open. Selected primary passages, figures and model checks have been reviewed, while full supplements, final-author version comparisons, independent reproduction and raw-data analysis remain incomplete. Onset, midpoint, noise-floor zero, spectroscopic gaps and normal-state measurement temperatures retain distinct meanings. Pressure and strain comparisons require matching phase and preparation rather than ordering headline temperatures.

Evidence: hypothesis. Sources: source-35fd62b7cb3c490c, source-df0c15d62982f853, source-4b5b65a5047eb1a9, source-0886448b2b71c919.

Verification scope: Named selected final/author passages and figures, original abstract or exact charge/Drude model counterexamples; no complete scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d5-claim-discovery-implications-1

A useful comparison records layer sequence, oxygen history, nominal and measured composition, substrate, thickness, pressure calibration, probe and temperature criterion. Controlled oxygen cycles and structural contrasts are informative only with their phase and interface changes documented. A promising design hypothesis should specify which variable changes, which confounders remain and what observation would distinguish competing mechanisms.

articles.body:
## Scope

Hydrogen-rich superconductors connect light nuclei, strong electron–phonon coupling and pressure-dependent chemistry. Ashcroft's metallic-hydrogen proposal and later hydrogen-dominant-alloy proposal motivate this route; neither established a recoverable ambient-pressure superconductor. H₃S and LaH₁₀ are important high-pressure experimental systems. Their formulae, pressure scales and sample histories must accompany any quoted transition temperature. [R1](#ref-source-6fbecff48a8989e8) [R2](#ref-source-ba29a1eb0f9df263) [R4](#ref-source-8b901b9c6008c434) [R7](#ref-source-1e6e868a12cdd34f)

“Chemical precompression” describes a design idea, not a guarantee of low operating pressure. A predicted metallic structure, a synthesized hydride and a superconducting phase are different achievements. Distinguish the starting H₂S reagent from its proposed H₃S product, and a clathrate-like hydrogen framework from directly measured hydrogen positions. The sulfur-hydride diffraction study supports the sulfur sublattice and coexistence with sulfur; its measured patterns cannot by themselves distinguish hydrogen arrangements with the same sulfur periodicity. [R2](#ref-source-ba29a1eb0f9df263) [R3](#ref-source-2b01ce847be6bc20) [R5](#ref-source-e7837a18f3252cb9)

## Mathematical assumptions

For a specified structure, a commonly used modified-McMillan estimate is $T_c=(\omega_{\log}/1.2)\exp[-1.04(1+\lambda)/(\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda))]$, with $\omega_{\log}$ expressed in kelvin here. Duan's harmonic calculations give $\lambda=2.07$, $\omega_{\log}=1125.1$ K for R3m at 130 GPa and $\lambda=2.19$, $\omega_{\log}=1334.6$ K for Im$\bar{3}$m at 200 GPa. Substitution with $\mu^*=0.13$ and 0.10 gives approximately 155–166 K and 191–204 K, respectively. This reproduces the printed estimate convention, without additional strong-coupling or spectral-shape factors; it does not reproduce the underlying density-functional perturbation calculation. [R3](#ref-source-2b01ce847be6bc20)

Hydrogen motion can invalidate a harmonic treatment. Errea and colleagues calculated a change from $\lambda=2.64$ to 1.84 for H₃S at 200 GPa when including anharmonicity. Their full isotropic Migdal–Eliashberg calculation with $\mu^*=0.16$ changed the calculated transition from 250 to 194 K. That table is not obtained by simply substituting parameters into the preceding approximate formula. Zero-point contributions also alter the calculated decomposition landscape: both $3\mathrm{H_2S}\rightarrow2\mathrm{H_3S}+\mathrm{S}$ and $5\mathrm{H_2S}\rightarrow3\mathrm{H_3S}+\mathrm{HS_2}$ conserve atoms, but atom balance alone does not establish stability or a reaction pathway. [R8](#ref-source-1bec081a84267ffb)

An isotope comparison uses $\alpha=\ln(T_{c,\mathrm H}/T_{c,\mathrm D})/\ln2$ only after checking structure, pressure and transition criteria. The final LaH₁₀ paper compares approximately 249 K and 180 K for fcc hydride and deuteride near 150 GPa; its Fig. 4 specifies 151 and 152 GPa. These rounded values give 0.468, while the paper states 0.46. The early author's 250/168 K comparison gives 0.573 and must not be silently substituted for the final result. Phase mixtures and different deuteride structures further limit interpretation. [R7](#ref-source-1e6e868a12cdd34f)

## Experimental criteria

For sulfur hydride, the 2015 report combined resistance, field response, isotope substitution and magnetization. Its author-version Fig. 4a reports a zero-field-cooled magnetic onset of 203(1) K at 155 GPa, with a 20 Oe field-cooled comparison. The plotted transport comparison is a different pressure, 145 GPa, and must not be treated as the identical specimen condition. Its transition criterion is the onset of deviation from normal metallic resistance. Measurements to 9 T support an extrapolated zero-temperature upper critical field of approximately 95–136 T; they are not direct measurements at 136 T. The authors explicitly state that their tiny samples were below the available SQUID sensitivity. The 2023 nitrogen-doped lutetium-hydride article was retracted on 7 November 2023 following concerns including sample provenance, measurements and processing. ## Mathematical assumptions

For a specified structure, a commonly used modified-McMillan estimate is $T_c=(\omega_{\log}/1.2)\exp[-1.04(1+\lambda)/(\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda))]$, with $\omega_{\log}$ expressed in kelvin here. Duan's harmonic calculations give $\lambda=2.07$, $\omega_{\log}=1125.1$ K for R3m at 130 GPa and $\lambda=2.19$, $\omega_{\log}=1334.6$ K for Im$\bar{3}$m at 200 GPa. Substitution with $\mu^*=0.13$ and 0.10 gives approximately 155–166 K and 191–204 K, respectively. This reproduces the printed estimate convention, without additional strong-coupling or spectral-shape factors; it does not reproduce the underlying density-functional perturbation calculation. [R3](#ref-source-2b01ce847be6bc20)

Hydrogen motion can invalidate a harmonic treatment. Errea and colleagues calculated a change from $\lambda=2.64$ to 1.84 for H₃S at 200 GPa when including anharmonicity. Their full isotropic Migdal–Eliashberg calculation with $\mu^*=0.16$ changed the calculated transition from 250 to 194 K. An isotope comparison uses $\alpha=\ln(T_{c,\mathrm H}/T_{c,\mathrm D})/\ln2$ only after checking structure, pressure and transition criteria. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d6-claim-scope-1

Hydrogen-rich superconductors connect light nuclei, strong electron–phonon coupling and pressure-dependent chemistry. Ashcroft's metallic-hydrogen proposal and later hydrogen-dominant-alloy proposal motivate this route; neither established a recoverable ambient-pressure superconductor. H₃S and LaH₁₀ are important high-pressure experimental systems. Their formulae, pressure scales and sample histories must accompany any quoted transition temperature.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-6fbecff48a8989e8, source-ba29a1eb0f9df263, source-8b901b9c6008c434, source-1e6e868a12cdd34f.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-scope-2

“Chemical precompression” describes a design idea, not a guarantee of low operating pressure. A predicted metallic structure, a synthesized hydride and a superconducting phase are different achievements. Distinguish the starting H₂S reagent from its proposed H₃S product, and a clathrate-like hydrogen framework from directly measured hydrogen positions. The sulfur-hydride diffraction study supports the sulfur sublattice and coexistence with sulfur; its measured patterns cannot by themselves distinguish hydrogen arrangements with the same sulfur periodicity.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-ba29a1eb0f9df263, source-2b01ce847be6bc20, source-e7837a18f3252cb9.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

For a specified structure, a commonly used modified-McMillan estimate is $T_c=(\omega_{\log}/1.2)\exp[-1.04(1+\lambda)/(\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda))]$, with $\omega_{\log}$ expressed in kelvin here. Duan's harmonic calculations give $\lambda=2.07$, $\omega_{\log}=1125.1$ K for R3m at 130 GPa and $\lambda=2.19$, $\omega_{\log}=1334.6$ K for Im$\bar{3}$m at 200 GPa. Substitution with $\mu^*=0.13$ and 0.10 gives approximately 155–166 K and 191–204 K, respectively. This reproduces the printed estimate convention, without additional strong-coupling or spectral-shape factors; it does not reproduce the underlying density-functional perturbation calculation.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-2b01ce847be6bc20.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

Hydrogen motion can invalidate a harmonic treatment. Errea and colleagues calculated a change from $\lambda=2.64$ to 1.84 for H₃S at 200 GPa when including anharmonicity. Their full isotropic Migdal–Eliashberg calculation with $\mu^*=0.16$ changed the calculated transition from 250 to 194 K. That table is not obtained by simply substituting parameters into the preceding approximate formula. Zero-point contributions also alter the calculated decomposition landscape: both $3\mathrm{H_2S}\rightarrow2\mathrm{H_3S}+\mathrm{S}$ and $5\mathrm{H_2S}\rightarrow3\mathrm{H_3S}+\mathrm{HS_2}$ conserve atoms, but atom balance alone does not establish stability or a reaction pathway.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1bec081a84267ffb.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

An isotope comparison uses $\alpha=\ln(T_{c,\mathrm H}/T_{c,\mathrm D})/\ln2$ only after checking structure, pressure and transition criteria. The final LaH₁₀ paper compares approximately 249 K and 180 K for fcc hydride and deuteride near 150 GPa; its Fig. 4 specifies 151 and 152 GPa. These rounded values give 0.468, while the paper states 0.46. The early author's 250/168 K comparison gives 0.573 and must not be silently substituted for the final result. Phase mixtures and different deuteride structures further limit interpretation.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1e6e868a12cdd34f.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-experimental-criteria-1

For sulfur hydride, the 2015 report combined resistance, field response, isotope substitution and magnetization. Its author-version Fig. 4a reports a zero-field-cooled magnetic onset of 203(1) K at 155 GPa, with a 20 Oe field-cooled comparison. The plotted transport comparison is a different pressure, 145 GPa, and must not be treated as the identical specimen condition. Background subtraction and diamond-anvil-cell contributions require scrutiny; this scoped reading does not independently reproduce raw magnetization. The later simultaneous diffraction/transport experiment on deuteride at 173 GPa provides structural context, not a direct measurement of every hydrogen coordinate.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-8b901b9c6008c434, source-e7837a18f3252cb9.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-experimental-criteria-2

The two early lanthanum-superhydride studies have different evidence scopes. Somayazulu's author v3 describes a large resistance drop around 260 K, with room-temperature pressure changing from 188 to 196 GPa across a thermal cycle; pressure at the actual transition was not measured in that run. The lowest four-probe resistance was about 20 μΩ, while pseudo-four-probe measurements carried contact-resistance limitations. This should not be rewritten as an independently established zero-resistance or magnetic-shielding result. The final journal abstract was checked, but the selected detailed methods here come from the identified author version.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-77b774e18b0f50c7.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Drozdov's final 2019 LaH₁₀ paper reports zero resistance, isotope dependence and field suppression, with a maximum near 250–252 K around 170 GPa. Its transition criterion is the onset of deviation from normal metallic resistance. Measurements to 9 T support an extrapolated zero-temperature upper critical field of approximately 95–136 T; they are not direct measurements at 136 T. The authors explicitly state that their tiny samples were below the available SQUID sensitivity. Their H₂/D₂ vibron pressure estimates were often 10–30 GPa lower than diamond-edge estimates around 150 GPa, so pressure calibrations cannot be freely interchanged.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-1e6e868a12cdd34f.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

The 2020 carbonaceous-sulfur-hydride article was retracted on 26 September 2022. The corrected notice identifies concerns about non-standard, user-defined magnetic-background subtraction; all authors disagreed with the retraction. The 2023 nitrogen-doped lutetium-hydride article was retracted on 7 November 2023 following concerns including sample provenance, measurements and processing. These original papers remain linked as historical claims, accompanied by their notices. Their claimed temperatures are not usable experimental benchmarks in this catalogue. A retraction notice is not a substitute for an independent misconduct finding.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-d04f7965dca4d5a5, source-754d75026e52d9ac, source-a7b93ad4f4896402, source-98bc73a5e1c86c78.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

An independent LuH₂±xNᵧ study reported no superconductivity above 2 K over 0.4–40.1 GPa in its transport measurements. That constrains its tested samples and synthesis route; it does not prove that every possible Lu–N–H composition is nonsuperconducting. The final published pressure range differs from an early preprint's narrower range. In particular, a blue-to-pink colour change is not a superconductivity measurement.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-151c87f0eda0236f.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-discovery-implications-1

A credible search must connect composition and structure to dynamical and thermodynamic stability, finite-temperature and nuclear-quantum effects, synthesis access and multiple superconductivity probes. A finite structure search can miss larger cells; absence of imaginary harmonic frequencies is a local dynamical check, not proof of global stability. Preserve decompression history, mixed phases, pressure standards and unsuccessful samples instead of ranking formulae by isolated temperature claims.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-2b01ce847be6bc20, source-e7837a18f3252cb9, source-1bec081a84267ffb.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra, not independent raw-data reproduction or full scientific acceptance.

### scwiki-d6-claim-discovery-implications-2

A June 2026 study recovered Y₃Fe₄H₂₀ at ambient pressure after synthesis above about 60 GPa, with survival on the scale of tens of hours. This is useful progress in hydride recovery, but its reported SQUID test found no superconductivity down to 3 K in the tested recovered sample. Hydrogen positions were supported by structure searches, and the sample was small and not pure. Recovery, long-term stability and ambient-pressure superconductivity remain distinct questions. Full raw-data, convergence and cross-laboratory assessment remain open for this article.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-f9dfe34f7dffd9d2.

Conditions: Named source/version, sample, pressure calibration and probe limits; withdrawn claims are historical only.

claims.statement: Pair transfer and impurity interband scattering are different processes. articles.body:
## Scope

Magnesium diboride, MgB₂, is a useful benchmark for electron–phonon superconductivity with different gap scales on different Fermi-surface sheets. Its 2001 discovery report combined magnetization and resistivity near 39 K in a simple hexagonal compound. This historical temperature is not a universal sample constant or an upper bound on phonon-mediated superconductivity. [R1](#ref-source-fade6558e7eafb2b) [R6](#ref-source-7c4eac077ae5e221)

Boron honeycomb layers provide most of the electronic states near the Fermi level. The approximately cylindrical σ sheets derive mainly from in-plane boron orbitals; the π sheets have substantial out-of-plane character. Strong coupling of σ states to boron bond stretching helps explain the large gap. “Two gaps” is a useful reduction of a momentum-dependent problem: Choi's calculation at 4 K spans 6.4–7.2 meV on σ sheets and 1.2–3.7 meV on π sheets, with averages of 6.8 and 1.8 meV. These are calculated distributions, not two exactly constant measured gaps. [R2](#ref-source-a720b8200872878c) [R6](#ref-source-7c4eac077ae5e221)

## Mathematical assumptions

In an illustrative clean weak-coupling model with a shared cutoff, the linearized equations are $\Delta_i=L(T)\sum_j\lambda_{ij}\Delta_j$. The largest positive eigenvalue of the pairing matrix determines the first instability. Off-diagonal pair-transfer terms can make both gap components nonzero at the same transition, even when their amplitudes differ. For the chosen toy matrix $\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}0.40&0.08\\0.04&0.15\end{pmatrix}$, the leading eigenvalue is approximately 0.4122 and $\Delta_2/\Delta_1\approx0.1526$ at onset. Pair transfer and impurity interband scattering are different processes. An elastic scattering rate contains impurity matrix elements and connects single-particle states; it must not replace $\lambda_{ij}$ in the pairing equation. Mazin's analysis distinguishes weak σ–π impurity mixing from potentially large scattering within each band. Its normal-state conductivity adds parallel band contributions, so a single residual resistivity cannot uniquely determine the interband rate. Using its illustrated in-plane plasma weights and intraband rates, a simplified residual-conductivity calculation shifts the σ share from about 33% to 92% between the selected clean and dirty examples. This is a model illustration, not a resistivity measurement or a calculation of the full temperature dependence. [R7](#ref-source-a9d7d0b720a3bafd)

For isotope substitutions, $\alpha_i=-\Delta\ln T_c/\Delta\ln M_i$ is a partial coefficient. Bud'ko's rounded 40.2 K and 39.2 K values give $\alpha_{\mathrm B}\approx0.264$ using masses 10 and 11, consistent with the reported $0.26\pm0.03$. ## Experimental criteria

The original discovery paper reported a resistive onset of 39 K and an endpoint of 38 K using four probes at zero applied field. Magnetization used zero-field-cooled and field-cooled protocols at 10 Oe; the authors estimated a 49% superconducting volume fraction at 5 K. Their 196 MPa argon pressure was used during hot isostatic synthesis at 973 K for ten hours. It is not the pressure of the superconductivity measurement. Onset, endpoint, magnetic response and synthesis conditions must remain separate fields. [R1](#ref-source-fade6558e7eafb2b)

Bud'ko used a 2% diamagnetic-onset criterion on warming after zero-field cooling, with a 25 G measuring field. The isotopically enriched samples had narrow but different transition widths. This does not mean that 1 T is the bulk upper critical field, and these spectra alone do not determine the relative sign of the gaps. The final Choi calculation uses the anisotropic Eliashberg framework and compares calculated thermodynamics with experiments. Spectroscopic weights depend on geometry and matrix elements; fitting two components is strongest when checked against independent thermodynamic and field-dependent evidence. The original specific-heat datasets and full anisotropic numerical calculation have not been independently reproduced in this review. The Hinks author manuscript contains a version issue: Table 1 prints a Mg mass of 25.001 for a sample family, while the methods describe enriched ²⁶Mg. This discrepancy is retained as unresolved pending comparison with the final published table. No Mg-mass refit is presented. The boron ratios use the explicitly printed boron masses and temperatures. [R4](#ref-source-60ffd9b4ef2c9ccd) [R7](#ref-source-a9d7d0b720a3bafd)

Materials development must connect gap physics to usable conductors. This reference is currently checked only through the publisher's indexed summary and the authors' publication record; the electric-field criterion, full methods and coil comparison require further review. Engineering current density uses the whole composite cross-section, unlike a current density normalized to superconducting material alone. Neither operating temperature nor a current-density benchmark should enter a transition-temperature ranking. [R8](#ref-source-39e103ef0175cc7e)

Preserve processing, connectivity, field orientation, temperature and voltage criterion when comparing wires. Increasing intraband disorder, changing band filling and increasing interband impurity mixing are not interchangeable interventions. A useful candidate must satisfy its operating requirements as well as the microscopic pairing model; this article's scoped calculations do not certify a wire or magnet design. [R7](#ref-source-a9d7d0b720a3bafd) [R8](#ref-source-39e103ef0175cc7e)

## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d7-claim-scope-1

Magnesium diboride, MgB₂, is a useful benchmark for electron–phonon superconductivity with different gap scales on different Fermi-surface sheets. Its 2001 discovery report combined magnetization and resistivity near 39 K in a simple hexagonal compound. This historical temperature is not a universal sample constant or an upper bound on phonon-mediated superconductivity.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-fade6558e7eafb2b, source-7c4eac077ae5e221.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-scope-2

Boron honeycomb layers provide most of the electronic states near the Fermi level. The approximately cylindrical σ sheets derive mainly from in-plane boron orbitals; the π sheets have substantial out-of-plane character. Strong coupling of σ states to boron bond stretching helps explain the large gap. “Two gaps” is a useful reduction of a momentum-dependent problem: Choi's calculation at 4 K spans 6.4–7.2 meV on σ sheets and 1.2–3.7 meV on π sheets, with averages of 6.8 and 1.8 meV. These are calculated distributions, not two exactly constant measured gaps.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-a720b8200872878c, source-7c4eac077ae5e221.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

In an illustrative clean weak-coupling model with a shared cutoff, the linearized equations are $\Delta_i=L(T)\sum_j\lambda_{ij}\Delta_j$. The largest positive eigenvalue of the pairing matrix determines the first instability. Off-diagonal pair-transfer terms can make both gap components nonzero at the same transition, even when their amplitudes differ. For the chosen toy matrix $\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}0.40&0.08\\0.04&0.15\end{pmatrix}$, the leading eigenvalue is approximately 0.4122 and $\Delta_2/\Delta_1\approx0.1526$ at onset. Setting both off-diagonal entries to zero removes the induced second component at the higher transition. These numbers illustrate coupled equations; they are not fitted MgB₂ parameters.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-7c4eac077ae5e221, source-a9d7d0b720a3bafd.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

Pair transfer and impurity interband scattering are different processes. An elastic scattering rate contains impurity matrix elements and connects single-particle states; it must not replace $\lambda_{ij}$ in the pairing equation. Mazin's analysis distinguishes weak σ–π impurity mixing from potentially large scattering within each band. Its normal-state conductivity adds parallel band contributions, so a single residual resistivity cannot uniquely determine the interband rate. Using its illustrated in-plane plasma weights and intraband rates, a simplified residual-conductivity calculation shifts the σ share from about 33% to 92% between the selected clean and dirty examples. This is a model illustration, not a resistivity measurement or a calculation of the full temperature dependence.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-a9d7d0b720a3bafd.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

For isotope substitutions, $\alpha_i=-\Delta\ln T_c/\Delta\ln M_i$ is a partial coefficient. Bud'ko's rounded 40.2 K and 39.2 K values give $\alpha_{\mathrm B}\approx0.264$ using masses 10 and 11, consistent with the reported $0.26\pm0.03$. Hinks separately measured both elements and reported approximately $\alpha_{\mathrm B}=0.30(1)$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{Mg}}=0.02(1)$. Their sum near 0.32 differs from the simplest harmonic single-scale expectation of 0.5. This does not uniquely isolate anharmonicity, Coulomb effects or multiband contributions.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-22ad55507a1e49c5, source-60ffd9b4ef2c9ccd.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-experimental-criteria-1

The original discovery paper reported a resistive onset of 39 K and an endpoint of 38 K using four probes at zero applied field. Magnetization used zero-field-cooled and field-cooled protocols at 10 Oe; the authors estimated a 49% superconducting volume fraction at 5 K. Their 196 MPa argon pressure was used during hot isostatic synthesis at 973 K for ten hours. It is not the pressure of the superconductivity measurement. Onset, endpoint, magnetic response and synthesis conditions must remain separate fields.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-fade6558e7eafb2b.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Bud'ko used a 2% diamagnetic-onset criterion on warming after zero-field cooling, with a 25 G measuring field. The isotopically enriched samples had narrow but different transition widths. Hinks used a 1 G field and compared extrapolated onset with a 10% criterion; natural and enriched Mg samples showed possible impurity differences that the authors could not quantify. The Mg contribution therefore belongs to the Hinks study, not to the earlier boron-only experiment. The six printed boron comparisons have been recalculated here, but the raw magnetization has not been refitted.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-22ad55507a1e49c5, source-60ffd9b4ef2c9ccd.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Szabó's Cu–MgB₂ point contacts showed small and large gap scales around 2.8 and 7 meV. Their two-component BTK fits kept interface transparency and relative weight fixed across temperature; thermal smearing makes the two contributions harder to separate near the bulk transition. Fields up to 1 T preferentially suppressed the small-gap spectral contribution, helping reveal the large-gap features. This does not mean that 1 T is the bulk upper critical field, and these spectra alone do not determine the relative sign of the gaps. Using a transition temperature of 39 K, the low-temperature gap ratios are approximately 1.67 and 4.17, rather than a single weak-coupling BCS ratio.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-69ced9b5dda860f1.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

The final Choi calculation uses the anisotropic Eliashberg framework and compares calculated thermodynamics with experiments. Its successful description does not turn a two-constant-gap approximation into an exact band-resolved result. Spectroscopic weights depend on geometry and matrix elements; fitting two components is strongest when checked against independent thermodynamic and field-dependent evidence. The original specific-heat datasets and full anisotropic numerical calculation have not been independently reproduced in this review.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-69ced9b5dda860f1, source-7c4eac077ae5e221.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra only; final-version/raw-data issues explicitly retained.

### scwiki-d7-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

The Hinks author manuscript contains a version issue: Table 1 prints a Mg mass of 25.001 for a sample family, while the methods describe enriched ²⁶Mg. This discrepancy is retained as unresolved pending comparison with the final published table. No Mg-mass refit is presented. The boron ratios use the explicitly printed boron masses and temperatures. Likewise, the Mazin author PDF's generated date is not its submission date; the cited version is the arXiv submission of 1 April 2002.

### scwiki-d7-claim-discovery-implications-1

Materials development must connect gap physics to usable conductors. A 2026 study of square, 19-filament MgB₂ wire reports a 14.2% filling factor and an engineering-current benchmark at 4.2 K and 6.5 T. This reference is currently checked only through the publisher's indexed summary and the authors' publication record; the electric-field criterion, full methods and coil comparison require further review. Engineering current density uses the whole composite cross-section, unlike a current density normalized to superconducting material alone. Neither operating temperature nor a current-density benchmark should enter a transition-temperature ranking.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-39e103ef0175cc7e.

Conditions: Source-specific sample, temperature, probe, isotope and publication version; toy models are not fitted material results.

### scwiki-d7-claim-discovery-implications-2

Preserve processing, connectivity, field orientation, temperature and voltage criterion when comparing wires. Increasing intraband disorder, changing band filling and increasing interband impurity mixing are not interchangeable interventions. A useful candidate must satisfy its operating requirements as well as the microscopic pairing model; this article's scoped calculations do not certify a wire or magnet design.

articles.body:
## Scope

Heavy-fermion superconductors pair electrons in a strongly renormalized metallic state. Their large low-temperature electronic heat capacity and magnetic response reflect interactions involving partially filled f shells, not unusually heavy atoms moving as Cooper pairs. CeCu₂Si₂ established this class in 1979; the discovery paper reported a transition near 0.5 K. Different compositions and probes need not reproduce that exact number. The family is a laboratory for competing correlations rather than a single pairing mechanism. [R1](#ref-source-0ebda9b697c1f7fd) [R5](#ref-source-5962cf8038597944)

Kondo screening, conduction-electron-mediated magnetic interactions, hybridization and valence changes provide useful organizing ideas. Doniach's competition between magnetic order and a compensated state is a model framework. Proximity to a magnetic boundary does not by itself identify the pairing interaction or predict a superconducting transition. Uranium compounds also require attention to itinerant 5f character and strong spin–orbit coupling; a label borrowed from a cerium compound is not a complete microscopic description. [R2](#ref-source-1bdac37fd450eb32) [R6](#ref-source-e7c77a3327daf5c6) [R9](#ref-source-15aec45a868e9fb9)

## Mathematical assumptions

In a Fermi-liquid regime, the electronic coefficient $\gamma=\lim_{T\to0}C_e/T$ is proportional to the renormalized density of states. A finite-temperature value of total $C/T$ is not automatically that limit. Petrovic's CeCoIn₅ report gives about 290 mJ mol⁻¹ K⁻² above 2.5 K but a much larger low-temperature normal-state value under field. Thus its apparent $\Delta C/(\gamma T_c)\approx4.5$ cannot be converted mechanically into a coupling strength using a temperature-independent normal-state baseline. [R5](#ref-source-5962cf8038597944)

Kittaka's CeCu₂Si₂ analysis subtracts a nuclear term. With numerical field $h$ in tesla and temperature $t$ in kelvin, its empirical expression is $C_n/T=(7.4h^2+0.1)t^{-3}\times10^{-6}$ J mol⁻¹ K⁻². At 60 mK it gives approximately 0.00046, 0.111 and 0.309 J mol⁻¹ K⁻² for 0, 1.8 and 3 T. These recalculations illustrate the size of the correction; they are not a new fit or evidence that any arbitrary subtraction is acceptable. [R3](#ref-source-2764bce38246bfae)

Pang's simplified band-mixing model uses $|\Delta(\varphi)|=\sqrt{a^2\cos^2(2\varphi)+b^2\sin^2(2\varphi)}$ at zero temperature. For nonzero amplitudes on the assumed cylinder, the minimum is $\min(|a|,|b|)$; exchanging them preserves angular averages. The reported S-type fit uses $a=2.5k_BT_c$ and $b=0.58k_BT_c$. This magnitude does not specify the full band matrix or its time-reversal properties. A scalar chiral gap can have the same magnitude; that algebraic coincidence does not equate the two physical states. [R4](#ref-source-e721bddb9ef11661)

## Experimental criteria

The CeCu₂Si₂ specific-heat study used a 13.8 mg S-type crystal, measurements down to 40 mK and a nuclear correction constrained by high-field normal-state data. It reported low-energy behavior consistent with full gaps and no detected in-plane angular oscillation within stated sensitivity. The result constrains quasiparticles weighted strongly by thermodynamics; it is not a universal exclusion of every possible small-band node. The author manuscript's February 2014 version must not be dated from its later PDF generation stamp. [R3](#ref-source-2764bce38246bfae)

Pang's penetration-depth measurements reached 40 mK. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d8-claim-scope-1

Heavy-fermion superconductors pair electrons in a strongly renormalized metallic state. Their large low-temperature electronic heat capacity and magnetic response reflect interactions involving partially filled f shells, not unusually heavy atoms moving as Cooper pairs. CeCu₂Si₂ established this class in 1979; the discovery paper reported a transition near 0.5 K. Different compositions and probes need not reproduce that exact number. The family is a laboratory for competing correlations rather than a single pairing mechanism.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-0ebda9b697c1f7fd, source-5962cf8038597944.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-scope-2

Kondo screening, conduction-electron-mediated magnetic interactions, hybridization and valence changes provide useful organizing ideas. Doniach's competition between magnetic order and a compensated state is a model framework. Proximity to a magnetic boundary does not by itself identify the pairing interaction or predict a superconducting transition. Uranium compounds also require attention to itinerant 5f character and strong spin–orbit coupling; a label borrowed from a cerium compound is not a complete microscopic description.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1bdac37fd450eb32, source-e7c77a3327daf5c6, source-15aec45a868e9fb9.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

In a Fermi-liquid regime, the electronic coefficient $\gamma=\lim_{T\to0}C_e/T$ is proportional to the renormalized density of states. A finite-temperature value of total $C/T$ is not automatically that limit. Petrovic's CeCoIn₅ report gives about 290 mJ mol⁻¹ K⁻² above 2.5 K but a much larger low-temperature normal-state value under field. Thus its apparent $\Delta C/(\gamma T_c)\approx4.5$ cannot be converted mechanically into a coupling strength using a temperature-independent normal-state baseline.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-5962cf8038597944.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

Kittaka's CeCu₂Si₂ analysis subtracts a nuclear term. With numerical field $h$ in tesla and temperature $t$ in kelvin, its empirical expression is $C_n/T=(7.4h^2+0.1)t^{-3}\times10^{-6}$ J mol⁻¹ K⁻². At 60 mK it gives approximately 0.00046, 0.111 and 0.309 J mol⁻¹ K⁻² for 0, 1.8 and 3 T. These recalculations illustrate the size of the correction; they are not a new fit or evidence that any arbitrary subtraction is acceptable.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-2764bce38246bfae.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

Pang's simplified band-mixing model uses $|\Delta(\varphi)|=\sqrt{a^2\cos^2(2\varphi)+b^2\sin^2(2\varphi)}$ at zero temperature. For nonzero amplitudes on the assumed cylinder, the minimum is $\min(|a|,|b|)$; exchanging them preserves angular averages. The reported S-type fit uses $a=2.5k_BT_c$ and $b=0.58k_BT_c$. This magnitude does not specify the full band matrix or its time-reversal properties. A scalar chiral gap can have the same magnitude; that algebraic coincidence does not equate the two physical states.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-e721bddb9ef11661.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-experimental-criteria-1

The CeCu₂Si₂ specific-heat study used a 13.8 mg S-type crystal, measurements down to 40 mK and a nuclear correction constrained by high-field normal-state data. It reported low-energy behavior consistent with full gaps and no detected in-plane angular oscillation within stated sensitivity. The result constrains quasiparticles weighted strongly by thermodynamics; it is not a universal exclusion of every possible small-band node. The author manuscript's February 2014 version must not be dated from its later PDF generation stamp.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-2764bce38246bfae.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Pang's penetration-depth measurements reached 40 mK. Its S-type sample showed a specific-heat transition near 0.64 K; an A/S-type sample showed superconducting and antiferromagnetic anomalies near 0.53 and 0.7 K. These are different transitions. Nodeless low-temperature behavior motivates the proposed d+d description, but fitting these data does not uniquely settle the order parameter. Raw-data refitting and the complete supplement remain outside this scoped review.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-e721bddb9ef11661.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-experimental-criteria-3

For CeCoIn₅, the discovery study combined zero resistance, magnetic shielding and a heat-capacity anomaly near 2.3 K. It also found substantially different upper critical fields parallel and perpendicular to the c axis. Later neutron work found magnetic order that disappears with superconductivity at the high-field boundary. A coupled magnetic Q phase therefore cannot be described as a clean demonstration of a standalone textbook FFLO state.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-5962cf8038597944, source-fda01ade7737b638.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

CeCu₂Si₂ should not be assigned an unqualified textbook nodal d-wave label. Full-gap thermodynamics, sign-sensitive interpretations and band structure must be reconciled. Its pressure response adds another question: Holmes measured resistivity and ac heat capacity above 6 GPa in helium and interpreted anomalies near 4.5 GPa through valence fluctuations. That interpretation is a proposed mechanism, not a direct measurement of a unique pairing interaction.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-2764bce38246bfae, source-e721bddb9ef11661, source-e7c77a3327daf5c6.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

UPt₃ has multiple superconducting phases and Kerr evidence constraining time-reversal symmetry. Heating, field training and the phase being probed matter. This does not uniquely select f-wave symmetry or establish a topological device. URhGe and UCoGe provide coexistence evidence for ferromagnetism and superconductivity, but their magnetic and superconducting transition temperatures are distinct. Their respective field responses cannot be exchanged between compounds.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-d3edee404071ac81, source-15aec45a868e9fb9, source-a4695ba5bfa789f3.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-limits-and-disputes-3

UTe₂ requires particularly careful qualifiers. Antiferromagnetic neutron fluctuations, transverse high-field fluctuations and sample-dependent Kerr results probe different conditions. The 2023 Kerr study found no spontaneous signal in the tested single-transition samples; it does not negate every other superconducting phase. No single large upper critical field, fluctuation spectrum or null Kerr observation determines spin structure and topology together.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-df199ac9453d6985, source-15cfc4a2f9587af0, source-dd4e897d833ce69c.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-discovery-implications-1

The 2025 UTe₂ halo study mapped transport boundaries with pulsed fields, generally near 0.63 K, using resistance and contactless proximity-detector measurements. Tilting away from the b axis revealed an extended high-field region. The experiment reached approximately 73 T; extrapolated persistence beyond that field is not a measured upper boundary. Its multicomponent triplet interpretation remains a model conclusion. Supplementary sample details, heating corrections and the deposited raw data have not been independently reanalyzed here.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-0c4d7cebb12a0d5b.

Conditions: Material, sample, pressure, field direction and probe-specific conditions; model amplitudes and operating temperatures are not measured transition temperatures.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded algebra; full scientific acceptance and original-data reproduction remain open.

### scwiki-d8-claim-discovery-implications-2

The 2026 transverse-fluctuation study measured the normal state at 4 K; superconducting phase boundaries at 300 mK were comparisons with earlier work. Neither temperature is a newly measured transition temperature in that experiment. Discovery records should retain the sample, pressure, field direction, probe and criterion, then compare mechanisms across compatible conditions. The goal is to identify informative constraints, not rank unrelated temperatures or convert candidate topology into an established engineering capability.

articles.body:
## Scope

Alkali-doped fullerides join molecular vibrations, narrow electronic bands and strong local interactions in one material family. In ideal A₃C₆₀, three donated electrons half-fill the three molecular t₁ᵤ orbitals, whose spin capacity is six. Potassium, rubidium and cesium compounds must be identified by stoichiometry, crystal structure and preparation. Pressure-induced equilibrium superconductivity and light-driven responses are separate evidence classes. [R5](#ref-source-e2b9d469a7c556df) [R7](#ref-source-07be806c0002c690)

The 1991 potassium discovery already illustrates why one temperature is insufficient: the abstract reports a thin-film resistive onset near 16 K and essentially vanishing resistance by 5 K, while bulk magnetic and microwave measurements indicate an 18 K transition. The subsequent rubidium report gives a maximum of 28 K from bulk magnetic and microwave evidence. These abstract-level checks establish historical observations; they do not constitute a complete reassessment of the original specimens. [R1](#ref-source-51b1a52d16139e58) [R2](#ref-source-0fb5ae1290bd2998)

## Mathematical assumptions

One influential model represents each molecule by three effective p-like orbitals with local terms $H_U=U(n-3)^2/2$ and $H_J=J[2\mathbf S^2+\mathbf L^2/2]+5J(n-3)^2/6$. Angular momenta are dimensionless. In this convention ordinary Hund exchange has $J=-J_H<0$; integrating out Jahn–Teller vibrations can instead give $J=-J_H+J_{JT}>0$. This static reduction requires the coherent electronic scale $ZW$ to lie below the relevant phonon energy. It should not be applied across the whole bandwidth range without checking retardation. [R5](#ref-source-e2b9d469a7c556df)

At exactly three electrons, the model multiplets $^4S$, $^2D$ and $^2P$ have energies $15J/2$, $9J/2$ and $5J/2$, with respective degeneracies 4, 10 and 6. They account for $\binom{6}{3}=20$ local states. Positive effective $J$ favors the low-spin $^2P$ multiplet; negative $J$ favors $^4S$. ## Experimental criteria

For fcc Cs₃C₆₀, Ganin and colleagues report a pressure-dependent magnetic onset: 25.6 K at 1.3 kbar has only about 0.1% shielding, whereas 29.7 K at 2.2 kbar has about 12%. Mitrano's optical study and Budden's longer-lived driven response concern pumped K₃C₆₀. Fullerides motivate simultaneous control of bandwidth, local vibronic interactions, molecular valence and disorder. ## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-d9-claim-scope-1

Alkali-doped fullerides join molecular vibrations, narrow electronic bands and strong local interactions in one material family. In ideal A₃C₆₀, three donated electrons half-fill the three molecular t₁ᵤ orbitals, whose spin capacity is six. Potassium, rubidium and cesium compounds must be identified by stoichiometry, crystal structure and preparation. Pressure-induced equilibrium superconductivity and light-driven responses are separate evidence classes.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-e2b9d469a7c556df, source-07be806c0002c690.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-scope-2

The 1991 potassium discovery already illustrates why one temperature is insufficient: the abstract reports a thin-film resistive onset near 16 K and essentially vanishing resistance by 5 K, while bulk magnetic and microwave measurements indicate an 18 K transition. The subsequent rubidium report gives a maximum of 28 K from bulk magnetic and microwave evidence. These abstract-level checks establish historical observations; they do not constitute a complete reassessment of the original specimens.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-51b1a52d16139e58, source-0fb5ae1290bd2998.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

One influential model represents each molecule by three effective p-like orbitals with local terms $H_U=U(n-3)^2/2$ and $H_J=J[2\mathbf S^2+\mathbf L^2/2]+5J(n-3)^2/6$. Angular momenta are dimensionless. In this convention ordinary Hund exchange has $J=-J_H<0$; integrating out Jahn–Teller vibrations can instead give $J=-J_H+J_{JT}>0$. This static reduction requires the coherent electronic scale $ZW$ to lie below the relevant phonon energy. It should not be applied across the whole bandwidth range without checking retardation.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-e2b9d469a7c556df.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

At exactly three electrons, the model multiplets $^4S$, $^2D$ and $^2P$ have energies $15J/2$, $9J/2$ and $5J/2$, with respective degeneracies 4, 10 and 6. They account for $\binom{6}{3}=20$ local states. Positive effective $J$ favors the low-spin $^2P$ multiplet; negative $J$ favors $^4S$. This is an algebraic check of the effective local Hamiltonian, not a measured molecular spectrum or proof of superconducting order.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-e2b9d469a7c556df.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

The heuristic Cooper-channel amplitude $A^*\simeq ZU-10J/3$ illustrates how correlations can reduce repulsion relative to an inverted exchange. For illustrative fixed ratios $U/W=0.5$ and $J/W=0.05$, its sign changes at $Z=1/3$. Simultaneously the coherent bandwidth is $ZW$: decreasing $Z$ does not supply an unlimited transition-temperature gain. The published argument explicitly allows deviations near the Mott boundary; its underlying DMFT model uses an infinite-coordination Bethe lattice. No self-consistent DMFT calculation or measured transition follows from this toy sweep.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-e2b9d469a7c556df.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-experimental-criteria-1

For fcc Cs₃C₆₀, Ganin and colleagues report a pressure-dependent magnetic onset: 25.6 K at 1.3 kbar has only about 0.1% shielding, whereas 29.7 K at 2.2 kbar has about 12%. The maximum is approximately 35 K near 7 kbar, equivalent to 0.7 GPa. Measurements use 20 Oe, zero-field-cooled/field-cooled protocols and a tin pressure reference. A15 Cs₃C₆₀ reaches a separately reported maximum near 38 K; its value must not be assigned to the fcc sample.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-634d02f3c2bfde0d, source-5e6d3e7ed715ad6a.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-experimental-criteria-2

The fcc study also separates magnetic ordering near 2.2 K from the A15 ordering scale near 46 K. Neither is a superconducting transition. Multiphase powders and small shielding fractions require particular care when locating the first superconducting signal. The magnetometry pressure range ends near 10.6 kbar; the separate diffraction measurements extend to much higher pressures. Combining those ranges would falsely imply that superconductivity was measured throughout the structural experiment.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-5e6d3e7ed715ad6a.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Published online on 9 June 2026, Shchukin and colleagues tune Rb uptake in nanostructured C₆₀ films. Figure 2f labels Rb₂.₇₁C₆₀ with $T_{\mathrm{onset}}=22.4$ K and $T_{\mathrm{zero}}=7.0$ K, and Rb₂.₉₈C₆₀ with 26.4 K and 14.5 K. The former criterion is a local resistivity maximum; the latter uses $d\rho/dT<5\times10^{-4}$ mΩ cm K⁻¹ in the plotted low-temperature window. It is a stated operational criterion, not an instrument-independent definition of exact zero resistance.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-64cd48d99353501a.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-experimental-criteria-4

That experiment uses Raman analysis with relative scattering cross sections to estimate composition, and van der Pauw transport. The 10 μA intercalation current differs from the 1 μA resistance-probe current. Stoichiometry, grain connectivity, thickness and transition criterion must accompany any comparison with bulk rubidium fullerides. The supplement and underlying transport datasets have not been independently reanalyzed here.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-64cd48d99353501a.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Mitrano's optical study and Budden's longer-lived driven response concern pumped K₃C₆₀. A finite-frequency inductive response and suppressed transient resistance constrain the nonequilibrium state, but do not by themselves establish an equilibrium thermodynamic transition. Budden's 100 K operating condition is therefore recorded as a transient-response temperature with no equilibrium Tc. Its pulsed two-terminal readout and static four-terminal contact calibration are distinct measurement steps. Pulse conditions, delay, lifetime and alternative conductivity models remain essential.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-6ee3670220e24ff1, source-07be806c0002c690.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

The historical hole-doped C₆₀ claim at 52 K was retracted on 6 March 2003. The original paper and its notice are retained together for traceability; the withdrawn value is excluded from experimental transition records. The notice identifies concerns about device-measurement data following an independent investigation. A citation in an older, otherwise valid paper does not restore the withdrawn claim.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-091fb85b144daad9, source-8822fee6435cf8cc.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-discovery-implications-1

Fullerides motivate simultaneous control of bandwidth, local vibronic interactions, molecular valence and disorder. A superconducting dome near a Mott state is compatible with cooperation between phonons and correlations; it does not uniquely determine the pairing kernel. Neither a fully open gap nor proximity to a magnetic insulator proves that one interaction acts alone. Report model assumptions beside the experimental evidence used to constrain them.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-5e6d3e7ed715ad6a, source-e2b9d469a7c556df.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

### scwiki-d9-claim-discovery-implications-2

Current-driven intercalation offers a method for tuning samples rather than a new bulk temperature record. Reproducible optimization needs composition maps, measurement-current controls and comparable transition definitions. Keep pressure polymorphs and optically driven states separate when selecting targets: their conditions cannot be collapsed into a single family-wide Tc ranking.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-64cd48d99353501a, source-5e6d3e7ed715ad6a, source-07be806c0002c690.

Conditions: Stoichiometry, polymorph, pressure, probe and criterion are distinct; transient and magnetic temperatures are not equilibrium Tc.

Verification scope: Selected original passages, dated retraction notice and bounded model algebra; full scientific acceptance remains open.

articles.body:
## Scope

Pressure changes interatomic distances, electronic bandwidths, lattice vibrations and phase stability. It can also change the material itself through structural conversion or chemical reaction. A diamond anvil cell identifies an apparatus; it does not establish a purely hydrostatic stress state at the sample. Pressure medium, temperature, loading history and sample geometry belong to every quantitative comparison. [R1](#ref-source-c1c9ef4bc5cf71dd) [R2](#ref-source-a631bcd83d23567b) [R5](#ref-source-8b901b9c6008c434)

This article concerns measurements while pressure is applied. A state retained after rapid pressure release has a different thermodynamic and kinetic history. Deng's 2026 pressure-quench paper explicitly separates creating a phase under load, releasing pressure and characterizing the recovered state. Its reported 151 K scale must not be pooled with an in-situ pressure curve. Here only its abstract and introductory protocol are checked; the detailed transition criterion and recovery evidence require a separate review. [R7](#ref-source-14d1e9e0097f7ffb)

## Mathematical assumptions

With tensile stress positive, define $P=-\mathrm{tr}(\sigma)/3$ and $s_{ij}=\sigma_{ij}+P\delta_{ij}$. Then $\sigma_{ij}=-P\delta_{ij}+s_{ij}$ with $\mathrm{tr}(s)=0$. Hydrostatic stress has $s=0$; equal mean pressure does not imply equal deviatoric stress. A measured pressure dependence is a path through several changing variables. In the simplified weak-coupling expression $T_c=A\omega\exp(-1/\lambda)$, holding A fixed gives $d\ln T_c/dP=d\ln\omega/dP+\lambda^{-2}d\lambda/dP$. Torikachvili and colleagues used sample-resistance anomalies, cross-checked against manganin, to locate freezing-related changes in pressure media. Medvedev's Fe1.01Se study reports an approximately 36.7 K resistive transition at 8.9 GPa and a decrease at higher pressures. Onset, midpoint, zero resistance and magnetic or thermodynamic signatures answer different questions. The high-pressure FeSe curves broaden and coexist with a structurally transformed fraction; a surviving conducting path is not a direct bulk-volume measurement. For transferable discovery records, preserve composition, pressure interval, medium, calibrant, temperature, protocol and transition criterion. Quote a slope only over its stated phase and pressure interval. Keep ambient recovered states, in-situ high-pressure phases and theoretical estimates separately searchable. Pressure can expose useful physics without guaranteeing a recoverable ambient material or a technologically useful conductor. [R5](#ref-source-8b901b9c6008c434) [R6](#ref-source-1e6e868a12cdd34f) [R7](#ref-source-14d1e9e0097f7ffb)

Check: published-abstract-and-introductory-protocol-only. Checked: 2026-10-18. Published online 9 March 2026; issue 17 March. Abstract and introduction through three-stage pressure-quench protocol read. Subsequent access returned a browser challenge; detailed transition criterion, figures and recovery data were not checked. No accepted transition-temperature record is added from this limited reading.
### Ref source-ba10e800a1246bf6

[R8] Theory of Superconductivity (1957). [DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175). Publication: journal-article. Check: primary-full-text-scoped-check.
