articles.body:
## Scope

A Wilson loop describes transport around a closed path within a specified band subspace. Its eigenvalues survive unitary changes of basis inside that subspace; individual matrix entries do not. Use a fixed-rank, isolated projector and a consistent boundary identification. An insulator's occupied bands and a fully gapped Bogoliubov Hamiltonian's negative-energy bands are different physical constructions. A computed phase spectrum alone does not demonstrate superconductivity, a measured bulk gap or Majorana modes. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

The loop can organize Chern winding, time-reversal topology and hybrid Wannier centers. Those interpretations require additional assumptions. A closed-loop phase is not generally quantized, and an attractive crossing pattern is not sufficient evidence for a topological invariant. Zak's original abstract emphasizes symmetry-dependent quantization; the complete original derivation has not been reviewed here. [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R4](#ref-source-50b4c7274c53cf48)

## Mathematical assumptions

Let the columns of $U_j$ form an orthonormal frame. Define $\mathcal A=iU^\dagger dU$ and forward overlaps $M_j=U_j^\dagger U_{j+1}$. In a periodic model basis, close the final link with $U_N=U_0$ and order $W=M_0M_1\cdots M_{N-1}$ from left to right along the path. Since $M_j=I-i\mathcal A_j\Delta k+O(\Delta k^2)$, the corresponding ordered exponential has $-i\mathcal A$, not $+i\mathcal A$. For one band, $\arg W=-\gamma$ modulo $2\pi$, where $\gamma=\oint\mathcal A$. The inverse-loop convention is also valid if every phase and orientation is translated consistently. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82)

Under $U_j\mapsto U_jG_j$, with unitary $G_j$, each link becomes $G_j^\dagger M_jG_{j+1}$ and the closed product becomes $G_0^\dagger WG_0$. Interior factors cancel. This algebra explains both spectral gauge invariance and the need for closure. Actual Bloch bases can require a reciprocal-lattice sewing operator and orbital-position information instead of a naive endpoint identification. A different orbital embedding is not automatically a harmless gauge rotation within the same physical projector. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271)

Finite-step overlaps are generally not unitary. For $M_j=V_j\Sigma_j Z_j^\dagger$, use its polar unitary factor $Q_j=V_jZ_j^\dagger$ when the overlap is nonsingular. This construction preserves gauge covariance and yields a unitary discrete product. Record the smallest singular values, subspace dimension, direct gap and mesh convergence. Polar projection cannot repair a singular overlap, an incorrectly selected subspace or an unresolved band touching. [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

An independent rank-two example combines spinors $(\cos(\vartheta/2),e^{iwt}\sin(\vartheta/2))$ in separate two-dimensional blocks. Their analytic forward phases are $2\pi w\sin^2(\vartheta/2)$ modulo $2\pi$. Meshes of 32, 64 and 128 points approach these phases while raw-product eigenvalue magnitudes remain below one. Random $U(2)$ frame rotations, shifted basepoints and reversed paths pass the covariance and conjugation checks. Omitting the closing link deliberately breaks spectral gauge invariance. These are synthetic checks, not a material calculation. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90)

For an increasing-$k_x$ loop and positive $(k_x,k_y)$ orientation, the continuously unwrapped phase $\Theta(k_y)=\arg\det W(k_y)$ winds by $2\pi C$ as $k_y$ traverses its period in this convention. Four lower-band examples of $h=(\sin k_x,\sin k_y,m+\cos k_x+\cos k_y)\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma$ give $C=0,+1,-1,0$ at $m=-3,-1,+1,+3$. Three meshes agree with separate analytic-curvature quadratures, and reversing the loop reverses the sign. The critical masses $-2,0,2$ have explicit gap zeros and are rejected. Integer output alone is not a convergence certificate. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

## Experimental criteria

In a two-dimensional band insulator with time reversal satisfying $\mathcal T^2=-1$, the parity of Kramers-partner exchange over half the transverse Brillouin zone diagnoses the $\mathbb Z_2$ class. Preserve the complete occupied projector, the bulk gap and symmetry constraints. Sorting principal phases independently at every point can invent discontinuities at a branch cut; follow spectral connectivity or a validated gap-tracking procedure. The local checks above do not implement or certify a general $\mathbb Z_2$ classifier. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90)

For a single band with the stated Bloch convention, a hybrid center satisfies $\bar x/a=\gamma/(2\pi)=-\arg W/(2\pi)$ modulo one. In multiple bands, Wilson eigenphases correspond to centers in the appropriate parallel-transport or maximally localized hybrid construction, not arbitrary individual Wannier functions. Physical electronic polarization also needs electron charge, occupations, cell volume and a consistent origin; total polarization includes ionic contributions. Insulating adiabatic changes can be meaningful while an absolute branch remains ambiguous by a polarization quantum. A BdG phase spectrum cannot simply be substituted into the ordinary electron-polarization formula. [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

An experimental comparison needs an explicit map from the measured observable to the modeled projector, including sample state, orbital basis, energy window and relevant symmetry. Band inversion, a calculated loop or an isolated boundary feature does not by itself verify the full pairing state. No experimental transition temperature or material certification is assigned to the synthetic examples on this page. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

## Limits and disputes

An isolated band manifold can have a well-defined Wilson loop even when a material is metallic. Its invariant is then not automatically the invariant of all physically occupied states: a Fermi surface makes that projector change rank. Likewise, band disentanglement selects a model subspace whose validity needs separate evidence. For BdG systems, respect particle-hole and time-reversal constraints and avoid interpreting Nambu duplication as independent electron occupations. Strong interactions, disorder and nodal systems can require different formulations. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

Complete scientific acceptance remains open. Selected author and published passages, two original polarization pages and independent numerical examples have been checked. The full Yu equivalence proof, full Zak derivation, final-version comparisons, realistic orbital sewing, material fits and a general time-reversal classifier have not been reproduced. The numerical checks certify only the stated bounded constructions. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271) [R4](#ref-source-50b4c7274c53cf48)

## Discovery implications

Archive the Hamiltonian or projector, basis and embedding, symmetry operators, loop orientation, sewing rule and phase convention with every topology claim. Keep raw singular values and mesh history alongside the plotted spectrum. Compare a simple limit with an independent curvature or symmetry calculation before interpreting a complicated model. This makes a Wilson-loop result a reproducible hypothesis about a specified system rather than an unsupported label attached to a candidate superconductor. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

## Related topics

[Berry curvature](/scwiki/berry-curvature), [Chern number](/scwiki/chern-number), [time-reversal-invariant topology](/scwiki/time-reversal-invariant-topological-superconductivity), and [Majorana zero modes](/scwiki/majorana-zero-modes).

Since $M_j=I-i\mathcal A_j\Delta k+O(\Delta k^2)$, the corresponding ordered exponential has $-i\mathcal A$, not $+i\mathcal A$. For one band, $\arg W=-\gamma$ modulo $2\pi$, where $\gamma=\oint\mathcal A$. The inverse-loop convention is also valid if every phase and orientation is translated consistently. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82)

Under $U_j\mapsto U_jG_j$, with unitary $G_j$, each link becomes $G_j^\dagger M_jG_{j+1}$ and the closed product becomes $G_0^\dagger WG_0$. Interior factors cancel. This algebra explains both spectral gauge invariance and the need for closure. Actual Bloch bases can require a reciprocal-lattice sewing operator and orbital-position information instead of a naive endpoint identification. A different orbital embedding is not automatically a harmless gauge rotation within the same physical projector. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271)

Finite-step overlaps are generally not unitary. For $M_j=V_j\Sigma_j Z_j^\dagger$, use its polar unitary factor $Q_j=V_jZ_j^\dagger$ when the overlap is nonsingular. This construction preserves gauge covariance and yields a unitary discrete product. Record the smallest singular values, subspace dimension, direct gap and mesh convergence. Polar projection cannot repair a singular overlap, an incorrectly selected subspace or an unresolved band touching. [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

An independent rank-two example combines spinors $(\cos(\vartheta/2),e^{iwt}\sin(\vartheta/2))$ in separate two-dimensional blocks. Their analytic forward phases are $2\pi w\sin^2(\vartheta/2)$ modulo $2\pi$. Meshes of 32, 64 and 128 points approach these phases while raw-product eigenvalue magnitudes remain below one. Random $U(2)$ frame rotations, shifted basepoints and reversed paths pass the covariance and conjugation checks. Omitting the closing link deliberately breaks spectral gauge invariance. These are synthetic checks, not a material calculation. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90)

For an increasing-$k_x$ loop and positive $(k_x,k_y)$ orientation, the continuously unwrapped phase $\Theta(k_y)=\arg\det W(k_y)$ winds by $2\pi C$ as $k_y$ traverses its period in this convention. Four lower-band examples of $h=(\sin k_x,\sin k_y,m+\cos k_x+\cos k_y)\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma$ give $C=0,+1,-1,0$ at $m=-3,-1,+1,+3$. Three meshes agree with separate analytic-curvature quadratures, and reversing the loop reverses the sign. The critical masses $-2,0,2$ have explicit gap zeros and are rejected. Integer output alone is not a convergence certificate. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

## Experimental criteria

In a two-dimensional band insulator with time reversal satisfying $\mathcal T^2=-1$, the parity of Kramers-partner exchange over half the transverse Brillouin zone diagnoses the $\mathbb Z_2$ class. Preserve the complete occupied projector, the bulk gap and symmetry constraints. Sorting principal phases independently at every point can invent discontinuities at a branch cut; follow spectral connectivity or a validated gap-tracking procedure. The local checks above do not implement or certify a general $\mathbb Z_2$ classifier. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90)

For a single band with the stated Bloch convention, a hybrid center satisfies $\bar x/a=\gamma/(2\pi)=-\arg W/(2\pi)$ modulo one. In multiple bands, Wilson eigenphases correspond to centers in the appropriate parallel-transport or maximally localized hybrid construction, not arbitrary individual Wannier functions. Physical electronic polarization also needs electron charge, occupations, cell volume and a consistent origin; total polarization includes ionic contributions. Insulating adiabatic changes can be meaningful while an absolute branch remains ambiguous by a polarization quantum. A BdG phase spectrum cannot simply be substituted into the ordinary electron-polarization formula. [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

An experimental comparison needs an explicit map from the measured observable to the modeled projector, including sample state, orbital basis, energy window and relevant symmetry. Band inversion, a calculated loop or an isolated boundary feature does not by itself verify the full pairing state. No experimental transition temperature or material certification is assigned to the synthetic examples on this page. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

## Limits and disputes

An isolated band manifold can have a well-defined Wilson loop even when a material is metallic. Its invariant is then not automatically the invariant of all physically occupied states: a Fermi surface makes that projector change rank. Likewise, band disentanglement selects a model subspace whose validity needs separate evidence. For BdG systems, respect particle-hole and time-reversal constraints and avoid interpreting Nambu duplication as independent electron occupations. Strong interactions, disorder and nodal systems can require different formulations. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0) [R6](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

Complete scientific acceptance remains open. Selected author and published passages, two original polarization pages and independent numerical examples have been checked. The full Yu equivalence proof, full Zak derivation, final-version comparisons, realistic orbital sewing, material fits and a general time-reversal classifier have not been reproduced. The numerical checks certify only the stated bounded constructions. [R1](#ref-source-9302d42436e83c82) [R2](#ref-source-fd30087dfafb8d90) [R3](#ref-source-f3affc7c4f9e1271) [R4](#ref-source-50b4c7274c53cf48)

## Discovery implications

Archive the Hamiltonian or projector, basis and embedding, symmetry operators, loop orientation, sewing rule and phase convention with every topology claim. Keep raw singular values and mesh history alongside the plotted spectrum. Compare a simple limit with an independent curvature or symmetry calculation before interpreting a complicated model. This makes a Wilson-loop result a reproducible hypothesis about a specified system rather than an unsupported label attached to a candidate superconductor. A Wilson loop describes transport around a closed path within a specified band subspace. Its eigenvalues survive unitary changes of basis inside that subspace; individual matrix entries do not. claims.statement: For an isolated normalized Bloch state, use $A_i=i\langle u|\partial_i u\rangle$ and $\Omega_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i=-2\mathrm{Im}\,Q_{ij}$. Under $u\rightarrow e^{i\phi}u$, the connection changes as $A_i\rightarrow A_i-\partial_i\phi$, while curvature is unchanged. The closed-loop phase $\gamma=\oint A_i dk_i$ is defined modulo $2\pi$. In a smooth patch, Stokes' theorem relates it to the curvature flux. Nontrivial bundles can require multiple patches and transition functions; a globally smooth eigenvector should not be assumed.

claims.statement: For a nondegenerate eigenstate of $H$, differentiating the eigenvalue equation gives $\langle m|\partial_i n\rangle=\langle m|\partial_iH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)$ for $m\ne n$. Consequently $\Omega_{n,ij}=-2\mathrm{Im}\sum_{m\ne n}\langle n|\partial_iH|m\rangle\langle m|\partial_jH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)^2$. Small denominators require resolving the neighboring bands and the validity of the isolated-band approximation. Exactly degenerate states require a subspace treatment, not arbitrary assignments to individual eigenvectors. Wilczek–Zee supplies the historical non-Abelian extension; its full derivation is not audited here.

claims.statement: With electron charge $-e$, $e>0$, and zero magnetic field, the weak-field semiclassical equations are $\hbar\dot{\mathbf k}=-e\mathbf E$ and $\dot{\mathbf r}=\hbar^{-1}\nabla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon-\dot{\mathbf k}\times\boldsymbol\Omega$. For the clean intrinsic response, $\sigma_{xy}^{\rm int}=-(e^2/\hbar)\sum_n\int d^dk\,f_n\Omega_{n,xy}/(2\pi)^d$, with $j_x=\sigma_{xy}E_y$. The two-dimensional quantity is a sheet conductance; in three dimensions it has conductivity units. Haldane's checked manuscript uses the opposite connection sign, so its curvature and displayed Hall sign must be translated together.

claims.statement: For a gapped two-dimensional occupied subspace, $C=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\rm BZ}\mathrm{Tr}\,\Omega_{xy}\,d^2k$ is an integer under the stated orientation. articles.body:
## Scope

Berry curvature describes local geometric twisting of a quantum-state family in parameter space. In a crystal, momentum-space curvature can contribute to electronic transport, but curvature, anomalous Hall conductivity and superconducting chirality are different objects. Specify whether the states belong to a normal-state Hamiltonian, a Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian or a selected degenerate subspace before drawing a topological conclusion. Berry's original construction separates geometric and dynamical phases during adiabatic evolution. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47)

The inherited chapter includes the Xiao–Chang–Niu and Nagaosa reviews as broader reading. Here the defining phase equations are checked against Berry's original paper, semiclassical motion against Sundaram–Niu, and the metallic Hall interpretation against Haldane. Review citations are not substitutes for a completed audit of every underlying experiment. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R2](#ref-source-fcaa37740551d83d) [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R4](#ref-source-7faba5d556864a32) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207)

## Mathematical assumptions

For an isolated normalized Bloch state, use $A_i=i\langle u|\partial_i u\rangle$ and $\Omega_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i=-2\mathrm{Im}\,Q_{ij}$. Under $u\rightarrow e^{i\phi}u$, the connection changes as $A_i\rightarrow A_i-\partial_i\phi$, while curvature is unchanged. The closed-loop phase $\gamma=\oint A_i dk_i$ is defined modulo $2\pi$. In a smooth patch, Stokes' theorem relates it to the curvature flux. Nontrivial bundles can require multiple patches and transition functions; a globally smooth eigenvector should not be assumed. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47)

For a nondegenerate eigenstate of $H$, differentiating the eigenvalue equation gives $\langle m|\partial_i n\rangle=\langle m|\partial_iH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)$ for $m\ne n$. Consequently $\Omega_{n,ij}=-2\mathrm{Im}\sum_{m\ne n}\langle n|\partial_iH|m\rangle\langle m|\partial_jH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)^2$. Small denominators require resolving the neighboring bands and the validity of the isolated-band approximation. Exactly degenerate states require a subspace treatment, not arbitrary assignments to individual eigenvectors. Wilczek–Zee supplies the historical non-Abelian extension; its full derivation is not audited here. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R8](#ref-source-0eb769764cf8ed2a)

With electron charge $-e$, $e>0$, and zero magnetic field, the weak-field semiclassical equations are $\hbar\dot{\mathbf k}=-e\mathbf E$ and $\dot{\mathbf r}=\hbar^{-1}\nabla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon-\dot{\mathbf k}\times\boldsymbol\Omega$. For the clean intrinsic response, $\sigma_{xy}^{\rm int}=-(e^2/\hbar)\sum_n\int d^dk\,f_n\Omega_{n,xy}/(2\pi)^d$, with $j_x=\sigma_{xy}E_y$. The two-dimensional quantity is a sheet conductance; in three dimensions it has conductivity units. Haldane's checked manuscript uses the opposite connection sign, so its curvature and displayed Hall sign must be translated together. [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207)

For a gapped two-dimensional occupied subspace, $C=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\rm BZ}\mathrm{Tr}\,\Omega_{xy}\,d^2k$ is an integer under the stated orientation. The corresponding clean filled-band result in this convention is $\sigma_{xy}=-Ce^2/h$. A metal can still contain an isolated band with an integer band Chern number; its partially occupied curvature integral is generally not that integer. Haldane expresses the nonquantized metallic contribution through Fermi-surface Berry phases, retaining a quantized ambiguity and Brillouin-zone boundary terms. It is not a license to discard all filled-band contributions. [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47)

As a bounded check, the spinor $u=(\cos(\theta/2),e^{i\varphi}\sin(\theta/2))$ taken around increasing $\varphi$ at fixed $\theta$ gives $\gamma=-\pi(1-\cos\theta)$ modulo $2\pi$. We compare cyclic overlap products with an independently integrated curvature flux, reverse the loop orientation and apply phase changes at every point. The energy-denominator formula and Hall-current sign are checked separately. These calculations validate conventions in a model, not a material's measured topology. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207)

## Experimental criteria

An anomalous Hall measurement is not a unique image of a curvature hotspot. Onoda and colleagues' original impurity-transport study distinguishes skew-scattering and intrinsic regimes within its dilute-impurity approximation; that is not a universal material-independent scaling law. Separate magnetic state, occupation, disorder and the conductivity-to-resistivity conversion before fitting a mechanism. A finite normal-state Hall signal does not determine the topology of a superconducting gap. [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R7](#ref-source-eb48700c5a38e363)

Mielke and colleagues studied KV₃Sb₅ using muon spin relaxation. The checked author manuscript finds enhanced relaxation around the approximately 80 K charge-order scale, while the selected zero-field relaxation stays approximately constant through the separate superconducting transition. It explicitly notes that zero-field results alone cannot establish the time-reversal-breaking interpretation because charge order can modify nuclear electric-field gradients. Longitudinal-field and higher-field controls form part of the argument. This is evidence about the charge-ordered material, not a direct reconstruction of Berry curvature or a demonstration of chiral superconductivity. The 80 K record is excluded from superconducting-temperature search. [R5](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3)

## Limits and disputes

Time reversal relates the curvature of symmetry-partner states with opposite sign at opposite momenta; inversion relates the corresponding curvature with the same sign. For spinful systems with both symmetries, treat the Kramers subspace appropriately. Cancellation of charge Hall response does not imply that all spin, valley or non-Abelian structure is trivial. Likewise, broken time reversal alone does not guarantee a nonzero measured Hall component: other symmetries or cancellations can forbid it. [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207) [R8](#ref-source-0eb769764cf8ed2a)

This review visually checks Berry's original pages 46–47 and Haldane author v5 page 1, and reads selected Haldane, Sundaram–Niu and Mielke passages. The Haldane author copy prints an apparent repeated-momentum typo in its time-reversal equation; the transformation stated here follows the consistent symmetry argument rather than that literal expression. Full journal comparisons, non-Abelian derivations, disorder calculations and raw-data review remain open. Complete scientific acceptance has not been reached. [R1](#ref-source-f93105756c21da04) [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R5](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207) [R7](#ref-source-eb48700c5a38e363) [R8](#ref-source-0eb769764cf8ed2a)

## Discovery implications

Use curvature maps together with band gaps, occupation and symmetry, and test response predictions against independent measurements. For superconducting topology, calculate the appropriate gapped BdG subspace and compare relevant boundary or thermal probes. Keep a charge-order signal, normal-state anomalous Hall effect and a new symmetry change below the superconducting transition as separate claims. A promising normal-state band structure is an input to this analysis, not its conclusion. [R3](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47) [R5](#ref-source-484da7abcc165cd3)

## Related topics

Compare [quantum metric](/scwiki/quantum-metric), [chiral pairing](/scwiki/chiral-pairing), [topological pairing](/scwiki/topological-superconductivity) and [geometric superfluid weight](/scwiki/geometric-superfluid-weight).

## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-f2-claim-scope-1

Berry curvature describes local geometric twisting of a quantum-state family in parameter space. In a crystal, momentum-space curvature can contribute to electronic transport, but curvature, anomalous Hall conductivity and superconducting chirality are different objects. Specify whether the states belong to a normal-state Hamiltonian, a Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian or a selected degenerate subspace before drawing a topological conclusion. Berry's original construction separates geometric and dynamical phases during adiabatic evolution.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f93105756c21da04, source-381ad96944c0fa47.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-scope-2

The inherited chapter includes the Xiao–Chang–Niu and Nagaosa reviews as broader reading. Here the defining phase equations are checked against Berry's original paper, semiclassical motion against Sundaram–Niu, and the metallic Hall interpretation against Haldane. Review citations are not substitutes for a completed audit of every underlying experiment.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f93105756c21da04, source-fcaa37740551d83d, source-381ad96944c0fa47, source-7faba5d556864a32, source-113ed6da444bd207.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

For an isolated normalized Bloch state, use $A_i=i\langle u|\partial_i u\rangle$ and $\Omega_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i=-2\mathrm{Im}\,Q_{ij}$. Under $u\rightarrow e^{i\phi}u$, the connection changes as $A_i\rightarrow A_i-\partial_i\phi$, while curvature is unchanged. The closed-loop phase $\gamma=\oint A_i dk_i$ is defined modulo $2\pi$. In a smooth patch, Stokes' theorem relates it to the curvature flux. Nontrivial bundles can require multiple patches and transition functions; a globally smooth eigenvector should not be assumed.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f93105756c21da04, source-381ad96944c0fa47.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

For a nondegenerate eigenstate of $H$, differentiating the eigenvalue equation gives $\langle m|\partial_i n\rangle=\langle m|\partial_iH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)$ for $m\ne n$. Consequently $\Omega_{n,ij}=-2\mathrm{Im}\sum_{m\ne n}\langle n|\partial_iH|m\rangle\langle m|\partial_jH|n\rangle/(E_n-E_m)^2$. Small denominators require resolving the neighboring bands and the validity of the isolated-band approximation. Exactly degenerate states require a subspace treatment, not arbitrary assignments to individual eigenvectors. Wilczek–Zee supplies the historical non-Abelian extension; its full derivation is not audited here.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f93105756c21da04, source-0eb769764cf8ed2a.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

With electron charge $-e$, $e>0$, and zero magnetic field, the weak-field semiclassical equations are $\hbar\dot{\mathbf k}=-e\mathbf E$ and $\dot{\mathbf r}=\hbar^{-1}\nabla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon-\dot{\mathbf k}\times\boldsymbol\Omega$. For the clean intrinsic response, $\sigma_{xy}^{\rm int}=-(e^2/\hbar)\sum_n\int d^dk\,f_n\Omega_{n,xy}/(2\pi)^d$, with $j_x=\sigma_{xy}E_y$. The two-dimensional quantity is a sheet conductance; in three dimensions it has conductivity units. Haldane's checked manuscript uses the opposite connection sign, so its curvature and displayed Hall sign must be translated together.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-381ad96944c0fa47, source-113ed6da444bd207.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-mathematical-assumptions-4

For a gapped two-dimensional occupied subspace, $C=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\rm BZ}\mathrm{Tr}\,\Omega_{xy}\,d^2k$ is an integer under the stated orientation. The corresponding clean filled-band result in this convention is $\sigma_{xy}=-Ce^2/h$. A metal can still contain an isolated band with an integer band Chern number; its partially occupied curvature integral is generally not that integer. Haldane expresses the nonquantized metallic contribution through Fermi-surface Berry phases, retaining a quantized ambiguity and Brillouin-zone boundary terms. It is not a license to discard all filled-band contributions.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-381ad96944c0fa47.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-mathematical-assumptions-5

As a bounded check, the spinor $u=(\cos(\theta/2),e^{i\varphi}\sin(\theta/2))$ taken around increasing $\varphi$ at fixed $\theta$ gives $\gamma=-\pi(1-\cos\theta)$ modulo $2\pi$. We compare cyclic overlap products with an independently integrated curvature flux, reverse the loop orientation and apply phase changes at every point. The energy-denominator formula and Hall-current sign are checked separately. These calculations validate conventions in a model, not a material's measured topology.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-f93105756c21da04, source-113ed6da444bd207.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-experimental-criteria-1

An anomalous Hall measurement is not a unique image of a curvature hotspot. Onoda and colleagues' original impurity-transport study distinguishes skew-scattering and intrinsic regimes within its dilute-impurity approximation; that is not a universal material-independent scaling law. Separate magnetic state, occupation, disorder and the conductivity-to-resistivity conversion before fitting a mechanism. A finite normal-state Hall signal does not determine the topology of a superconducting gap.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-381ad96944c0fa47, source-eb48700c5a38e363.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Mielke and colleagues studied KV₃Sb₅ using muon spin relaxation. The checked author manuscript finds enhanced relaxation around the approximately 80 K charge-order scale, while the selected zero-field relaxation stays approximately constant through the separate superconducting transition. It explicitly notes that zero-field results alone cannot establish the time-reversal-breaking interpretation because charge order can modify nuclear electric-field gradients. Longitudinal-field and higher-field controls form part of the argument. This is evidence about the charge-ordered material, not a direct reconstruction of Berry curvature or a demonstration of chiral superconductivity. The 80 K record is excluded from superconducting-temperature search.

Evidence: experiment. Sources: source-484da7abcc165cd3.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

Verification scope: Selected primary equations and experimental passages; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f2-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

Time reversal relates the curvature of symmetry-partner states with opposite sign at opposite momenta; inversion relates the corresponding curvature with the same sign. For spinful systems with both symmetries, treat the Kramers subspace appropriately. Cancellation of charge Hall response does not imply that all spin, valley or non-Abelian structure is trivial. Likewise, broken time reversal alone does not guarantee a nonzero measured Hall component: other symmetries or cancellations can forbid it.

Conditions: Explicit curvature sign, electron charge, coordinates, dimensional units, isolated-band/subspace conditions and normal-state versus superconducting evidence.

### scwiki-f2-claim-limits-and-disputes-2

This review visually checks Berry's original pages 46–47 and Haldane author v5 page 1, and reads selected Haldane, Sundaram–Niu and Mielke passages. Use curvature maps together with band gaps, occupation and symmetry, and test response predictions against independent measurements. For superconducting topology, calculate the appropriate gapped BdG subspace and compare relevant boundary or thermal probes. Keep a charge-order signal, normal-state anomalous Hall effect and a new symmetry change below the superconducting transition as separate claims. A promising normal-state band structure is an input to this analysis, not its conclusion.

articles.body:
## Scope

A Chern number characterizes a smooth, isolated family of quantum subspaces over a closed two-dimensional parameter surface. In a periodic crystal that surface can be the Brillouin-zone torus. The normal-state occupied-electron subspace and the negative-energy Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) subspace are different constructions: calculate and label them separately. Local Berry curvature, an integer band invariant and an observed transport coefficient should not be used interchangeably. [R1](#ref-source-5052964ec3dcf748) [R4](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a) [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

The TKNN work connects a gap in a two-dimensional electron problem to quantized Hall conductance. Haldane's later lattice model shows that Landau levels are not required for a nonzero quantized Hall response. These are foundational model results, not evidence that a normal-state Chern band necessarily becomes a topological superconductor. Here their original publisher abstracts establish this historical context; complete original-paper audits remain open. [R1](#ref-source-5052964ec3dcf748) [R2](#ref-source-9b742057f40ad284)

## Mathematical assumptions

Use the convention of the [Berry-curvature article](/scwiki/berry-curvature): $\mathcal A_i=i\Psi^\dagger\partial_i\Psi$ for an orthonormal frame of the selected subspace, $\mathcal F_{xy}=\partial_x\mathcal A_y-\partial_y\mathcal A_x-i[\mathcal A_x,\mathcal A_y]$, and $C=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\rm BZ}\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal F_{xy}\,d^2k$. The subspace must remain separated from its complement throughout the Brillouin zone. Degeneracies inside the selected multiplet do not invalidate its total invariant, but arbitrary individual-band assignments at those degeneracies can fail. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

A nonzero invariant obstructs a single globally smooth periodic frame. One uses compatible local frames or a gauge-invariant discrete construction. For a continuous deformation that preserves the subspace gap and the closed integration surface, the integer cannot change. This is a statement about the quantum-state bundle, not an identification of momentum-space Berry curvature with the Gaussian curvature of a physical surface. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

For the clean, zero-temperature filled-electron-band response, with electron charge $-e$, $e>0$, positive $(k_x,k_y)$ orientation and $j_x=\sigma_{xy}E_y$, the convention used here gives $\sigma_{xy}=-Ce^2/h$. This sign follows the anomalous velocity and charge current used in F2; reversing orientation or the curvature definition changes the displayed relation. A partially occupied metallic band need not give an integer Hall response even when its complete band has an integer Chern number. Do not apply this electron charge-transport formula to a BdG integer without deriving the appropriate physical response. [R1](#ref-source-5052964ec3dcf748) [R4](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207) [R7](#ref-source-381ad96944c0fa47)

For a bounded numerical example, take $H=\sin k_x\,\sigma_x+\sin k_y\,\sigma_y+(m+\cos k_x+\cos k_y)\sigma_z$, with dimensionless momenta and a fixed energy unit. The lower-band curvature is $\Omega_{xy}=\mathbf d\cdot(\partial_x\mathbf d\times\partial_y\mathbf d)/(2|\mathbf d|^3)$ in our convention. Analytic gap zeros occur only at $m=-2,0,2$. The lower-band values at $m=-3,-1,1,3$ are respectively $0,1,-1,0$. These are illustrative Hamiltonian results, not measured material properties. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0) [R6](#ref-source-113ed6da444bd207)

We compare normalized-overlap lattice sums on $12^2$, $24^2$ and $48^2$ meshes against an independently integrated analytic curvature on $64^2$ and $128^2$ meshes. Pointwise phase changes leave the result unchanged; reversing one momentum direction reverses its sign. We also reject the analytically identified gap-closing points. A positive gap sampled on a finite grid alone would not exclude an unsampled closing in a general Hamiltonian. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

## Experimental criteria

For a normal-state Hall interpretation, identify the carrier subspace, occupation, bulk gap and response convention. Hatsugai's original work relates the bulk TKNN integer to edge-state winding for a square-lattice quantum Hall model. ## Mathematical assumptions

Use the convention of the [Berry-curvature article](/scwiki/berry-curvature): $\mathcal A_i=i\Psi^\dagger\partial_i\Psi$ for an orthonormal frame of the selected subspace, $\mathcal F_{xy}=\partial_x\mathcal A_y-\partial_y\mathcal A_x-i[\mathcal A_x,\mathcal A_y]$, and $C=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\rm BZ}\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal F_{xy}\,d^2k$. The subspace must remain separated from its complement throughout the Brillouin zone. Degeneracies inside the selected multiplet do not invalidate its total invariant, but arbitrary individual-band assignments at those degeneracies can fail. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

A nonzero invariant obstructs a single globally smooth periodic frame. One uses compatible local frames or a gauge-invariant discrete construction. For a continuous deformation that preserves the subspace gap and the closed integration surface, the integer cannot change. This is a statement about the quantum-state bundle, not an identification of momentum-space Berry curvature with the Gaussian curvature of a physical surface. [R5](#ref-source-688ad98fc33198c0)

For the clean, zero-temperature filled-electron-band response, with electron charge $-e$, $e>0$, positive $(k_x,k_y)$ orientation and $j_x=\sigma_{xy}E_y$, the convention used here gives $\sigma_{xy}=-Ce^2/h$. This sign follows the anomalous velocity and charge current used in F2; reversing orientation or the curvature definition changes the displayed relation. We compare normalized-overlap lattice sums on $12^2$, $24^2$ and $48^2$ meshes against an independently integrated analytic curvature on $64^2$ and $128^2$ meshes. Pointwise phase changes leave the result unchanged; reversing one momentum direction reverses its sign. We also reject the analytically identified gap-closing points. articles.body:
## Scope

Class DIII describes a gapped Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian with time-reversal and particle–hole symmetries whose single-particle antiunitary operators square to $-1$ and $+1$, respectively. It is a symmetry class, not a pairing mechanism or a certificate that a particular material is topological. Dimension, the bulk gap and the allowed perturbations must be specified before assigning an invariant. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

For the stable, noninteracting strong classification, DIII has $\mathbb Z_2$ sectors in one and two spatial dimensions and an integer $\mathbb Z$ classification in three. By comparison, class D has $\mathbb Z_2$, $\mathbb Z$ and a trivial strong classification in dimensions one, two and three. Extra crystalline or translation symmetries can introduce further distinctions; the simple table does not enumerate those. In particular, “2D DIII is trivial” and “3D DIII has only a binary invariant” are incorrect statements of this free-fermion classification. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

## Mathematical assumptions

Write $T=U_TK$ and $C=U_CK$, where $K$ is complex conjugation. The requirements are $U_TH(\mathbf k)^*U_T^\dagger=H(-\mathbf k)$, $U_CH(\mathbf k)^*U_C^\dagger=-H(-\mathbf k)$, $U_TU_T^*=-I$ and $U_CU_C^*=I$. A suitably phased product of the two antiunitary operations gives a unitary chiral symmetry that anticommutes with $H$. Merely checking the ordinary matrix squares $U_T^2$ and $U_C^2$ would miss the conjugation in the antiunitary operation. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

An explicit illustrative lattice model in the basis $(c_\uparrow,c_\downarrow,c_\uparrow^\dagger,c_\downarrow^\dagger)$ is $H=\xi\tau_z\otimes I+\sin k_x\,\tau_x\otimes\sigma_z+\sin k_y\,\tau_y\otimes I$, with $\xi=m+\cos k_x+\cos k_y$. Here $U_T=I\otimes i\sigma_y$, $U_C=\tau_x\otimes I$, and a Hermitian chiral operator is $\tau_x\otimes\sigma_y$. Its squared spectrum is $E^2=\xi^2+\sin^2k_x+\sin^2k_y$. Sixteen selected parameter/momentum points pass Hermiticity, both antiunitary relations, chiral anticommutation and this spectral identity. These checks establish the stated model relations, not a general classification proof or a material realization. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

The boundary distinction can be seen in a Majorana edge basis. For one helical pair, take $h(k)=vk\sigma_z$, $T=i\sigma_yK$ and $C=K$. A constant mass $m_e\sigma_y$ anticommutes with the velocity and preserves particle–hole symmetry but is time-reversal odd. For two copies, $h=vk\sigma_z\otimes I$ admits the time-reversal-even mass $m_e\sigma_x\otimes\rho_y$, where $\rho$ acts on the copies; its spectrum obeys $E^2=v^2k^2+m_e^2$. This bounded calculation illustrates an even–odd distinction. It does not cover arbitrary interactions or a self-consistent microscopic edge. [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

In three dimensions the free-fermion invariant is an integer winding number. The odd-parity criterion of Fu and Berg instead determines its parity, $\nu=n\bmod2$. Their sufficient criterion assumes a fully gapped, time-reversal-invariant, centrosymmetric odd-parity superconductor. The simple Fermi-surface reduction is made in a weak-pairing setting with normal bands at time-reversal-invariant momenta separated from the Fermi energy. An odd enclosed count establishes odd parity under those assumptions; an even count does not establish that the integer is zero. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441)

## Experimental criteria

The Balian–Werthamer description of superfluid helium-3 B is a three-dimensional DIII prototype with unit winding in the convention of the checked classification paper. It is an atomic superfluid, not a solid superconducting device. A surface-state model and a particular experimental signal are different levels of evidence; this article does not independently review helium-3 surface spectroscopy or assign a pressure-independent transition temperature. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

Fu and Berg's application to copper-intercalated Bi₂Se₃ is a two-orbital pairing model and a proposed route to test odd parity. It does not by itself settle a specimen's pairing symmetry, gap or topology. For any solid candidate, establish time-reversal behavior and the bulk quasiparticle gap, evaluate a justified invariant or sufficient criterion, and compare the predicted boundary response with measurements that address competing explanations. A zero-bias feature alone does not complete this sequence. [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441)

Qi and colleagues' paired Majorana defect construction concerns a time-reversal-invariant defect: in their equal-spin example, a vortex in one component coincides with an antivortex in the other. Do not transfer that conclusion automatically to an ordinary magnetic vortex, which breaks time reversal. The paper's boundary construction and protected Kramers structure also should not be read as experimental evidence of braiding or of a completed topological qubit. [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

## Limits and disputes

The free-fermion table and an interacting many-body classification are distinct. Fidkowski, Chen and Vishwanath discuss symmetric gapped surfaces with topological order. The later Metlitski and colleagues preprint explicitly analyzes the interaction reduction to $\mathbb Z_{16}$, focusing on even-index surfaces. That is not a replacement of the three-dimensional free-fermion integer by a universal $\mathbb Z_2$ label. In the many-body discussion time reversal squares to fermion parity; the single-particle $T^2=-1$ statement must be interpreted at the appropriate level. [R4](#ref-source-acd86eaeefff7bad) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

We visually checked the DIII classification row, read selected original author passages on helical boundaries and odd-parity conditions, and performed explicit small-matrix checks. Full journal-version comparisons, the interacting surface construction and material-specific evidence audits remain open. Complete scientific acceptance has not been reached. The 2014 interaction source is labelled as a preprint; its presence in the bibliography is not a claim that its full proof has been reproduced. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

## Discovery implications

Use DIII as a conditional classification after identifying the physical symmetries and a gapped BdG description. State whether a result is a full integer, its parity or a boundary-model prediction. Report what changes when time reversal is broken, when the gap closes, or when additional symmetries or strong interactions are included. This keeps a useful theoretical criterion separate from an experimentally established material property. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

## Related topics

Compare [Chern number](/scwiki/chern-number), [topological superconductivity](/scwiki/topological-superconductivity), [chiral pairing](/scwiki/chiral-pairing) and [Berry curvature](/scwiki/berry-curvature).

## Scope

Class DIII describes a gapped Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian with time-reversal and particle–hole symmetries whose single-particle antiunitary operators square to $-1$ and $+1$, respectively. It is a symmetry class, not a pairing mechanism or a certificate that a particular material is topological. Dimension, the bulk gap and the allowed perturbations must be specified before assigning an invariant. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

For the stable, noninteracting strong classification, DIII has $\mathbb Z_2$ sectors in one and two spatial dimensions and an integer $\mathbb Z$ classification in three. By comparison, class D has $\mathbb Z_2$, $\mathbb Z$ and a trivial strong classification in dimensions one, two and three. Extra crystalline or translation symmetries can introduce further distinctions; the simple table does not enumerate those. In particular, “2D DIII is trivial” and “3D DIII has only a binary invariant” are incorrect statements of this free-fermion classification. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

## Mathematical assumptions

Write $T=U_TK$ and $C=U_CK$, where $K$ is complex conjugation. The requirements are $U_TH(\mathbf k)^*U_T^\dagger=H(-\mathbf k)$, $U_CH(\mathbf k)^*U_C^\dagger=-H(-\mathbf k)$, $U_TU_T^*=-I$ and $U_CU_C^*=I$. A suitably phased product of the two antiunitary operations gives a unitary chiral symmetry that anticommutes with $H$. Merely checking the ordinary matrix squares $U_T^2$ and $U_C^2$ would miss the conjugation in the antiunitary operation. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace)

An explicit illustrative lattice model in the basis $(c_\uparrow,c_\downarrow,c_\uparrow^\dagger,c_\downarrow^\dagger)$ is $H=\xi\tau_z\otimes I+\sin k_x\,\tau_x\otimes\sigma_z+\sin k_y\,\tau_y\otimes I$, with $\xi=m+\cos k_x+\cos k_y$. Here $U_T=I\otimes i\sigma_y$, $U_C=\tau_x\otimes I$, and a Hermitian chiral operator is $\tau_x\otimes\sigma_y$. Its squared spectrum is $E^2=\xi^2+\sin^2k_x+\sin^2k_y$. Sixteen selected parameter/momentum points pass Hermiticity, both antiunitary relations, chiral anticommutation and this spectral identity. These checks establish the stated model relations, not a general classification proof or a material realization. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

The boundary distinction can be seen in a Majorana edge basis. For one helical pair, take $h(k)=vk\sigma_z$, $T=i\sigma_yK$ and $C=K$. A constant mass $m_e\sigma_y$ anticommutes with the velocity and preserves particle–hole symmetry but is time-reversal odd. For two copies, $h=vk\sigma_z\otimes I$ admits the time-reversal-even mass $m_e\sigma_x\otimes\rho_y$, where $\rho$ acts on the copies; its spectrum obeys $E^2=v^2k^2+m_e^2$. This bounded calculation illustrates an even–odd distinction. It does not cover arbitrary interactions or a self-consistent microscopic edge. [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

In three dimensions the free-fermion invariant is an integer winding number. The odd-parity criterion of Fu and Berg instead determines its parity, $\nu=n\bmod2$. Their sufficient criterion assumes a fully gapped, time-reversal-invariant, centrosymmetric odd-parity superconductor. The simple Fermi-surface reduction is made in a weak-pairing setting with normal bands at time-reversal-invariant momenta separated from the Fermi energy. An odd enclosed count establishes odd parity under those assumptions; an even count does not establish that the integer is zero. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441)

## Experimental criteria

The Balian–Werthamer description of superfluid helium-3 B is a three-dimensional DIII prototype with unit winding in the convention of the checked classification paper. It is an atomic superfluid, not a solid superconducting device. A surface-state model and a particular experimental signal are different levels of evidence; this article does not independently review helium-3 surface spectroscopy or assign a pressure-independent transition temperature. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

Fu and Berg's application to copper-intercalated Bi₂Se₃ is a two-orbital pairing model and a proposed route to test odd parity. It does not by itself settle a specimen's pairing symmetry, gap or topology. For any solid candidate, establish time-reversal behavior and the bulk quasiparticle gap, evaluate a justified invariant or sufficient criterion, and compare the predicted boundary response with measurements that address competing explanations. A zero-bias feature alone does not complete this sequence. [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441)

Qi and colleagues' paired Majorana defect construction concerns a time-reversal-invariant defect: in their equal-spin example, a vortex in one component coincides with an antivortex in the other. Do not transfer that conclusion automatically to an ordinary magnetic vortex, which breaks time reversal. The paper's boundary construction and protected Kramers structure also should not be read as experimental evidence of braiding or of a completed topological qubit. [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf)

## Limits and disputes

The free-fermion table and an interacting many-body classification are distinct. Fidkowski, Chen and Vishwanath discuss symmetric gapped surfaces with topological order. The later Metlitski and colleagues preprint explicitly analyzes the interaction reduction to $\mathbb Z_{16}$, focusing on even-index surfaces. That is not a replacement of the three-dimensional free-fermion integer by a universal $\mathbb Z_2$ label. In the many-body discussion time reversal squares to fermion parity; the single-particle $T^2=-1$ statement must be interpreted at the appropriate level. [R4](#ref-source-acd86eaeefff7bad) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

We visually checked the DIII classification row, read selected original author passages on helical boundaries and odd-parity conditions, and performed explicit small-matrix checks. Full journal-version comparisons, the interacting surface construction and material-specific evidence audits remain open. Complete scientific acceptance has not been reached. The 2014 interaction source is labelled as a preprint; its presence in the bibliography is not a claim that its full proof has been reproduced. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R2](#ref-source-5eb9e7b0c0c3b0cf) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

## Discovery implications

Use DIII as a conditional classification after identifying the physical symmetries and a gapped BdG description. State whether a result is a full integer, its parity or a boundary-model prediction. Report what changes when time reversal is broken, when the gap closes, or when additional symmetries or strong interactions are included. This keeps a useful theoretical criterion separate from an experimentally established material property. [R1](#ref-source-37986d2488e4cace) [R3](#ref-source-4e92d11d59fb3441) [R5](#ref-source-1555be5a67a1d730)

claims.statement: A Majorana operator is self-adjoint. A Majorana zero mode additionally represents a zero-energy degree of freedom of a specified Hamiltonian, localized at an end, boundary or defect in an appropriate setting. Decomposing an ordinary fermion into two self-adjoint operators is always possible; that algebra alone establishes neither spatial separation nor topological protection. Here the ideal chain, experimental readout and claims about fault-tolerant computation are treated separately.

claims.statement: Fix the normalization $\{\gamma_i,\gamma_j\}=2\delta_{ij}$ and $\gamma_i^\dagger=\gamma_i$. Then $c=(\gamma_1+i\gamma_2)/2$, $n=c^\dagger c=(1+i\gamma_1\gamma_2)/2$ and the occupation parity is $P=(-1)^n=1-2n=-i\gamma_1\gamma_2$. Papers may normalize the operators or label parity signs differently. Mixing a factor $1/\sqrt2$ from another convention into these equations would spoil the fermionic anticommutator.

claims.statement: For a uniform spinless chain, use hopping $t$, chemical potential $\mu$, real pairing $\Delta$, lattice spacing one and open ends. The bulk excitation spectrum satisfies $E(k)^2=(2t\cos k+\mu)^2+4\Delta^2\sin^2k$. The gapped topological domain is $|\mu|<2|t|$ with $\Delta\ne0$; $|\mu|=2|t|$ closes the gap. At $\mu=0$ and $t=\Delta>0$, the ideal finite chain has exactly unpaired endpoint operators. More general finite chains can have overlap splitting: exponential localization does not imply exactly zero energy at every length.

claims.statement: The minimal two-site model makes a useful distinction explicit. With $\delta=(\mu_L+\mu_R)/2$ and $\epsilon=(\mu_L-\mu_R)/2$, its even and odd energies are $E_e^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\delta^2+\Delta^2}$ and $E_o^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\epsilon^2+t^2}$. At $t=\Delta$ and zero onsite energies the ground states coincide. Detuning one site leaves this ideal degeneracy intact, whereas common detuning gives a quadratic splitting and changing $t-\Delta$ gives a linear one. Direct four-state diagonalization checks these relations; they explain why a two-site sweet spot is not equivalent to generic long-chain protection.

articles.body:
## Scope

A Majorana operator is self-adjoint. A Majorana zero mode additionally represents a zero-energy degree of freedom of a specified Hamiltonian, localized at an end, boundary or defect in an appropriate setting. Decomposing an ordinary fermion into two self-adjoint operators is always possible; that algebra alone establishes neither spatial separation nor topological protection. Here the ideal chain, experimental readout and claims about fault-tolerant computation are treated separately. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847)

Chiral two-dimensional pairing and one-dimensional superconducting chains provide distinct theoretical settings. Read and Green connect the weak-pairing spinless chiral state to non-Abelian quasiholes; its weak-pairing terminology is not a synonym for weak interaction strength. A proposed Hamiltonian or boundary solution does not establish the pairing state or topology of a measured solid. [R2](#ref-source-a33c639b7db4f05a)

## Mathematical assumptions

Fix the normalization $\{\gamma_i,\gamma_j\}=2\delta_{ij}$ and $\gamma_i^\dagger=\gamma_i$. Then $c=(\gamma_1+i\gamma_2)/2$, $n=c^\dagger c=(1+i\gamma_1\gamma_2)/2$ and the occupation parity is $P=(-1)^n=1-2n=-i\gamma_1\gamma_2$. Papers may normalize the operators or label parity signs differently. Mixing a factor $1/\sqrt2$ from another convention into these equations would spoil the fermionic anticommutator. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847) [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a)

For a uniform spinless chain, use hopping $t$, chemical potential $\mu$, real pairing $\Delta$, lattice spacing one and open ends. The bulk excitation spectrum satisfies $E(k)^2=(2t\cos k+\mu)^2+4\Delta^2\sin^2k$. The gapped topological domain is $|\mu|<2|t|$ with $\Delta\ne0$; $|\mu|=2|t|$ closes the gap. At $\mu=0$ and $t=\Delta>0$, the ideal finite chain has exactly unpaired endpoint operators. More general finite chains can have overlap splitting: exponential localization does not imply exactly zero energy at every length. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847)

Our bounded calculation checks the Majorana algebra, compares eight small-chain many-body spectra with independently constructed BdG spectra, verifies exact endpoint commutators at the special point, and follows decreasing overlap splitting for one sequence of increasing chain lengths. These are model checks. They do not fit a device, establish a universal prefactor or exclude oscillatory splitting at other parameters. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847)

The minimal two-site model makes a useful distinction explicit. With $\delta=(\mu_L+\mu_R)/2$ and $\epsilon=(\mu_L-\mu_R)/2$, its even and odd energies are $E_e^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\delta^2+\Delta^2}$ and $E_o^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\epsilon^2+t^2}$. At $t=\Delta$ and zero onsite energies the ground states coincide. Detuning one site leaves this ideal degeneracy intact, whereas common detuning gives a quadratic splitting and changing $t-\Delta$ gives a linear one. Direct four-state diagonalization checks these relations; they explain why a two-site sweet spot is not equivalent to generic long-chain protection. [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a)

## Experimental criteria

In the ideal grounded-superconductor tunneling setup analyzed by Law, Lee and Ng, a Majorana resonance can produce conductance $2e^2/h$. Interpreting a measured peak requires the actual coupling, resolution, temperature and competing states. Pan and Das Sarma model trivial low-energy peaks from mechanisms including confinement and disorder, and discuss limitations of end-to-end correlations in short wires. Their theoretical alternatives are reasons to test a signal, not a diagnosis of every later experiment. [R3](#ref-source-1b46269f3dd05cd6) [R4](#ref-source-dca781066e96eecc)

Aghaee and colleagues, published on 19 February 2025, report interferometric single-shot fermion-parity readout. Their selected results include millisecond-scale parity dwell times and approximately 1% assignment error at an optimized measurement time. The paper explicitly states that the measurements do not uniquely distinguish topological Majorana modes from suitably tuned low-energy Andreev states. It also constrains the alternatives through support at both wire ends and weak coupling to other low-energy states. Preserve both the achieved readout and that unresolved interpretation. [R5](#ref-source-e3824a8727c3ec54)

Van Loo and colleagues, published online on 11 February 2026, read out the parity of a minimal InSb–Al quantum-dot chain through quantum capacitance. The selected author text reports lifetimes exceeding a millisecond and contrasts the readout with a local charge sensor unable to distinguish parity at the sweet spot. The authors explicitly describe limited protection in this two-site device. The accepted-author version was uploaded on 6 October 2026; that upload is not the experiment's publication date. [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a)

Spectroscopy, parity lifetime, readout fidelity, robustness, fusion and exchange probe different properties. Report the measured observable and the alternatives addressed by that particular protocol. A parity readout result alone does not demonstrate a non-Abelian exchange operation or a fault-tolerant processor. There is no platform-independent checklist in which every local zero-bias feature automatically advances toward a universal confirmation threshold. [R4](#ref-source-dca781066e96eecc) [R5](#ref-source-e3824a8727c3ec54) [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a)

A 10 July 2026 preprint by Zatelli and colleagues reports coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains. The authors distinguish partial protection at the sweet spot from the unprotected degeneracy-lifting operations used for rotation. No journal acceptance was verified here; this is not a demonstrated braid or a certified gate fidelity. [R9](#ref-source-818818441532a8ec)

## Limits and disputes

The 2018 article “Quantized Majorana conductance” was retracted on 8 March 2021. The authors' notice describes undisclosed charge-jump corrections, a mislabeled axis and recalibration shifting plateau values above the claimed quantized conductance. The withdrawn positive claim is retained only as a historical record with its retraction notice. It cannot validate a device, and its retraction does not itself settle every other Majorana proposal. [R7](#ref-source-6a7f18eec743e89d) [R8](#ref-source-f127bb2d99183698)

This review checks selected original chain and readout passages, two-site energy equations, the author-institution retraction text and bounded calculations. The transport alternatives remain at original-abstract scope here; full device datasets, supplementary analyses, final-version comparisons and platform-by-platform fusion or braiding audits remain open. Complete scientific acceptance has not been reached. Neither commercial terminology nor a manuscript upload date closes those gaps. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847) [R4](#ref-source-dca781066e96eecc) [R5](#ref-source-e3824a8727c3ec54) [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a) [R8](#ref-source-f127bb2d99183698)

## Discovery implications

Keep the operator convention, physical geometry, bulk-gap assumptions and measurement protocol attached to each claim. Search for a reproducible combination of localization, controlled perturbations and protocol-specific evidence, while reporting failed or ambiguous tests. Separate a useful quantum-device component from a verified topological phase and from a demonstrated computational operation. This article does not make a worldwide priority claim or certify a material family from a single resonance. [R1](#ref-source-ade538b429fdd847) [R4](#ref-source-dca781066e96eecc) [R5](#ref-source-e3824a8727c3ec54) [R6](#ref-source-a3c2dc153700478a)

## Related topics

Continue with [topological superconductivity](/scwiki/topological-superconductivity), [time-reversal-invariant topology](/scwiki/time-reversal-invariant-topological-superconductivity), [Chern number](/scwiki/chern-number), [chiral pairing](/scwiki/chiral-pairing) and [Andreev reflection](/scwiki/andreev-reflection).

For a dated comparison of spectroscopy, control and exchange criteria, see [the Majorana identification question](/scwiki/open-questions/n4).

## Claim evidence and conditions

### scwiki-f5-claim-scope-1

A Majorana operator is self-adjoint. A Majorana zero mode additionally represents a zero-energy degree of freedom of a specified Hamiltonian, localized at an end, boundary or defect in an appropriate setting. Decomposing an ordinary fermion into two self-adjoint operators is always possible; that algebra alone establishes neither spatial separation nor topological protection. Here the ideal chain, experimental readout and claims about fault-tolerant computation are treated separately.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-ade538b429fdd847.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-scope-2

Chiral two-dimensional pairing and one-dimensional superconducting chains provide distinct theoretical settings. Read and Green connect the weak-pairing spinless chiral state to non-Abelian quasiholes; its weak-pairing terminology is not a synonym for weak interaction strength. A proposed Hamiltonian or boundary solution does not establish the pairing state or topology of a measured solid.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-a33c639b7db4f05a.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-1

Fix the normalization $\{\gamma_i,\gamma_j\}=2\delta_{ij}$ and $\gamma_i^\dagger=\gamma_i$. Then $c=(\gamma_1+i\gamma_2)/2$, $n=c^\dagger c=(1+i\gamma_1\gamma_2)/2$ and the occupation parity is $P=(-1)^n=1-2n=-i\gamma_1\gamma_2$. Papers may normalize the operators or label parity signs differently. Mixing a factor $1/\sqrt2$ from another convention into these equations would spoil the fermionic anticommutator.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-ade538b429fdd847, source-a3c2dc153700478a.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-2

For a uniform spinless chain, use hopping $t$, chemical potential $\mu$, real pairing $\Delta$, lattice spacing one and open ends. The bulk excitation spectrum satisfies $E(k)^2=(2t\cos k+\mu)^2+4\Delta^2\sin^2k$. The gapped topological domain is $|\mu|<2|t|$ with $\Delta\ne0$; $|\mu|=2|t|$ closes the gap. At $\mu=0$ and $t=\Delta>0$, the ideal finite chain has exactly unpaired endpoint operators. More general finite chains can have overlap splitting: exponential localization does not imply exactly zero energy at every length.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-ade538b429fdd847.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-3

Our bounded calculation checks the Majorana algebra, compares eight small-chain many-body spectra with independently constructed BdG spectra, verifies exact endpoint commutators at the special point, and follows decreasing overlap splitting for one sequence of increasing chain lengths. These are model checks. They do not fit a device, establish a universal prefactor or exclude oscillatory splitting at other parameters.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-ade538b429fdd847.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-mathematical-assumptions-4

The minimal two-site model makes a useful distinction explicit. With $\delta=(\mu_L+\mu_R)/2$ and $\epsilon=(\mu_L-\mu_R)/2$, its even and odd energies are $E_e^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\delta^2+\Delta^2}$ and $E_o^\pm=-\delta\pm\sqrt{\epsilon^2+t^2}$. At $t=\Delta$ and zero onsite energies the ground states coincide. Detuning one site leaves this ideal degeneracy intact, whereas common detuning gives a quadratic splitting and changing $t-\Delta$ gives a linear one. Direct four-state diagonalization checks these relations; they explain why a two-site sweet spot is not equivalent to generic long-chain protection.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-a3c2dc153700478a.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-experimental-criteria-1

In the ideal grounded-superconductor tunneling setup analyzed by Law, Lee and Ng, a Majorana resonance can produce conductance $2e^2/h$. Interpreting a measured peak requires the actual coupling, resolution, temperature and competing states. Pan and Das Sarma model trivial low-energy peaks from mechanisms including confinement and disorder, and discuss limitations of end-to-end correlations in short wires. Their theoretical alternatives are reasons to test a signal, not a diagnosis of every later experiment.

Evidence: theory. Sources: source-1b46269f3dd05cd6, source-dca781066e96eecc.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-experimental-criteria-2

Aghaee and colleagues, published on 19 February 2025, report interferometric single-shot fermion-parity readout. Their selected results include millisecond-scale parity dwell times and approximately 1% assignment error at an optimized measurement time. The paper explicitly states that the measurements do not uniquely distinguish topological Majorana modes from suitably tuned low-energy Andreev states. It also constrains the alternatives through support at both wire ends and weak coupling to other low-energy states. Preserve both the achieved readout and that unresolved interpretation.

Evidence: experimental. Sources: source-e3824a8727c3ec54.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-experimental-criteria-3

Van Loo and colleagues, published online on 11 February 2026, read out the parity of a minimal InSb–Al quantum-dot chain through quantum capacitance. The selected author text reports lifetimes exceeding a millisecond and contrasts the readout with a local charge sensor unable to distinguish parity at the sweet spot. The authors explicitly describe limited protection in this two-site device. The accepted-author version was uploaded on 6 October 2026; that upload is not the experiment's publication date.

Evidence: experimental. Sources: source-a3c2dc153700478a.

Conditions: Explicit Majorana normalization, model length and perturbations; device-specific parity readout, publication date and retraction status.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-experimental-criteria-4

Spectroscopy, parity lifetime, readout fidelity, robustness, fusion and exchange probe different properties. Report the measured observable and the alternatives addressed by that particular protocol. A parity readout result alone does not demonstrate a non-Abelian exchange operation or a fault-tolerant processor. There is no platform-independent checklist in which every local zero-bias feature automatically advances toward a universal confirmation threshold.

Verification scope: Selected primary passages and bounded Fock/BdG calculations; complete scientific acceptance open.

### scwiki-f5-claim-limits-and-disputes-1

The 2018 article “Quantized Majorana conductance” was retracted on 8 March 2021. The authors' notice describes undisclosed charge-jump corrections, a mislabeled axis and recalibration shifting plateau values above the claimed quantized conductance. The withdrawn positive claim is retained only as a historical record with its retraction notice. It cannot validate a device, and its retraction does not itself settle every other Majorana proposal.

This review checks selected original chain and readout passages, two-site energy equations, the author-institution retraction text and bounded calculations. The transport alternatives remain at original-abstract scope here; full device datasets, supplementary analyses, final-version comparisons and platform-by-platform fusion or braiding audits remain open. Keep the operator convention, physical geometry, bulk-gap assumptions and measurement protocol attached to each claim. Search for a reproducible combination of localization, controlled perturbations and protocol-specific evidence, while reporting failed or ambiguous tests. Separate a useful quantum-device component from a verified topological phase and from a demonstrated computational operation. This article does not make a worldwide priority claim or certify a material family from a single resonance.

A 10 July 2026 preprint by Zatelli and colleagues reports coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains. articles.body:
## Scope

Flat-band superconductivity involves two distinct questions: whether electrons develop a pairing amplitude, and whether the resulting state resists a spatial phase twist. A narrow dispersion can favor pairing while suppressing the usual velocity contribution to current. Neither a large density of states nor a large mean-field gap establishes a high measured transition temperature. [R1](#ref-source-fdf091e09e7f4a6f) [R2](#ref-source-b43340ce5c356e49)

This article focuses on the scale hierarchy and response calculation. The isolated-band reduction of Peotta and Törmä assumes a bandwidth small compared with the attraction, itself small compared with the separation to other bands, together with an appropriate uniform pairing field. Those are conditions for that reduction, not necessary conditions for every superconducting flat-band system. Huhtinen and colleagues also analyze situations where a touching dispersive band can help within their mean-field treatment. [R1](#ref-source-fdf091e09e7f4a6f) [R4](#ref-source-72f7ddb9f13bbd81)

## Mathematical assumptions

As an independent pairing illustration, take one state per spin per cell, half filling, a rectangular density of states $\rho(\xi)=1/W$ over $-W/2\lt\xi\lt W/2$, and an effective attraction $G>0$. Absorb the Hartree shift into the chemical potential. The zero-temperature reduced mean-field gap is $\Delta_0=W/[2\sinh(W/G)]$. Its linearized pairing onset obeys $1=(G/W)\int_0^{W/2}\tanh[\xi/(2k_BT_{\rm pair})]\,d\xi/\xi$. State counting and the projected interaction are fixed here; $G$ is not automatically a multiorbital lattice's bare onsite attraction. [R1](#ref-source-fdf091e09e7f4a6f) [R2](#ref-source-b43340ce5c356e49)

In this illustration, $W/G\to0$ gives $\Delta_0\to G/2$ and $k_BT_{\rm pair}\to G/4$. Seven bandwidth ratios were checked using an independent zero-temperature quadrature and numerical roots of the onset equation. The gap-to-pairing-scale ratio approaches two in the flat limit and approximately 1.764 in the broad-band weak-coupling regime. This density-of-states model specifies no Bloch eigenvectors, current operator or phase stiffness. Its pairing onset must not be relabelled an experimental $T_c$. [R1](#ref-source-fdf091e09e7f4a6f) [R2](#ref-source-b43340ce5c356e49)

For the multiband response, a conventional/geometric split is useful only with its precise definitions. An isolated flat band can have zero conventional contribution while its wavefunctions support a geometric contribution. The corrected response includes how the orbital pairing fields change under the applied twist. In the time-reversal-symmetric isolated-flat-band setting with uniform pairing, Huhtinen and colleagues connect the response to the minimal integrated quantum metric, rather than an arbitrary orbital representation's unrelaxed metric expression. [R1](#ref-source-fdf091e09e7f4a6f) [R3](#ref-source-fa7a165c8c344a63) [R4](#ref-source-72f7ddb9f13bbd81)

A separate scalar example shows why relaxation matters. Let a free-energy density be $f(Q,\eta)=D_0Q^2/2+bQ\eta+a\eta^2/2$, with $a>0$, an imposed phase gradient $Q$ and a relaxable internal coordinate $\eta$. Minimization gives $\eta_*=-bQ/a$ and $D_{\rm relaxed}=D_0-b^2/a$. A stable example with $D_0=a=b=1$ has positive frozen curvature but zero relaxed curvature. Four parameter sets and twelve coordinate changes $\eta'=\eta+cQ$ reproduce the same relaxed response while the frozen curvature can change. This illustrates a chain-rule correction, not a full superconducting lattice calculation. [R4](#ref-source-72f7ddb9f13bbd81)

Quantum-metric normalization also matters. In this Wiki, $g_{ij}=\operatorname{Re}\langle\partial_i u|(1-|u\rangle\langle u|)|\partial_j u\rangle$. ## Mathematical assumptions

As an independent pairing illustration, take one state per spin per cell, half filling, a rectangular density of states $\rho(\xi)=1/W$ over $-W/2\lt\xi\lt W/2$, and an effective attraction $G>0$.
